blind_text:
statement: Among a population of predictive models, selection favors the one with the lowest recent average surprisal (-log p(observation)), a survival-of-the-least-surprised rule where low scorers are culled and replaced by mutated copies of high scorers. This creates a competitive predictor market where a proper scoring rule directly determines persistence and propagation.
what exists: population of models {p_i}; observation stream o_t; running score S_i (moving average negative log-likelihood)
what changes: each model does local parameter updates between selection events; the population is periodically reweighted/culled by S_i
what persists: models with sustained low surprisal persist across resampling steps
what is selected: models with lowest cumulative negative log-likelihood on recent data
what can reproduce: high-scoring models are copied with mutation to replace low scorers
what can learn: individual models perform local learning (e.g., gradient) between selection events
what can transfer: a surviving model's parameters transfer to descendants and to environments with similar [X]
distinguishing observable: population-average surprisal decreases faster than any single model's isolated learning curve, and adapts faster to regime shifts, than a null twin with identical local learning but no selection/replacement (parallel independent learners)
minimal world: Data generated by two Markov chains that switch abruptly at random times; run 20 models with local learning plus selection-and-mutation (window 50), vs. a null twin with the same 20 models and learning rule but no culling; measure time-to-adapt after each regime switch.

statement: Synaptic weight between two units changes in proportion to the product of their activities, strengthening when both are co-active and weakening (via a decay or anti-correlation term) otherwise, with soft bounds preventing unbounded growth. This converts persistent statistical correlation between two signals into a persistent physical parameter (the weight).
what exists: pre-synaptic activity x; post-synaptic activity y; synaptic weight w with soft upper/lower bounds; learning rate eta
what changes: dw = eta * x * y - decay(w), applied every timestep, with the decay/bound term preventing runaway growth
what persists: the accumulated weight value, which encodes the history of joint activity between the two units
what is selected: synapses whose endpoints show sustained co-activity are selected for strengthening over synapses with uncorrelated or anti-correlated endpoints
what can reproduce: the resulting weight value can be copied to initialize a naive synapse exposed to the same input [X], reproducing similar steady-state weight
what can learn: the network learns the pairwise correlational structure of its input stream
what can transfer: the learned weight generalizes to samples drawn from the same joint distribution of x and y
distinguishing observable: weight trajectory should track the running covariance of x and y (rising/falling smoothly with correlation strength) rather than following a fixed schedule or random walk
minimal world: a two-neuron toy world driven by two input streams with a tunable correlation coefficient; intervention: abruptly change the correlation coefficient mid-run and observe weight re-equilibration; null twin: a synapse updated by random increments matched in mean and variance to the [X] updates but statistically independent of the actual x*y product.

blind_text:
statement: A buffer stores compressed state-transition sequences from online experience; during offline periods with no external input, sequences are resampled from the buffer (biased toward high prediction-error or high-reward items) and replayed through the network, driving further plasticity on general-purpose (slow) weights. This actively reshapes weights using reinstated activity patterns rather than merely preserving them.
what exists: replay buffer of (state, action, next-state, error/reward) tuples; fast/episode-specific weights; slow/general weights; sampling priority score per buffer item
what changes: offline, sampled sequences drive reactivation of stored activity patterns, and slow weights update via [X] plasticity on this reactivated activity, weighted by sampling priority
what persists: slow weights persist across sessions; buffer items persist until sufficiently replayed, then decay
what is selected: sequences with higher priority (prediction error or reward magnitude, recency) are preferentially selected for replay
what can reproduce: not applicable to individual traces; replay-priority parameters can be varied and selected across agent populations by task performance
what can learn: the network improves sample efficiency, generalizing predictive/value structure from limited online experience via offline rehearsal
what can transfer: weight changes consolidated via replay generalize learned associations to test contexts sharing structure with replayed sequences
distinguishing observable: measure test performance after an offline period with no stimuli: the mechanism predicts improvement ("overnight" gains) driven purely by internally generated replay, whereas a model with an identical buffer but no offline replay-driven weight update shows no change in performance across the same offline interval.
minimal world: An agent explores a small graph-structured environment collecting reward, storing transitions in a buffer. After a fixed period of online exploration, both models undergo an offline phase with zero external input; the mechanism model replays buffered sequences and updates weights, the null twin holds weights fixed (or replays purely randomly with no priority) during the same offline window. Test-phase value-estimation accuracy after the offline period is the diagnostic, controlling for total online experience between conditions.

blind_text:
statement: Two pressures act simultaneously on the same tensor-shaped distribution: an entropy-maximizing pressure pulling toward the least-biased solution given marginal constraints, and a rank-compressing pressure pulling the parameter or moment tensor toward low multilinear rank. Because these pressures generally have different fixed points, their joint action produces a specific bias in unconstrained interactions absent under either pressure alone.
what exists: An order-k moment/constraint tensor, an exponential-family candidate distribution, and an explicit rank penalty on the natural-parameter or moment tensor.
what changes: The objective L = -H[p] + β(constraint violation) + γ(rank penalty) is optimized by alternating gradient/dual-ascent steps as γ is scanned.
what persists: The constraint set persists throughout; only the achieved rank/entropy operating point moves as γ varies.
what is selected: Configurations lying on the Pareto frontier of (constraint error, effective rank) are retained as γ is annealed.
what can reproduce: Pareto-optimal solutions at one γ seed initialization for the next γ along a homotopy path.
what can learn: The system learns the entire entropy-rank tradeoff curve for a given constraint set, not just a single solution.
what can transfer: The curvature/inflection location of the entropy-rank frontier is a property of the interaction graph and can be compared across different variable systems.
distinguishing observable: Entropy(R) at convergence shows a strictly concave curve with an interior knee under the combined pressures; pure MaxEnt (no rank pressure) shows a flat curve at full-rank entropy, and pure rank compression (no entropy pressure) shows collapse to low-entropy solutions irrespective of R — neither alone produces a knee.
minimal world: Four binary variables with empirical pairwise plus one triple-wise marginal constraint (16-cell tensor). Intervention: sweep γ from 0 to large while constraint-violation pressure stays active, recording entropy and effective [X]-rank at convergence. Null twin: apply the identical rank penalty to a randomly shuffled tensor of matched shape and Frobenius norm but no real interaction structure; its entropy(R) curve should be flat/uninformative, lacking the knee seen in the real world.

blind_text:
statement: A latent mapping is trained on unlabeled temporal sequences to favor components that change slowly over time while remaining informative and mutually decorrelated. This slowness prior causes latent dimensions to align with persistent underlying causes of the data rather than fast nuisance fluctuations. The resulting factorized code separates causal structure from noise without supervision.
what exists: observation sequence x_t; latent mapping f; latent variables z_t = f(x_t)
what changes: f is updated to minimize squared temporal derivatives of z components subject to a variance/decorrelation constraint (slow feature objective).
what persists: The learned mapping f and the ranking of latent dimensions by temporal smoothness persist across similar-[X] domains.
what is selected: Latent dimensions corresponding to slowly changing generative causes are favored over fast-varying nuisance dimensions.
what can reproduce: The sorted slow-feature basis can be transplanted into other agents facing similar sequence [X].
what can learn: f is learned purely self-supervised from temporal sequences.
what can transfer: Slow latents trained on one sequence domain support fast downstream learning in a related domain sharing the same slow causal factors.
distinguishing observable: The slowest latent dimensions align with ground-truth task-relevant factors (measured via linear probe accuracy) far better than the fastest dimensions or a randomly chosen subset.
minimal world: Rendered sequences of a rotating/translating object with independent fast pixel noise; train f with a slowness objective versus a reconstruction-only objective. Null twin: an [X] of matched architecture/capacity trained only to reconstruct x_t from z_t with no temporal term, whose latent ranking shows no correlation with slow task-relevant factors.

blind_text:
statement: A system continuously updates its internal parameters to reduce the mismatch between predicted and actual sensory input, with the update direction set by the local gradient of squared prediction error. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The population-of-β selection framing is an optional add-on. The claimed guarantee of perfect nuisance invariance under distribution shift is stronger than VIB provides in general. It holds only when nuisance is statistically independent of Y and the variational bound is tight.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant/disentangled representation learning via minimal sufficient statistics (Achille & Soatto 2018, 'Emergence of invariance and disentanglement'; information dropout)
nearest_priors.explains: The link between minimality (low I(Z;X)) and invariance to nuisances. Explains why the bottleneck discards nuisance and yields near-zero ∂Z/∂nuisance and transfer to shifted nuisance distributions
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific encoder-decoder training protocol is the same as VIB rather than distinct. It does not add the population/β selection aspect.

nearest_priors.name: Rate-distortion theory / β-VAE-style KL-regularised latent capacity control; minimum description length
nearest_priors.explains: The capacity parameter β trading rate I(Z;X) against a distortion term, KL regularisation with injectable noise, and β annealing
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Here distortion is supervised prediction of Y rather than reconstruction of X, so these frameworks do not by themselves select task-relevant over nuisance dimensions.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing. The only extra is the optional suggestion of embedding networks with varying β in a population for selection studies, which is a trivial hyperparameter-sweep or evolutionary wrapper. The invariance-under-shift claim is a known consequence (and known limitation) of the IB.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Make the nuisance spuriously correlated with Y in training and decorrelated at test. Standard VIB will retain the spurious nuisance because it is predictive of Y, so it degrades under shift. A mechanism that truly identified 'causal' task signal would not degrade. Also run a matched-capacity control with only dropout or weight decay: if robustness matches VIB, the effect is generic regularisation rather than an information bottleneck.

blind_text:
statement: Information is stored as codewords of a linear [X]; retrieval computes a syndrome from a possibly corrupted readout and looks up the most likely error pattern to correct it, so recall is exactly robust to any error pattern up to half the code's minimum distance. Robustness is a discrete guaranteed threshold property, not a graded statistical one.
what exists: message vectors m; generator matrix G; codeword c = mG; parity-check matrix H with [X]^T=0; noisy readout c' = c + e; syndrome s = Hc'^T
what changes: decoding maps syndrome s to an estimated error e_hat via a fixed lookup table, then corrects c_hat = c' - e_hat
what persists: the encoded message identity persists exactly through decoding as long as weight(e) <= floor((d_min-1)/2)
what is selected: code parameters (G,H, hence minimum distance) are selected/evolved to match the noise level of the environment
what can reproduce: the same original message is reproduced from many independently corrupted readouts of the same codeword
what can learn: the code itself (choice of G,H, or an adaptive decoder) can be tuned/learned from observed error [X] to maximize successful decode rate
what can transfer: the same decoding procedure transfers unchanged to any message encoded with the same code
distinguishing observable: recall accuracy as a function of the number of corrupted bits shows a sharp threshold (perfect recall below d_min/2, then abrupt failure) versus an uncoded direct-storage baseline with the same total redundancy budget, which shows smooth graceful degradation instead of a threshold
minimal world: World: 4-bit messages encoded with a (7,4) [X] code, corrupted by flipping a controlled number of bits at random. Intervention: sweep number of flipped bits from 0 to 3 and measure exact-recall rate via syndrome decoding. Null twin: same total number of bits (7) storing the message with simple triple-repetition-and-majority-vote instead of the [X] code, matched on redundancy ratio; it degrades gradually rather than showing the same sharp minimum-distance threshold.

nearest_priors.name: Hamming (7,4) code with syndrome (coset-leader / standard-array) decoding
nearest_priors.explains: Linear block code storage (c = mG), parity-check matrix with GH^T = 0, syndrome s = Hc'^T, and lookup of the most likely error pattern (the coset leader). It also explains the guaranteed correction of up to floor((d_min-1)/2) errors (1 bit for d = 3), exact recall at 0-1 flips, and certain miscorrection at 2 or more flips because the code is perfect. The same decoder works for every message, and repeated corrupted readouts decode to the same message.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not provide evolutionary or learned selection of G and H to match environmental noise. It also does not support the claim that a repetition baseline degrades 'gracefully': repetition codes are linear codes with the same kind of hard threshold.

nearest_priors.name: Adaptive / learned channel coding (code design matched to channel statistics, e.g. rate adaptation, neural or belief-propagation decoders trained on error statistics)
nearest_priors.explains: The 'what is selected' and 'what can learn' clauses: choosing the code rate or minimum distance for the noise level, and tuning the decoder from observed error patterns.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It adds nothing to the core syndrome-decoding mechanism, which is fixed-table and non-adaptive in the minimal world.

nearest_priors.name: Repetition code with majority vote / attractor-based associative memory (Hopfield) as graded-robustness contrast
nearest_priors.explains: Serves as the null-twin baseline. It covers redundancy-based error correction and the intended contrast between a hard threshold and graded degradation of recall.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Triple repetition of 4 bits needs 12 bits, not 7, so the matched null twin as specified is infeasible. Repetition decoding also has a per-block hard threshold, so the predicted smooth-versus-sharp contrast is not a mechanism difference.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing mechanistic. The only non-textbook element is the framing of code parameters as selected or evolved to match environmental noise, which is standard adaptive coding. The null-twin specification is internally inconsistent: 3x repetition of a 4-bit message cannot fit in 7 bits, and repetition coding is itself a threshold code. The 'distinguishing observable' therefore rests on a flawed baseline, but the core mechanism is runnable.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Sweep the number of flipped bits (0-3) for a Hamming (7,4) code and for a repetition code of equal length and rate, e.g. (3,1) applied per bit with the extra bits accounted for. Measure exact-recall rate per codeword. If both show threshold behaviour at floor((d_min-1)/2) set by their respective minimum distances, the mechanism is plain minimum-distance decoding with no novel ingredient. Separately, vary channel noise and check whether the 'selection/learning' step actually changes G and H toward the rate-distortion or capacity-appropriate code; this is standard adaptive coding.

blind_text:
statement: A population of candidate decomposition formats ([X], Tucker, [X]) at various ranks competes to fit the same fixed low-order marginal constraints, with fitness defined as achieved entropy per parameter used. Only formats whose implicit factorization pattern matches the hidden interaction [X] of the data survive under this parameter-normalized fitness.
what exists: Several candidate model classes over the same k discrete variables, a shared fixed target marginal constraint set, and a fitness score per candidate.
what changes: Each candidate is independently fit via its own MaxEnt-under-decomposition solver; fitness (entropy/parameter-count subject to violation tolerance) is then compared.
what persists: The target constraint set is fixed across all candidates; format identities persist within a round.
what is selected: The format/rank combination with highest entropy-per-parameter is selected; low-fitness candidates are eliminated.
what can reproduce: The winning format/rank spawns variant offspring at neighboring ranks for a subsequent selection round.
what can learn: Across rounds, the population converges toward the format most efficiently capturing the true interaction graph.
what can transfer: A winning format discovered on one variable set transfers as a structural hypothesis to a related, larger variable set.
distinguishing observable: The winning format's sparsity pattern matches the true generative interaction graph, whereas selecting by raw (non-normalized) entropy would always favor the highest-rank/most-flexible format regardless of true structure.
minimal world: Six binary variables generated by a Markov chain (favoring [X]). Intervention: tournament of [X]/Tucker/[X] candidates fit to shared pairwise marginals, recording entropy-per-parameter and tracking the winner across rank-mutation generations. Null twin: matched-size, matched-marginal-magnitude data drawn from a dense/generic interaction structure — [X] should no longer dominate the identical tournament.

nearest_priors.name: Tensor-network structure search by genetic/evolutionary algorithm (e.g., TNGA, Li & Sun 2020; TN-SS / rank search), which is also the tensor-train vs CP vs Tucker format selection problem
nearest_priors.field: Machine learning / tensor methods / numerical multilinear algebra
nearest_priors.explains: A population of candidate decomposition formats and ranks; each candidate fit independently; fitness that trades fit against parameter count; mutation to neighbouring ranks across generations; convergence toward the topology matching the data's correlation structure (a TT/MPS wins on Markov-chain data); reuse of the discovered structure on larger problems.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific fit objective, which is MaxEnt under fixed low-order marginal constraints rather than reconstruction error. The specific ratio fitness, entropy per parameter, rather than an additive penalty.

nearest_priors.name: Penalized model selection (MDL/BIC/AIC) over structured maximum-entropy / graphical models, including Chow-Liu and junction-tree structure learning
nearest_priors.explains: Why complexity normalization is needed: unpenalized likelihood or entropy criteria always prefer the most flexible model. Recovery of the true sparse interaction graph (a chain) from pairwise marginals. The null twin, where dense generative structure removes the advantage of the sparse format.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The population/tournament dynamics, rank mutation, and offspring generations. The use of tensor decomposition formats as the model classes.

nearest_priors.name: Maximum-entropy fitting of pairwise marginals with MPS/tensor-train ansatz (Born machines, DMRG-style MaxEnt, iterative proportional fitting within a low-rank family)
nearest_priors.explains: The per-candidate solver, MaxEnt constrained to a decomposition format. The fact that MPS/TT factorizations match 1D Markov-chain correlations with small bond dimension (area-law / chain-structure argument).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The cross-format competition, selection, reproduction and transfer.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the idiosyncratic choice of entropy-per-parameter as a ratio fitness rather than a standard additive MDL/BIC penalty. Achieved entropy under a format constraint is bounded by the unconstrained MaxEnt value. So the ratio mostly rewards small parameter counts, subject to the violation tolerance. That is a nonstandard, somewhat ad hoc criterion, but not a new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the same tournament with fitness replaced by standard BIC/MDL (log-likelihood of held-out data minus a (p/2)·log n penalty) and by reconstruction-error-plus-parameter penalty as in TNGA. If the same format/rank winners and generational trajectories appear on both the Markov-chain and dense-structure data, the mechanism reduces to penalized evolutionary structure search. It would count as distinct only if entropy-per-parameter selects differently and recovers the true graph more reliably. A further test is to vary tolerance and sample size, checking whether the ratio fitness degenerates to always choosing minimal rank.

statement: The gap between the abstract, unexecuted worst-case sensitivity bound and the empirically observed local sensitivity from executed trials acts as a driving force that reallocates exploration effort toward regions where this gap is largest. The law updates an exploration-rate field proportional to gap magnitude, coupling a never-executed static computation to an online sampling dynamic. This coupling has no counterpart when either quantity is used alone.
what exists: a spatial partition of the input domain into cells; per-cell abstract worst-case bound (from [X]); per-cell empirical sensitivity estimate (from executed trials); a per-cell exploration-rate variable
what changes: each step, the exploration rate of a cell is updated proportionally to the absolute gap between its abstract bound and its current empirical estimate; sampling effort in the next step is drawn proportionally to exploration rate
what persists: the abstract bounds persist as fixed ceilings unless the domain is refined; only empirical estimates and exploration rates evolve
what is selected: cells with persistently large gaps continue to attract sampling effort, while cells whose empirical estimate converges to its abstract bound see exploration rate decay
what can reproduce: N/A; this is a single-agent allocation dynamic
what can learn: the spatial map of gaps becomes an implicit map of where the program's true behavior is furthest from its worst-case abstraction, informative about local structure (e.g., true nonlinearity concentration)
what can transfer: the converged gap map transfers as an informative prior exploration policy for structurally similar programs
distinguishing observable: sampling effort over time concentrates in regions of high true curvature even though curvature was never directly measured, a pattern that a naive uniform or purely empirical-variance-driven exploration rule (matched in total sample budget) fails to reproduce because it lacks access to the abstract ceiling
minimal world: A 2D input domain with one region of hidden sharp nonlinearity and the rest smooth, discretized into 16 cells; intervention: relocate the nonlinear region between runs and check whether the exploration-rate field relocates accordingly; null twin: an exploration rule driven purely by empirical estimate variance (no abstract bound), matched in total samples, which reallocates more slowly and less precisely because it has no static ceiling to compare against.

statement: A population of coding units competes via lateral inhibition so that only a sparse subset is active for any input, and only active units update their receptive fields toward the current input (winner-take-most [X]). This yields an overcomplete but sparse dictionary of reusable features rather than a fully distributed code.
what exists: input vector x; unit weights w_i; activations a_i; lateral inhibitory connections
what changes: activations settle via competitive/inhibitory dynamics to a sparse pattern; weights of only the winning units update: w_i += lr*a_i*(x - w_i)
what persists: receptive fields tuned to frequently recurring input features persist and refine over time
what is selected: units whose current weights best match frequent input patterns win the competition repeatedly and get sharpened; rarely-winning units remain unspecialized or get reset
what can reproduce: optionally, an overused/high-variance unit can be duplicated/split into two specialized units
what can learn: a sparse dictionary of basis features spanning the input distribution
what can transfer: the learned [X] transfers to compress and reconstruct inputs sharing the same underlying feature [X]
distinguishing observable: reconstruction accuracy and code sparsity (kurtosis) under combinations of familiar features, compared to a fully distributed dense code of equal total weight norm and unit count without inhibition
minimal world: A world of small bar/patch stimuli combined additively; network learns a [X] via lateral inhibition. Intervention: present overlapping combinations at test time. Null twin: identical unit count and weight-update rule but without lateral inhibition, so all units update on every input (dense distributed code), matched total activation energy — measure interference/catastrophic overlap versus the sparse model.

blind_text:
statement: Feature weights are trained to minimize prediction loss subject to a penalty on the variance of predictive performance across multiple observed environments/interventions, forcing reliance on features whose relation to the target is invariant rather than merely correlated within any single environment. This selects causal features over environment-specific spurious correlates.
what exists: features from multiple environments e in E; target Y; predictor with weights w
what changes: w updated to minimize sum_e loss_e(w) + lambda*Var_e(loss_e(w)) (invariance penalty, [X]-like)
what persists: weight on genuinely causal features remains nonzero and stable across environments as training proceeds
what is selected: feature subsets whose predictive relationship with Y is stable across interventions are favored; environment-specific correlates are down-weighted
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: a distinction between causal and spurious predictors of Y from multi-environment data
what can transfer: invariant features transfer prediction accuracy to unseen environments; spurious features fail to transfer
distinguishing observable: held-out accuracy on a environment where the spurious correlation's sign is flipped: invariance-constrained model maintains accuracy while an empirical-risk-minimizing model of matched capacity and matched training accuracy degrades sharply
minimal world: Synthetic data where Y = f(causal feature C) + noise, and spurious feature S correlates with Y only via an environment-specific confound whose sign flips across environments. Intervention: test on a environment with the confound sign reversed. Null twin: standard [X] training without the invariance penalty, matched training-environment accuracy and model capacity — expected to rely on S and fail on the flipped test environment.

nearest_priors.name: Variance Risk Extrapolation (V-REx; Krueger et al. 2021, 'Out-of-Distribution Generalization via Risk Extrapolation')
nearest_priors.explains: Exact objective: sum of per-environment risks plus lambda times the variance of those risks. It explains the preference for features whose predictive relationship is stable across environments, the down-weighting of spurious correlates, and transfer to unseen or shifted environments. It also matches the evaluation: synthetic data with a spurious feature whose correlation flips at test time (Colored-MNIST-style), compared against ERM.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. The description's claim that it 'selects causal features' is stronger than V-REx's guarantee. Equalizing risks guarantees causal identification only under assumptions: enough diverse environments and interventions that do not touch Y's own mechanism.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant Risk Minimization (IRM; Arjovsky, Bottou, Gulrajani, Lopez-Paz 2019)
nearest_priors.explains: Multi-environment training with an invariance penalty added to ERM, the goal of isolating causal predictors from spurious ones, the flipped-correlation test environment, and the ERM null baseline with matched training accuracy.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Its penalty is the gradient norm of each environment's risk with respect to a dummy classifier scale, i.e. that the classifier be simultaneously optimal per environment. It is not the variance of losses across environments, so the described update rule differs.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant Causal Prediction (ICP; Peters, Bühlmann, Meinshausen 2016)
nearest_priors.explains: The principle that causal predictor sets have a conditional distribution of Y that is invariant across interventional environments. It also covers selecting feature subsets on that basis and the account of why invariant features transfer.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It uses hypothesis tests over subsets, giving confidence sets for causal parents, rather than gradient training of weights with a variance penalty. It also does not use penalized risk minimization.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing substantive; [X] is ERM (empirical risk minimization). The only gap is that the description overclaims: a variance-of-risk penalty guarantees causal selection only under V-REx's stated identifiability conditions. It can also trade off against covariate-shift robustness, and the description does not acknowledge either point.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Train V-REx and IRM on identical multi-environment data in two regimes. In the first, environments differ only in the spurious-correlation sign. In the second, they also differ in the noise level on Y given the causal feature (heteroskedastic label noise across environments). Variance-of-risk penalization is pushed away from the causal feature when irreducible noise differs by environment, because causal-feature risks are then unequal. IRM's per-environment optimality condition is not affected in this way. Record the weight on C and flipped-environment accuracy. If the described mechanism degrades in the second regime while IRM does not, it is the risk-variance (V-REx) mechanism, not a gradient-invariance one.

blind_text:
statement: The agent's internal belief about a causal effect is stored not as a point estimate or a probability distribution but as a sound abstract-domain object (an interval or zonotope) obtained by propagating a family of candidate causal models through [X]. Downstream decisions act directly on this object's bounds rather than on any single sampled value. This representation makes the soundness guarantee itself a first-class, storable, composable quantity.
what exists: a family of candidate causal models consistent with observed data; an abstract domain object summarizing the family's joint output range; a decision rule that consumes the object's lower/upper bounds
what changes: as data arrives, the candidate model family shrinks, and the abstract object is recomputed by re-propagating the smaller family through the same transfer functions
what persists: the soundness invariant that the true causal effect always lies within the stored object's bounds persists across all updates
what is selected: decision rules that act conservatively on the bound (e.g., worst-case bound) are favored when the object is wide; more aggressive rules are enabled only as the object narrows
what can reproduce: the representation format (not its contents) can be copied to instantiate belief objects for causal questions
what can learn: the object's width over time tracks reducible uncertainty, providing a learning-progress signal distinct from prediction error
what can transfer: a narrow abstract object learned for one causal query can be composed with objects from other queries to bound a joint downstream query without re-deriving from raw data
distinguishing observable: decisions made from the abstract-object representation remain valid (never violate the true bound) under adversarial resampling of the data, whereas decisions made from a point-estimate-with-confidence-interval representation constructed from the same data can be violated when the underlying model is misspecified in ways the confidence interval does not capture
minimal world: A causal query with a small family of structurally different candidate models (e.g., linear vs. saturating) all fitting the same finite dataset equally well; intervention: reveal which candidate model is true and check whether the stored bound contained it; null twin: a point-estimate-plus-confidence-interval representation fit by standard regression on the same data, matched in sample size, which can exclude the true model when misspecification is present.

statement: An agent maintains both general principles and a set of particular case-judgments; when a principle conflicts with a firmly held judgment on a specific case, the agent adjusts whichever component (principle or judgment) carries lower confidence, iterating local bidirectional revision until reaching a stable, mutually coherent fixed point. what changes: On each detected conflict between a principle and a judgment, the lower-confidence side is revised (a principle's scope/weight adjusted, or a judgment overturned); confidences update based on how often each side survives revision.
what persists: Whichever (P,J) configuration reaches a local coherence fixed point persists until a conflicting case arrives.
what is selected: Components (rules or verdicts) that repeatedly survive conflict resolution accrue higher confidence and become harder to revise.
what can reproduce: Stabilized (P,J) pairs can be copied to agents as initial priors.
what can learn: The confidence-update rule and the resulting equilibrium are themselves learned outcomes of repeated exposure to cases.
what can transfer: Converged principles can generalize to held-out cases never previously encountered.
distinguishing observable: Feed a sequence including deliberately anomalous cases inconsistent with the initial rule but consistent with high-confidence exemplars; measure whether the rule itself bends (revision events) and track generalization accuracy on held-out cases, contrasting with rule-only (never updates from cases) and case-only nearest-neighbor (no rule) nulls matched for training accuracy.

Track whether the rule is revised to accommodate high-confidence exemplars (reflective equilibrium) versus null twins (fixed-rule-only, or exemplar-only) matched on training accuracy but differing in generalization and revision-event signatures on held-out anomalies.

statement: The [X] gain is switched among several candidate gain matrices indexed by which specific [X] relation currently fails (e.g., a scale-relation failure routes to a gain tuned to trust the dynamics model more; an order-relation failure routes to a gain tuned to trust observations more). what is selected: the currently best-fitting model/controller pair, chosen by minimal accumulated residual score
what can reproduce: the candidate model bank could in principle be regenerated or extended by resampling theta_i values, though the core mechanism is selection, not generation

what can transfer: the model bank transfers to any plant known to switch among the same finite set of regimes

blind_text:
statement: Individuals carry a genetically fixed trait bias and a plastic component that adjusts phenotype toward an optimum within a lifetime at a fitness cost proportional to learning effort. Mutations shifting more of the adaptive value into the fixed genetic component are favored by selection when the environment's optimum is stable across generations, producing genetic assimilation of a previously learned trait.
what exists: population of individuals with genotype g; lifetime learning process moving phenotype p from g toward optimum p*; learning cost proportional to effort; fitness = performance(p_final) - cost
what changes: Mutation perturbs g each generation; individuals reproduce proportional to fitness; offspring inherit g plus mutation.
what persists: Population-level allele frequencies for g, inherited and accumulated across generations.
what is selected: Individuals whose g is closer to p* (requiring less costly learning) are favored for reproduction, especially under a stable p* across generations.
what can reproduce: Individuals reproduce with probability proportional to fitness; offspring inherit mutated genotypes.
what can learn: Within a lifetime, each individual still adjusts phenotype from g toward p* via the plastic mechanism.
what can transfer: A genetic bias discovered via learning is effectively transferred into a heritable substrate across generations, obviating relearning.
distinguishing observable: Track mean(g) across generations under a stable p* versus a p* redrawn randomly each generation: assimilation predicts convergence of mean(g) toward p* only under stability, while a model with zero learning cost predicts no directional drift of g under either condition.
minimal world: A population where each agent must reach target value p* for fitness, with genotype g and lifetime learning steps moving phenotype toward p* at cost c per step used. Intervention: compare stable p* across generations vs. p* redrawn randomly each generation. Null twin: identical setup with learning cost c=0 (free plasticity), under which mean(g) shows no drift toward p* even in the stable condition.

what can learn: not direct learning but evolvability: increased capacity to acquire subfunctions across generations

Intervention: introduce a subtask requiring a combination of existing primitives. Null twin: mutation operator limited to point mutations at matched overall mutation-rate budget — measure time-to-innovation and module-reuse rate difference on the subtask.

blind_text:
statement: Given a set of candidate hypotheses that fit observed data equally well (or within tolerance), select the hypothesis maximizing an explanatory-virtue score combining simplicity (low description length), scope (unification across independent explananda), and coherence with accepted background theory, rather than selecting by likelihood or simplicity alone.
what exists: dataset D; hypothesis set H={h1..hn}; likelihood L(D|h) per hypothesis; virtue features: complexity K(h), unification U(h), coherence C(h) with background theory
what changes: On data, recompute L for each h; recompute virtue score V(h) = w1*L + w2*(-K) + w3*U + w4*C; select argmax V as the accepted theory.
what persists: The weighting (w1..w4) is a stable, potentially agent-specific trait of the reasoner.
what is selected: The winning hypothesis is retained as the accepted theory guiding prediction/action until outscored by a hypothesis.
what can reproduce: Successful weightings (w1..w4) can be copied across agent populations for evolutionary tuning of explanatory taste.
what can learn: The weights can be learned via reinforcement from the downstream predictive success of the selected theory.
what can transfer: A weighting tuned in one domain can be applied to a domain's data to test whether it still selects the true generating hypothesis.
distinguishing observable: In scenarios where multiple hypotheses tie on training likelihood but diverge on held-out predictions, compare virtue-guided selection against a pure max-likelihood/random-tiebreak selector; the diagnostic region is exactly the tied-likelihood regime, and ablating individual virtue terms should isolate which one carries genuine predictive information.
minimal world: A synthetic curve-fitting world with multiple polynomial/rule hypotheses tied on training points but diverging on held-out points. Agent A selects via virtue-weighted score; null agent B selects uniformly at random among tied hypotheses (or always the highest-order fit). Measure held-out accuracy specifically in the tied-likelihood regime, and ablate each virtue term to test whether it individually carries out-of-sample predictive value.

This produces representations whose content is explicitly shaped by task-relevance rather than raw input fidelity.
what exists: input X (task-relevant bits + nuisance bits); stochastic latent Z with injected noise sigma; target Y; trade-off parameter beta
what changes: encoder/decoder weights updated by gradient descent on beta*I(Z;X) - I(Z;Y) (or its variational bound); sigma or beta scheduled over training
what persists: the minimal sufficient [X] structure encoded in Z once converged
what is selected: latent dimensions/directions that reduce reconstruction of Y-irrelevant variance while preserving Y-relevant variance
what can reproduce: not applicable directly
what can learn: which input features are sufficient [X] for Y
what can transfer: Z reused with a freshly trained lightweight decoder for a but related target Y' with little retraining
distinguishing observable: sweeping beta should show monotonically decreasing decodability of nuisance bits from Z while task-relevant bit decodability stays high until a sharp knee; an unconstrained encoder retains nuisance bits decodable well above chance regardless of beta
minimal world: synthetic dataset X = (relevant_bit, nuisance_bits) + noise, Y = relevant_bit; intervention: sweep beta and probe Z with linear decoders for relevant vs nuisance bits; null twin: identical architecture with beta fixed at 0 (no compression term), achieving equal task accuracy but leaving nuisance bits fully decodable from Z.

nearest_priors.name: Information Bottleneck (Tishby, Pereira & Bialek 1999) / Deep Variational Information Bottleneck (Alemi et al. 2017)
nearest_priors.explains: Nearly everything. It covers the stochastic encoder X->Z with injected noise and the Lagrangian beta*I(Z;X) - I(Z;Y) optimised through a variational bound by gradient descent. It explains why only the predictive (approximately minimal sufficient) statistics of X survive as beta grows and nuisance variation is discarded. It predicts the phase-transition knee in I(Z;Y) as beta is swept, and why beta=0 yields no pressure to discard nuisance information.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The explicit transfer claim, that Z can be reused with a lightweight probe for a related target Y'. The basic IB literature does not guarantee this, and it holds only when Y' depends on the same retained statistics. It also does not fix a specific annealing schedule for sigma or beta.

nearest_priors.name: Minimal sufficient statistics / nuisance-invariant representations (Achille & Soatto, 'Emergence of Invariance and Disentanglement', 2018)
nearest_priors.explains: It identifies [X] as 'statistics', meaning sufficient statistics for Y. It explains that minimal sufficiency implies invariance to nuisances. It connects noise injection (information dropout) to discarding nuisance bits, and motivates probing Z for nuisance decodability.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific beta-sweep training procedure, and the claim that an unconstrained encoder necessarily keeps nuisance bits decodable. Implicit SGD compression can partially remove them even at beta=0.

nearest_priors.name: Rate-distortion theory with a task-defined distortion (and beta-VAE-style rate penalties)
nearest_priors.explains: It explains the rate-versus-relevance trade-off curve, the monotone loss of information as the rate penalty rises, and the knee in the curve. It also covers noise-scheduled latent channels.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Its standard form uses input-reconstruction distortion (beta-VAE) rather than relevance to a separate target Y, so on its own it would not selectively keep Y-relevant bits over nuisance bits.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The transfer claim and the prediction that the beta=0 null twin leaves nuisance bits 'fully' decodable go slightly beyond what IB theory guarantees. The second is an empirical claim that is contested in the IB / SGD-compression debate, not a new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the minimal world with a VIB of identical architecture and compare the linear-probe decodability curves for relevant and nuisance bits, plus the location of the knee in beta. If the curves match up to reparameterisation of beta or sigma, the description is VIB. Any systematic deviation, such as nuisance decodability being non-monotone in beta, or relevant-bit loss occurring before nuisance loss, would indicate a different mechanism.

statement: When two dynamical subsystems are connected in a feedback loop, the interconnection is guaranteed stable if the product of their individual input-output gains is less than one, regardless of the internal complexity of either subsystem. This small-gain theorem gives a structural, model-free sufficient constraint for safely composing modules without knowing their exact internal dynamics, acting as a portable certificate rather than a case-specific tuning.

what changes: signals propagate around the loop; boundedness of loop signals depends only on whether gamma1*gamma2 is below or above 1
what persists: the gain bound of each module persists as a portable certificate independent of the module's internal structure
what is selected: only interconnections satisfying gamma1*gamma2 < 1 are stable and survive; others diverge and are excluded from viable compositions
what can reproduce: any subsystem satisfying the gain bound can be substituted into the loop while preserving the stability guarantee
what can learn: the effective gain of a module can be estimated online to check composability before connecting
what can transfer: a gain certificate for a module transfers across different partner modules and contexts
distinguishing observable: sweeping gamma1*gamma2 across the value 1 produces a sharp qualitative transition from bounded to unbounded loop signals, regardless of which specific partner module is used, unlike a pairing tuned only for one specific partner
minimal world: two black-box saturating nonlinear maps with tunable gain connected in a feedback ring. Mechanism world: sweep gamma1*gamma2 across 1 with a fixed [X] and observe the general threshold. Null twin: a controller hand-tuned to be stable only with one specific [X] (matched nominal gamma2), then [X] is swapped for a different subsystem with identical gamma2 but different internal order/structure. Mechanism-world composition remains stable purely from gamma1*gamma2<1; the tuned null twin becomes unstable despite identical gain [X].

blind_text:
statement: A population of simple predictive sub-models compete to predict the next observation; each model's weight is multiplied by its recent predictive likelihood (replicator/[X] update), and low-weight models are periodically pruned and replaced by mutated copies of high-weight models. Collective adaptation emerges from differential survival of models rather than gradient descent within any single model.
what exists: population of predictor sub-models f_j; weight w_j per model; shared observation stream; mutation/replacement operator
what changes: w_j *= likelihood(observation | f_j); normalize; prune bottom fraction and replace with mutated copies of top fraction
what persists: population-level concentration of weight on models matching the true generative process; surviving lineages
what is selected: models with highest recent predictive likelihood
what can reproduce: high-fitness models are copied (with mutation) into vacated population slots
what can learn: an implicit model of a possibly switching environment via shifting population composition rather than parameter gradients
what can transfer: surviving model structures adapt faster to structurally similar environments than reinitialized populations
distinguishing observable: after an abrupt regime switch, the population should recover faster than a single gradient-updated model of the same class, because minority pre-adapted models already existed in the tail of the distribution
minimal world: an environment that switches between two hidden Markov regimes; a population of order-k predictors competes via replicator updates; intervention: switch regime and measure recovery time and population diversity dynamics; null twin: a single predictor of the same class updated by online gradient descent, tuned to match pre-switch accuracy, compared on post-switch recovery speed.

nearest_priors.name: Sequential Monte Carlo / particle filter with resample-move rejuvenation (Gordon-Salmond-Smith bootstrap filter; Gilks & Berzuini resample-move; regularized/jittered particle filters), equivalently Bayesian model averaging implemented as discrete replicator dynamics (Harper; Shalizi)
nearest_priors.field: Bayesian statistics / signal processing / evolutionary game theory
nearest_priors.explains: Multiplying each weight by the likelihood and normalizing is exactly Bayes' rule and exactly the discrete replicator equation with likelihood as fitness, so [X] is almost certainly 'Bayesian'. Pruning low-weight particles and replacing them with perturbed copies of high-weight ones is resampling plus a move/jitter step. Weight concentrating on models that match the generative process is posterior concentration. Surviving lineages are particle genealogies. Tracking a switching hidden regime is standard filtering.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Deterministic truncation (bottom fraction replaced by copies of the top fraction) instead of stochastic multinomial or systematic resampling is a minor variant. The claim about transfer to structurally similar environments is not a standard particle-filter result.

nearest_priors.name: Multiplicative-weights / Hedge / Bayesian mixture of experts with fixed-share or tracking-the-best-expert (Littlestone-Warmuth; Herbster-Warmuth)
nearest_priors.explains: Experts compete on log-loss and weights are updated multiplicatively by predictive likelihood. Fast recovery after an abrupt regime switch comes from keeping weight mass in minority experts, which is what fixed-share is designed to do. This also covers the comparison against a single online-gradient learner.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It has no mutation or creation of new experts: the expert pool is fixed. It does not account for lineage structure or copy-with-variation reproduction.

nearest_priors.name: Evolutionary algorithms / evolution strategies with truncation selection, and learning classifier systems (Holland; XCS)
nearest_priors.explains: It explains the population of simple predictors, truncation selection of the bottom fraction, and mutated copies of the fittest. It also covers adaptation by differential survival rather than within-model gradients, maintenance of diversity for dynamic environments, and transfer via seeding with evolved populations.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Fitness here is typically not a cumulative multiplicative Bayesian likelihood weight. There is no explicit posterior interpretation of the normalized weights.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing structural. The mechanism is a resample-move particle filter (or Bayesian mixture of experts) over predictor structures, with truncation selection in place of stochastic resampling. The transfer claim and the specific 'faster than online gradient descent' recovery prediction are empirical consequences, not new machinery. Both are already discussed in the fixed-share and dynamic-environment evolutionary computation literatures.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare the described system against a standard bootstrap particle filter with multinomial resampling and Gaussian jitter of matched variance, and against a fixed-pool fixed-share mixture with a tuned share rate, all on the same two-regime HMM switch. If the recovery-time curves and diversity dynamics match the particle filter up to resampling-scheme noise, the mechanism is the particle filter. Then ablate mutation while keeping truncation, and separately ablate truncation while keeping a weight floor. If recovery depends only on retained tail mass (the weight floor), the fixed-share account suffices; if it requires generating new variants, the evolutionary/resample-move component is essential.

blind_text:
statement: Local weight updates are scaled by a per-channel precision estimate (inverse of recent error variance) that itself adapts online: channels with historically noisy/high-variance errors get down-weighted updates, while consistently reliable channels get amplified updates. This produces an emergent, context-sensitive learning rate per channel rather than a single global learning rate.
what exists: prediction channels with error signal e_i(t); running estimate of error variance v_i(t) per channel; precision pi_i(t) = 1/v_i(t); weights updated using precision-scaled error
what changes: v_i(t) <- (1-gamma)*v_i(t-1) + gamma*e_i(t)^2; pi_i(t) = 1/v_i(t); weight_i <- weight_i + alpha * pi_i(t) * e_i(t) * presynaptic_activity.
what persists: The precision profile pi_i persists as a running [X] encoding the relative reliability of each channel/context.
what is selected: Channels/predictions with consistently low error variance are given amplified influence on weight updates and downstream decisions (implicit selection of reliable predictors over noisy ones).
what can reproduce: A learned precision profile can be copied as a prior into a task instance facing similar heteroscedastic noise structure.
what can learn: Not just the content of predictions but which channels/contexts are reliable, adapting effective learning rate accordingly.
what can transfer: A precision profile learned in one noisy environment transfers to a environment with similar per-channel noise structure, producing faster, more stable adaptation than a learner starting with uniform precision.
distinguishing observable: Under experimentally injected heteroscedastic noise (some channels made noisier than others mid-training), the per-channel update magnitude should shrink specifically for the noisier channels and grow (relatively) for cleaner ones, tracking the injected noise profile; a fixed-learning-rate control (null) shows update magnitudes uniform across channels regardless of the injected noise structure, directly measurable via correlation between per-channel update size and per-channel injected noise variance.
minimal world: A multi-channel prediction task where each of several channels has an independently-set noise variance (some clean, some noisy) generating targets; the precision-weighted learner and a fixed-learning-rate learner are both trained online on the same channel stream. Intervention: after initial training, swap which channels are noisy vs clean and track how update magnitudes per channel adapt over subsequent trials. Null twin: the fixed-learning-rate learner, matched in architecture and average learning rate, subjected to the identical noise-swap intervention, expected to show no corresponding tracking of update magnitude to the noise assignment.

nearest_priors.name: Precision-weighted prediction error in predictive coding / free-energy learning (Friston; Feldman & Friston 2010)
nearest_priors.explains: Per-channel precision as inverse error variance, estimated online. Precision-scaled error driving local Hebbian-like weight updates (error x presynaptic activity). Down-weighting of unreliable channels. Precision acting as a learned reliability prior that can be reused.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. The specific EMA variance estimator is a simplification of the usual gradient-based precision learning. The transfer-as-copied-prior framing is an added experimental claim, not a new mechanism.

nearest_priors.name: Adaptive per-parameter learning rates: RMSprop / Adam / AdaGrad, and normalized or inverse-variance-weighted LMS
nearest_priors.explains: An EMA of squared signal, v <- (1-gamma)v + gamma*e^2, used to scale each channel's step. This yields an emergent per-channel effective learning rate instead of a global one. Warm-starting the optimizer state explains transfer.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: RMSprop normalizes by the square root of squared gradients, not the inverse error variance. It is also usually not interpreted as channel reliability or selection of predictors.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman filter gain / inverse-variance (Bayesian cue) weighting; Pearce-Hall and Mackintosh associability
nearest_priors.explains: Reliability-dependent weighting of evidence. Noisy sources receive smaller updates and reliable ones larger. Associability that adapts with the history of prediction error. Optimal cue combination by precision.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Kalman gain lowers learning under observation noise via a full variance model rather than an EMA of squared error. Pearce-Hall increases the learning rate with surprise, which is the opposite sign for volatile but reliable cues.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The only departure from standard precision-weighted predictive coding is using a raw EMA of squared prediction error as the variance estimate. That estimate conflates signal variance with noise variance, and it is a known heuristic.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Separate observation noise from volatility, meaning nonstationarity of the target mapping. A Kalman or hierarchical Bayesian learner (e.g., HGF) raises the learning rate for volatile but low-noise channels and lowers it for noisy stationary ones. The described EMA-of-squared-error rule lowers the rate for both, because both inflate e^2. Measure per-channel update magnitude under noise-only versus volatility-only manipulations.

blind_text:
statement: A mutation operator occasionally duplicates an existing functional module in a genome, leaving the original intact while applying subsequent mutations only to the copy. Over generations this produces module lineages that diverge into specialized variants while related tasks retain a shared ancestral core. Selection then can independently tune duplicated copies for different subtasks.
what exists: population of programs composed of modules with defined interfaces; module genealogy metadata
what changes: Duplication events copy a module (identical function) into the genome; point mutations then apply to the copy or elsewhere in the genome at a fixed background rate.
what persists: Original modules remain functional in the genome while duplicates diverge over generations; ancestry metadata persists.
what is selected: Programs with higher task fitness reproduce more; modules contributing to fitness gains are retained and further duplicated, deleterious duplicates are purged.
what can reproduce: Programs reproduce probabilistically by fitness, passing modules (with occasional duplication) to offspring.
what can learn: The population accumulates reusable, specialized sub-functions across generations.
what can transfer: A module evolved for one task can be reused with little modification in a task requiring a similar subcomputation.
distinguishing observable: Modules solving different tasks show detectable common ancestry (structural similarity) correlated with shared subtask demands, rather than unrelated convergent solutions.
minimal world: Genomes as trees of modules solving two related arithmetic subtasks embedded in a larger composite task; evolve populations with duplication+mutation versus point-mutation-only at matched total mutation rate, then track module ancestry and knock out candidate duplicated modules. Null twin: a point-mutation-only population with identical population size, generations, and mutation budget but no duplication operator, showing no ancestrally-related specialized module clusters.

blind_text:
statement: A system repeatedly applies a fixed local coarse-graining operator to its own representation, producing a tower of representations at increasing scales that keep only slow/relevant variables. Structure invariant under this flow (an [X] fixed point) becomes the emergent high-level representation, so hierarchy arises from repeated application of one simple rule rather than a designed architecture.
what exists: fine-grained state field x on a lattice/graph; coarse-graining operator R (block-average or majority); level sequence x^(0), x^(1)=R(x^(0)), ...
what changes: the representation is replaced by its coarse-grained image at each step; parameters of R may be tuned to preserve target [X] across the transform
what persists: features that are fixed points of R (self-similar structure) survive across levels
what is selected: coarse-graining rules maximizing retained predictive information about a downstream label at each step
what can reproduce: the same tuned operator R is reapplied identically at every level
what can learn: parameters of R are learned to preserve label-relevant [X] under repeated coarse-graining
what can transfer: coarse representations learned on one fine-grained instantiation transfer to systems with different fine details but matching coarse [X]
distinguishing observable: mutual information with the label decays much more slowly across levels than with nuisance details, giving a plateau at the true structural scale; a null twin coarse-graining via randomly permuted block assignment (matched compression ratio) shows label- and nuisance-information decaying at the same rate with no plateau
minimal world: A 1D/2D Ising-like lattice whose label is the sign of large-scale magnetization plus small-scale random noise spins; apply repeated block-decimation and measure mutual information with label vs. level, compared to a null twin using randomly permuted (scrambled-adjacency) block grouping with matched block size and arithmetic.

nearest_priors.name: Kadanoff block-spin / Wilson real-space renormalization group, where [X] = universality or an RG fixed point
nearest_priors.explains: It covers most of the mechanism. A fixed local coarse-graining operator (block averaging, majority rule or decimation) is applied repeatedly to a lattice field, giving a tower of scales. Irrelevant, fine-detail variables are discarded while relevant ones are kept. Fixed points of R define the self-similar structure that survives across levels. Universality accounts for transfer: systems with different microscopic details but the same coarse universality class share their coarse description. The Ising minimal world is the textbook example.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Classical RG has no downstream label. Its operator is designed by hand, not learned, and it is not chosen to maximise predictive information about a task variable.

nearest_priors.name: Real-space mutual information (RSMI) neural RG (Koch-Janusz & Ringel 2018), with related information-theoretic RG work (Lenggenhager et al.; Gordon et al.)
nearest_priors.explains: The parameters of the coarse-graining map are learned by maximising mutual information, and the learned map is then applied iteratively. It recovers relevant operators and fixed-point structure. It measures information retained across levels and compares it with poor coarse-grainings.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: RSMI maximises information about the spatial environment of each block, not about an external downstream label. The supervised, label-relevant selection criterion therefore has to come from elsewhere.

nearest_priors.name: Information bottleneck applied to deep hierarchical pooling (Tishby; also Mehta & Schwab's RBM–RG correspondence and weight-shared CNN/wavelet multiresolution pyramids)
nearest_priors.explains: It supplies the label-relevant compression: each layer keeps information about Y and discards nuisance information. A weight-shared local operator reapplied at every level gives hierarchy from one rule. Mutual information with the label versus with nuisance variables is plotted across layers.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It carries no notion of fixed points or universality of the operator itself. Standard CNNs also do not reuse one identical operator at every depth.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Very little. The only departure from RSMI-style learned real-space RG is that relevance is defined by a supervised downstream label rather than by the environment or long-range correlations. That amounts to swapping in an information-bottleneck objective. The permuted-adjacency null twin is a sensible control, but it is not a new mechanism: it simply destroys locality, and RG's relevance structure depends on locality.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Train R with the label objective on an Ising lattice where the label is deliberately set to a non-critical, non-long-range property, for example a local parity pattern that is RG-irrelevant. RG or RSMI would discard this information and flow to the physical fixed point regardless of the label. A label-driven bottleneck would instead keep the irrelevant-operator information and give a plateau at the wrong scale, with no fixed point matching known critical exponents. Separately, check whether the learned R's fixed point reproduces known exponents such as ν = 1 for the 2D Ising model.

blind_text:
statement: States are represented by their orbit under a specified symmetry group G, computed via a group-averaged or canonicalized invariant feature map, so the representation factors through the quotient space X/G. Inputs related by any g in G collapse to an identical representation. This produces automatic generalization to unseen group transformations without additional training examples covering them.
what exists: raw states x in X; a group G acting on X; an invariant map phi(x) (average or canonicalization over G)
what changes: raw x is replaced by phi(x) before downstream processing; candidate groups/generators can be swapped and tested
what persists: phi(x) is constant under x -> g.x for all g in G
what is selected: the candidate group whose induced phi minimizes downstream prediction error
what can reproduce: the canonicalization function can be copied to domains sharing the same symmetry
what can learn: which subgroup/generators actually leave the label invariant, via consistency testing
what can transfer: predictors trained on phi(x) transfer zero-shot to all g.x
distinguishing observable: zero-shot accuracy on group-transformed test inputs equals in-distribution accuracy for the invariant representation, while a non-equivariant representation of matched capacity shows a large accuracy drop under the same transformations
minimal world: Small grid images of shapes where label=shape identity and nuisance=90-degree rotation (G=cyclic rotation group). Train only on 0-degree orientation using phi(x)=average over the 4 rotations; test on unseen 90/180/270-degree rotations. The null twin uses raw pixel features of matched dimensionality and identical training but no group-averaging, then is tested identically.

nearest_priors.name: Group-averaged invariant features (Reynolds operator / invariant pooling; group-invariant networks such as G-CNNs with invariant pooling and Deep Sets-style symmetrization)
nearest_priors.field: Invariant theory; geometric deep learning; machine learning
nearest_priors.explains: Replacing x with phi(x)=(1/|G|)Σ_g f(g·x), which factors through X/G and is constant on orbits. It also explains exact zero-shot generalization to unseen group transforms, and why test accuracy on C4-rotated inputs matches in-distribution accuracy while raw pixel features drop sharply.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Choosing among candidate groups by downstream error, and learning which generators leave the label invariant.

nearest_priors.name: Canonicalization / orbit representatives (canonical forms, frame averaging, learned canonicalization, spatial transformer alignment)
nearest_priors.field: Algebra and computer vision; equivariant ML
nearest_priors.explains: The canonicalization alternative to averaging, representation factoring through the quotient, and reuse of the canonicalizer in other domains that share the symmetry.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The group-selection and consistency-testing loop.

nearest_priors.name: Symmetry discovery / learned invariance (Augerino, LieGAN, learned augmentation distributions, Bayesian model selection over invariances)
nearest_priors.explains: Selecting the subgroup or generators whose induced invariance minimizes prediction error or passes label-consistency tests, and rejecting over-large groups that would destroy label information.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Hard-coded exact invariance with no learning, which is the core of the minimal world.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The group-selection layer is standard invariance learning/model selection, and the minimal world only exercises fixed Reynolds averaging.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Include a label that is not invariant, such as a '6' vs '9' shape or orientation-dependent arrows. Plain Reynolds averaging with fixed G will collapse the classes to chance. The described selection mechanism should instead reject C4 in favour of a subgroup such as C2 or the trivial group. Separately, compare exact averaging against training on augmented raw pixels: only exact group averaging gives identical accuracy on every rotation for every input.

nearest_priors.field: Formal methods / constraint solving / controller synthesis
nearest_priors.explains: Constraint sets ordered by inclusion, which is the 'category ordered by refinement'. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The categorical framing itself: the terminal object/limit/cone vocabulary adds no operational content. It also does not cover the learned refinement-order heuristic or transfer of the limit object to related task diagrams.

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Search over whole parameter-set objects rather than variable assignments. It does not cover selecting a terminal object in a refinement order, or parallel cloning and transfer.
