blind_text:
statement: A predictor is trained across multiple environments that share a stable causal feature C -> Y but differ in the strength/sign of a spurious feature S's correlation with Y. An explicit invariance penalty forces the predictor's behavior to stay consistent when S is resampled (a synthetic do-operation) while C is held fixed, suppressing reliance on the environment-varying shortcut.
what exists: causal feature C; spurious feature S; label Y = f(C) + noise; multiple training environments e=1..E with different S-Y correlation strengths; predictor h(C,S)
what changes: training loss = sum_e risk_e(h) + lambda * (invariance penalty measuring prediction change under do-resampling of S at fixed C); weights are updated to jointly reduce risk and the penalty.
what persists: reliance on C strengthens over training as gradients exploiting S are actively suppressed by the penalty.
what is selected: feature-weight configurations producing consistent predictions across environments (i.e., invariant to S) are favored by the objective over configurations exploiting S.
what can reproduce: None; this is a training-time constraint on a single model.
what can learn: to use only the causal generative feature and ignore an environment-specific shortcut, inferred purely from cross-environment invariance, without being told which feature is causal.
what can transfer: the model generalizes to a environment where the S-Y correlation is reversed or absent, unlike a standard empirical-risk-minimization model.
distinguishing observable: accuracy on a test environment with the S-Y correlation flipped relative to training: the invariance-constrained model retains high accuracy while a matched-architecture [X] model (identical data, environments, and optimizer, but lambda=0) fails, revealing S-reliance.
minimal world: A synthetic dataset where C determines Y via a fixed function and S is a nuisance feature whose correlation with Y is 0.9 in env1, 0.7 in env2, and -0.9 in a held-out test env. Train (A) with the invariance penalty across env1/env2 and (B) an identical architecture with lambda=0 (null twin, pure [X]) on the same data. Evaluate both on the reversed test environment.

nearest_priors.name: Counterfactual invariance regularization / counterfactual consistency training (Veitch et al. 2021; counterfactual data augmentation with a consistency loss, cf. Kaushik et al. 2020, Garg et al. 2019 counterfactual logit pairing)
nearest_priors.field: causal machine learning / robust NLP and vision
nearest_priors.explains: A penalty on prediction change when the nuisance feature S is intervened on (resampled) with the causal feature C held fixed. It adds an ERM term plus a lambda-weighted consistency term. It suppresses the shortcut and transfers to test sets where the S-Y correlation is reversed. The null twin is ERM at lambda=0.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The claim that the causal feature is inferred 'without being told which feature is causal'. A counterfactual do-resampling of S requires knowing which variable is S. The multi-environment structure is also incidental here: the penalty works without environments.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant Risk Minimization (Arjovsky et al. 2019) and relatives (V-REx, Risk Extrapolation, IRMv1 gradient penalty)
nearest_priors.explains: Summed per-environment risk plus a lambda-weighted invariance penalty. Environments differ in spurious S-Y correlation while C->Y is stable. The causal feature is discovered purely from cross-environment invariance with no label on which feature is causal. It generalizes to a flipped-correlation test environment where ERM fails. This matches the standard colored-MNIST-style setup (0.9 / 0.7 / -0.9-like splits).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The penalty here is defined by prediction change under synthetic do-resampling of S at fixed C. IRM's penalty is per-environment optimality of a shared classifier (a gradient norm) or risk variance, and it needs no intervention oracle.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant Causal Prediction (Peters, Bühlmann & Meinshausen 2016) / domain-adversarial and group-robust training (DANN, GroupDRO)
nearest_priors.explains: Selects the predictors whose conditional relationship to Y is stable across environments, which identifies C as causal and rejects S. It gives robustness to shifted spurious correlations.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The gradient-based joint training with a soft lambda penalty on a single model (ICP uses hypothesis testing over subsets). The interventional resampling-consistency penalty is also not part of it.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing mechanistic; it is ERM + counterfactual-consistency/invariance penalty. One internal tension remains: the penalty requires an oracle for which feature to resample (S), yet the description claims causality is inferred purely from cross-environment invariance. That claim belongs to IRM, not to the stated penalty. The description thus blends two known mechanisms.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Remove the do-resampling oracle and keep only environment labels. Train (i) with the stated counterfactual-resampling penalty, which is now undefined or must guess S, and (ii) IRMv1/V-REx using only the environment partition. Evaluate both on the -0.9 environment. Separately, collapse env1 and env2 into a single environment. If the described model still succeeds with one environment, its effect comes from the counterfactual consistency penalty, not from cross-environment invariance, which would make IRM inapplicable.

blind_text:
statement: Agents write to and read from a shared scalar field embedded in the environment that decays over time, rather than storing history internally. Because the field outlives any individual agent and is shaped cumulatively by many agents' trajectories, it functions as a persistent, externalized, population-level memory that biases future behavior.
what exists: grid environment; scalar trace field per cell; mobile agents with position and simple local sensing; agent lifespan and replacement
what changes: Each step, agents deposit trace at their current cell proportional to task success, the field decays multiplicatively everywhere, and agents' movement probability is biased toward higher local field gradient.
what persists: The spatial trace pattern (e.g., an emergent low-cost route) persists across many agent lifetimes as long as deposit rate exceeds decay along that path.
what is selected: Paths/trajectories that get reinforced by more traffic are selected via positive feedback, independent of any single agent's memory.
what can reproduce: Agents reproduce probabilistically based on resources collected, but the field itself is inherited environmental structure, not genome.
what can learn: The population as a whole 'learns' an efficient path/policy even though no individual agent retains history.
what can transfer: spawned or replacement agents inherit the field's guidance immediately, transferring the population's accumulated knowledge without any information exchange between individuals.
distinguishing observable: Time-to-convergence on the shortest path decreases with population turnover rate in the field-mediated system and correlates with lagged field intensity along the eventual path; a null twin where agents move by the same local rule but read a field that is reset to random noise each step (deposits still happen but have zero persistence) shows no convergence and no lag correlation.
minimal world: World: a grid with a start and goal cell connected by two paths of different length; agents wander, deposit trace on success, field decays at rate d, movement biased by local field gradient. Intervention: measure fraction of agents taking the shorter path over time and its dependence on d and deposit rate. Null twin: identical agent movement and deposit rule, but the field array is overwritten with independent random noise (matched mean and variance to the real field) before each read step, eliminating persistence/spatial correlation while preserving field [X]; this twin never converges above chance on the shorter path.

nearest_priors.name: Stigmergy / pheromone-trail foraging (Grassé; Deneubourg et al. double-bridge experiment; Dorigo's Ant System / Ant Colony Optimization)
nearest_priors.field: Swarm intelligence, behavioral ecology, combinatorial optimization
nearest_priors.explains: Covers nearly all of the description. Agents deposit a trace in the environment, and the trace evaporates multiplicatively each step. Movement is biased toward stronger trace. Success-weighted deposits create positive feedback on shorter paths. The population converges on the shorter branch of a two-path bridge. The collective 'learns' a path with no individual memory. A persistence condition exists (deposit must exceed evaporation). The dependence on evaporation rate d and deposit rate is standard ACO parameter analysis.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Classic ACO does not include agent birth, death, or resource-based reproduction. It also makes no prediction that convergence speeds up with population turnover rate.

nearest_priors.name: Niche construction / ecological inheritance (Odling-Smee, Laland & Feldman)
nearest_priors.explains: Covers the framing of the field as non-genetic, inherited environmental structure. The field outlives individuals, and newborn agents benefit immediately from environmental modifications made by earlier generations. This is a second inheritance channel alongside reproduction.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not specify the evaporation dynamics, the gradient-following movement rule, or the shortest-path selection by positive feedback.

nearest_priors.name: Active walker / trail-formation models (Helbing, Schweitzer et al., human trail systems; also Physarum-style chemotaxis models)
nearest_priors.field: Statistical physics of self-organization, complex systems
nearest_priors.explains: Covers walkers that modify a decaying scalar field which in turn biases their motion by its gradient. These models produce emergent, persistent route networks that outlast individual walkers.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: They usually do not use success-weighted deposits, agent reproduction, or turnover-dependent convergence.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Two claims go beyond standard ACO. The first is that time-to-convergence decreases with population turnover rate. Plausibly this is because fresh agents behave less stochastically or bring no stale bias, but it is not a standard ACO result. The second is the resource-based reproduction layer. Both are handled by combining ACO with niche construction and ecological inheritance, and neither introduces a new mechanism. The null twin, a shuffled or noise field with matched marginal statistics, is a standard persistence-ablation control.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run standard ACO on the double bridge with a fixed population (no death or replacement) and vary d. Then add agent turnover at several rates, holding total agent-steps and deposit rate constant. If convergence time is independent of turnover once agent-steps are matched, the system is plain ACO. If convergence time falls with turnover beyond what the field explains, some agent-level state matters, such as reproduction biasing the population toward successful movers. Ablating reproduction (random replacement vs. resource-based replacement) isolates any contribution beyond stigmergy.

statement: A brief or weak synaptic activation event sets a transient molecular tag at that synapse without producing durable weight change; if within a limited time window a separate strong or novelty-driven event triggers a network-wide, non-synapse-specific production of plasticity-related resources, only tagged synapses capture those resources and convert their transient change into a lasting weight increase. what changes: a weak-stimulation event sets tag=1 (decaying over window τ_tag) and produces a small transient weight bump; if the global protein pool is elevated (triggered by a separate strong/ event) while tag=1, the synapse's durable weight increments proportionally to the protein pool level, converting the transient bump into a permanent change
what persists: the durable weight increment persists indefinitely once captured; the tag itself is transient and vanishes after the window regardless of capture
what is selected: among all weakly-tagged synapses across the network, only those whose tag overlaps in time with a protein-synthesis-triggering event are consolidated
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: the network can retroactively stabilize a behaviorally sub-threshold association if an unrelated salient/ event occurs within a critical time window, producing an associative rescue-of-weak-memory effect
what can transfer: consolidated associations persist as durable long-term memory usable in later test contexts, whereas untagged or uncaptured associations revert to baseline and are not retained
distinguishing observable: present a weak (sub-threshold for durable change) stimulus alone versus the same weak stimulus followed within the tag window by an unrelated strong/ stimulus, matching total stimulation exposure between conditions: the mechanism predicts durable strengthening of the weak association only in the paired condition, while a model in which durability depends solely on a synapse's own local stimulation strength (no shared protein pool, no tag) predicts no difference between conditions.
minimal world: A synapse receives a brief weak stimulation train known to be sub-threshold for lasting potentiation on its own. In one condition, an unrelated but strong/ stimulation event (driving a separate, non-overlapping set of synapses) occurs shortly afterward; in the control condition, no such event occurs, with total network stimulation matched by adding a strong event outside the tag window in a mismatch-timing control. The mechanism model implements a shared protein pool and per-synapse tags; the null twin implements local-only, synapse-autonomous consolidation with matched parameters for baseline potentiation magnitude. The diagnostic is durable weight retention at the weakly-stimulated synapse, which appears only in the mechanism model's within-window pairing condition.

nearest_priors.explains: Transient per-synapse tag set by weak stimulation. Strong or novelty event triggering non-synapse-specific plasticity-related protein synthesis. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. The description uses a network-wide pool, whereas the canonical version is mostly cell-wide or dendritic-compartment-wide. The linear proportional-to-pool capture rule is a modeling simplification (as in Clopath et al. 2008; Barrett et al. 2009).

nearest_priors.name: Three-factor learning rules / eligibility traces with neuromodulatory gating (e.g., dopamine-gated STDP, Izhikevich 2007; neo-Hebbian rules)
nearest_priors.explains: Local transient eligibility trace (tag) decaying over a window. A global broadcast third factor converts the trace into a durable weight change. Temporal credit assignment across delays.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The global factor here is a depletable protein resource triggered by a strong or novel event, not a reward-prediction signal. It does not by itself account for the separation of early-LTP and late-LTP or for resource capture and competition.

nearest_priors.name: Cascade / two-stage consolidation models (Clopath 2008 TagTriC model; Ziegler et al. 2015; Benna & Fusi synaptic consolidation)

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Generic cascade models (Fusi) lack the global cross-synapse resource sharing and the heterosynaptic rescue by an unrelated event. Only the STC-specific implementations include those features.

what can reproduce: Primitives can be recombined combinatorially to generate unboundedly many compositions from the same finite basis.

Null twin: an environment where each episode's rendering function is drawn independently at random (no shared primitive basis) but matched in per-episode observation [X] (same marginal distributions), so surface-level [X] match but there is no reusable substructure to exploit.

blind_text:
statement: A structural mutation operator duplicates a randomly chosen subgraph (a node together with its input edges) within a computation graph, creating a redundant parallel copy, and then allows the duplicate's parameters/operation to independently drift under subsequent point mutations across generations. This is distinct from point mutation alone because it creates a redundant substrate that can be preserved as backup or diverge into a specialized sub-function without disrupting the original pathway.
what exists: population of computation graphs (nodes = primitive ops, edges = data flow); genome = graph [X] + node parameters; a duplication-divergence mutation operator and a point-mutation operator
what changes: With probability p_dup, a random subgraph is duplicated and reattached in parallel to the original; with probability p_point (applied to all nodes including duplicates), individual node parameters/operations are perturbed; each generation, fitness-based selection determines which mutated graphs survive to reproduce.
what persists: Duplicated substructures persist as redundant backups across generations unless divergence and selection repurpose one copy into a distinct specialized sub-function.
what is selected: Graphs with higher task fitness reproduce more; among duplicate pairs, whichever divergent trajectory improves fitness (via specialization or robustness) is retained by selection.
what can reproduce: Whole graphs reproduce with mutation into the next generation; subgraphs 'reproduce' internally via the duplication step itself.
what can learn: Population-level structural learning across generations (which sub-functions are useful is discovered evolutionarily, not within a single lifetime).
what can transfer: A duplicated-and-diverged module that specialized into a sub-function can be excised and transplanted into a different graph solving a related task, tested for immediate functional contribution without further tuning.
distinguishing observable: Populations evolving under duplication-divergence should show a higher rate of acquisition of qualitatively sub-functions (measured via time-to-first-appearance of a functional module and via graph modularity/Q-score) than a matched population restricted to point mutations only at an equalized total mutation rate; the point-mutation-only population instead shows smoother, more gradual fitness gains without discrete modular innovation events.
minimal world: A population of small computation graphs solving a composite task requiring two distinct sub-functions (e.g. parity-of-half-the-inputs [X] magnitude-threshold-of-the-other-half) evolved via genetic search. Intervention: run the population under the duplication-divergence operator vs point-mutation-only, with total per-generation mutation rate equalized between conditions. Null twin: the point-mutation-only population, matched in total mutation rate and population size, tracked for the same modularity and -subfunction-[X] metrics across an equal number of generations.

blind_text:
statement: Among candidate decompositions of varying rank, the rank is selected as the smallest one whose held-out prediction error is within a tolerance of the best achievable error, implementing a complexity-penalized selection pressure over model structure rather than a fixed a priori rank.
what exists: a family of candidate models at ranks R=1,2,3,...; a held-out validation split of tensor entries; an error tolerance parameter
what changes: at each rank, factors are trained to convergence on the training split; validation error is recorded; the selected rank is the minimal one meeting the tolerance criterion.
what persists: only the selected-rank model and its factors persist forward; other candidates are discarded.
what is selected: the rank/model whose held-out generalization is adequate at minimal complexity.
what can reproduce: the selection procedure itself (train-multiple-ranks, pick-minimal-adequate) can be reapplied to any tensor task.
what can learn: an appropriate complexity level for a given data-generating process without being told the true rank.
what can transfer: the selection procedure transfers across tasks even though the selected rank itself may differ per task.
distinguishing observable: the selected rank should track the true generative rank across many resampled datasets of varying noise level, whereas a fixed-rank-always-maximal baseline shows constant rank regardless of noise and overfits (larger train/validation error gap) at high noise.
minimal world: Generate tensors from known true ranks (1, 2, 4) under several noise levels. Run the rank-selection procedure and record selected rank and held-out error versus a baseline that always fits the maximum candidate rank. The null twin performs the same multi-rank training and comparison but selects rank uniformly at random among candidates that beat a trivial baseline (matching the computational budget of training multiple ranks) rather than by the minimal-adequate criterion, showing whether the specific selection rule (not just trying multiple ranks) is responsible for tracking true rank.

nearest_priors.explains: Training candidate models at increasing complexity, recording held-out error, choosing the smallest one within a tolerance of the best, discarding the others, and reapplying the procedure across tasks. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing structural. The tensor-specific details, such as a held-out split over tensor entries and CP/Tucker factor training, are only the domain instantiation.

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The minimal-adequate tolerance rule is not intrinsic to it. Many variants pick the argmin instead, or use core consistency.

nearest_priors.name: Occam/parsimony-penalized selection (AIC/BIC/MDL, elbow/scree heuristics)
nearest_priors.explains: A complexity-penalized preference for the simplest adequate model, and recovery of the true rank as data grows.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It uses an analytic penalty rather than an empirical held-out tolerance, and has no explicit validation split.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The 'selection pressure / reproduce / transfer' framing is evolutionary-sounding vocabulary for an ordinary hyperparameter-selection procedure. The null twin, random choice among ranks that beat a trivial baseline, is a sensible ablation but not a new mechanism.

If selections coincide, the mechanism is the one-SE CV rule. Separately, compare against a BIC-selected rank to test whether the held-out tolerance offers anything beyond analytic penalization.

nearest_priors.name: Coincidence-detection gating / AND-gated plasticity (dual-modulator coincidence, e.g. NMDA-like or cAMP adenylyl cyclase coincidence detection) combined with morphogen-gradient prepatterning (Turing/Wolpert positional information)
nearest_priors.explains: The requirement for joint presence of two signals. Overlap-zone prepatterning of learning eligibility. Heritable, geometry-determined templates reproduced across offspring.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The informativeness criterion: a product/AND gate is exactly the null that the description says should persist under the redundancy manipulation.

parsed.unexplained_residual: The specific coupling is not covered by any single prior: a three-factor rule whose third factor is local co-information between two modulator time series and the Hebbian correlation. The sign convention of co-information (redundancy positive vs synergy positive) is left ambiguous, so it is unclear whether redundancy should collapse or enhance gating. The mechanism is still runnable, and each ingredient is known.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: On the grid, drive X and Y from a shared source with a linear mixing so their temporal fluctuations become redundant. Rescale each field so its time-averaged spatial concentration map is exactly unchanged. Then compare two conditions. Under a standard three-factor rule gated by X·Y (or X AND Y), plastic zones should be unchanged. Under the co-information-gated rule, plastic zones should vanish (or flip, depending on sign convention). Also test the reverse: decorrelate X and Y at fixed concentration and check whether learning is restored.

blind_text:
statement: A recurrent network of nonlinear units maintains its global coupling strength near a critical value (edge of chaos, where the largest Lyapunov exponent is approximately zero) via a local homeostatic gain-adjustment rule, rather than a fixed or externally-tuned coupling. This self-tuned [X] jointly maximizes both short-term memory capacity and input-separation ability, providing a general-purpose substrate usable across many downstream readout tasks.
what exists: recurrent network of nonlinear units with local gain parameter per unit; global/local coupling strength g; homeostatic rule targeting a set-point of local activity variance; external driving input; linear readout layer
what changes: Each step, units update via nonlinear recurrent dynamics driven by input; each unit's local gain adjusts slowly to bring its activity variance toward a homeostatic target, indirectly moving the effective coupling g toward the critical value for the current input [X].
what persists: The dynamical regime (near-zero Lyapunov exponent) is maintained as an attracting operating point of the homeostatic feedback, persisting despite changes in input [X].
what is selected: No explicit selection process; the homeostatic rule itself acts as a local, task-independent optimization toward the critical regime.
what can reproduce: Not applicable.
what can learn: The homeostatic gain rule learns/tracks the appropriate coupling without any supervised signal (unsupervised self-tuning); separately, a linear readout learns specific tasks from the network's states.
what can transfer: The same underlying network, once at [X], supports multiple different linear readouts (multiple tasks) with high performance, i.e., the representation transfers across tasks better than off-critical regimes.
distinguishing observable: Sweeping the coupling parameter g and measuring both delayed-recall memory capacity and stimulus-separation capacity shows both jointly peak near the same critical g, and the homeostatic system's effective g tracks this peak as input [X] change; a null twin with a fixed (non-adaptive) coupling value chosen to match the average dynamical range but without local homeostatic feedback fails to re-track the peak when input [X] shift, showing degraded joint memory/separation performance after the shift.
minimal world: World: a recurrent network of tanh units receiving a time-varying scalar input stream with two different statistical regimes (regime A, then regime B) presented in sequence; a local homeostatic gain-adjustment rule updates each unit's gain based on a target activity variance. Intervention: measure memory capacity (linear reconstruction of past input) and separation capacity (distinguishability of nearby input trajectories) as functions of swept fixed g, and separately track these metrics over time for the homeostatically-adapting network across the regime A-to-B transition. Null twin: same network and readout tasks, but coupling g is fixed at the value optimal for regime A (no ongoing homeostatic adjustment); compare memory/separation performance of the adaptive vs. fixed-g network specifically during and after the transition to regime B.

nearest_priors.name: Reservoir computing / echo state network at the edge of chaos with intrinsic plasticity (Triesch-style IP; Schrauwen et al. 2008; Boedecker et al. 2012)
nearest_priors.explains: Recurrent tanh reservoir with a linear readout, and a local unsupervised gain/bias adaptation that targets activity statistics. Memory capacity (Jaeger) and separation property (Maass) both peak near a zero Lyapunov exponent. One reservoir serves multiple readouts.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Classic IP targets an output distribution (e.g., exponential or Gaussian), not variance explicitly. That it re-tracks criticality across input-regime shifts is claimed rather than guaranteed, since IP can overshoot into chaos.

nearest_priors.name: Homeostatic regulation toward criticality / flow control (Schubert & Gros 2021 'local homeostatic regulation of the spectral radius'; synaptic scaling, Turrigiano)
nearest_priors.explains: A local variance set-point rule drives the effective spectral radius or coupling g toward about 1 (the critical point), tracking input statistics. Target-variance homeostasis sets gain in an input-dependent way.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Joint memory/separation optimization and multi-task transfer are not intrinsic to it; they are imported from the reservoir literature.

nearest_priors.name: Self-organized criticality via adaptive networks (Bornholdt & Rohlf; Levina-Herrmann-Geisel dynamic synapses)
nearest_priors.explains: Local slow adaptation makes the critical regime an attracting fixed point of the dynamics, and it persists under perturbation.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Linear readouts, memory capacity and separation metrics, and the continuous tanh Lyapunov-exponent framing.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is unexplained. The only specific claim is that a variance set-point, rather than an entropy/IP target, robustly lands on λ≈0 across input regimes. This is known to depend on the input and is partially addressed by Schubert & Gros.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Swap the variance-target rule for standard IP (Triesch KL-to-exponential) and for flow control (Schubert–Gros). Across the A→B input shift, measure the post-shift Lyapunov exponent and the joint MC/separation. If the described rule shows no advantage, it is just the known prior. Also vary input amplitude alone to test whether the variance target conflates input drive with recurrent gain.

blind_text:
statement: Undercutting evidence sets a belief's active-flag to false without altering or deleting its stored content/confidence; removal of that evidence restores the active-flag, instantly reactivating the original belief. This is distinct from rebutting evidence, which directly updates confidence toward negation.
what exists: belief nodes with (content, confidence, active-flag); evidence nodes; defeater edges typed undercutting or rebutting
what changes: Firing an undercutting edge sets target active-flag false while preserving content/confidence; firing a rebutting edge updates confidence toward negation directly; removing the undercutting evidence restores active-flag true with content untouched.
what persists: Suppressed belief content and confidence persist unmodified in memory during suppression.
what is selected: None; this is a control signal governing usability, not a competitive selection process.
what can reproduce: N/A.
what can learn: The threshold of evidence strength required to trigger suppression can be tuned from downstream rates of false defeats versus missed defeats.
what can transfer: Defeater-type-to-belief-type mapping rules can transfer across belief instances of the same type.
distinguishing observable: After the defeater is removed, recovery of full original confidence is near-instantaneous (single timestep) for the suppress-and-preserve mechanism, versus a system that deletes/decrements on defeat and must slowly re-accumulate evidence to restore the belief, producing a measurable recovery-latency gap.
minimal world: A belief 'the light is on' supported by 3 evidence pieces; at t=20 add undercutting evidence ('visual system was drugged') that suppresses without contradicting; at t=40 remove that evidence. Null twin: identical setup but defeat implemented as confidence decrement/deletion requiring re-accumulation of the 3 evidences, compared on post-removal recovery time and content fidelity.

nearest_priors.name: Pollock's defeasible reasoning (undercutting vs rebutting defeaters), as implemented in OSCAR
nearest_priors.explains: The rebutting/undercutting distinction and the canonical example (a red-light percept undercut by 'illuminated by red light' or 'drugged'). Undercutters remove support without asserting the negation. Defeat status is recomputed so the conclusion is reinstated when the defeater is withdrawn, and the underlying inference graph is preserved rather than deleted. Pollock also attaches degrees of justification to conclusions.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The explicit per-node boolean active-flag held separately from a stored confidence. Pollock treats rebuttal as a competing reason for the negation, not a direct confidence update. Nor does it cover tuning the defeat threshold from false-defeat versus missed-defeat rates, or learned transfer of defeater-type-to-belief-type mapping rules.

nearest_priors.name: Justification-based Truth Maintenance System (Doyle JTMS) with IN/OUT labelling and non-monotonic justifications
nearest_priors.explains: Nodes persist with their content while their status toggles IN/OUT. An 'unless'/OUT-list justification acts as an undercutter. Retracting the defeating assumption relabels the node IN in a single propagation step, with no re-derivation of evidence, which gives the instantaneous recovery that is the distinguishing observable.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Graded confidence and a rebutting edge that updates confidence toward negation. Threshold learning and rule transfer are also absent.

nearest_priors.name: Dung abstract argumentation / ASPIC+ with undercut and rebut attacks (reinstatement)
nearest_priors.explains: Typed attacks (undercut vs rebut) and acceptance status recomputed from the attack graph. Removing an attacker reinstates the argument unchanged.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Numeric confidence dynamics, learned thresholds and transfer. Weighted or probabilistic variants would be needed for the confidence part.

parsed.unexplained_residual: The only additions are minor engineering ones. First, the defeat-trigger threshold is learned from the downstream cost of false versus missed defeats, which is ordinary signal-detection criterion tuning. Second, defeater-to-belief-type mapping rules generalise across belief instances, which is ordinary schema or rule generalisation. Neither is central, and both are standard.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Present a rebutting defeater, then remove it, and compare recovery with the undercutting case. The description predicts that only undercut recovery is single-step, because rebuttal directly overwrote confidence. In Pollock/JTMS/Dung, removing a rebutting argument also reinstates the belief instantly, since status is recomputed from the graph. A slow recovery after rebutter removal would indicate the described hybrid, where rebuttal is an in-place update and only undercut is status-gating.

blind_text:
statement: Belief-forming pathways are scored not on single-environment accuracy but on accuracy across many perturbed replicas of the environment that hold the target truth fixed while resampling nuisance variables. Pathways whose correctness depended on accidental correlation with nuisance variables collapse under perturbation and are pruned, while causally-coupled pathways survive.
what exists: population of belief-forming pathways (sensor-to-inference chains); a hidden truth-maker variable; resamplable nuisance variables; per-pathway accuracy score across replicas
what changes: Each round, the environment is resampled on nuisance variables holding truth fixed; pathway accuracy is recomputed across replicas; pathways below a survival threshold are pruned or down-weighted, survivors are retained (optionally mutated) for the next round.
what persists: Pathways causally coupled to the truth-maker persist across many perturbation rounds; accidentally-correct pathways do not.
what is selected: Causally-grounded pathways are selected over Gettier-style accidentally-correct pathways.
what can reproduce: Surviving pathways can be duplicated and mutated to seed the next generation.
what can learn: Pathway parameters adapt under selection to strengthen causal coupling to the truth-maker.
what can transfer: Surviving pathway structure transfers to environment instances sharing the same causal truth-maker but different nuisance values.
distinguishing observable: In the original fixed training environment, a causally-grounded pathway and an accidentally-correct pathway show identical accuracy; only across perturbed replicas does the accidentally-correct pathway's accuracy collapse toward chance while the grounded one remains high — the signature requires the multi-replica test, not a single measurement.
minimal world: A hidden hour-variable H; pathway A reads H via a noisy but causally coupled clock sensor; pathway B outputs a fixed constant that happens to equal H in the training environment. Both score 100% in the original single environment. Null twin: evaluate only in the original environment (cannot distinguish A and B); true test resamples H across many replicas while holding training-environment marginal [X] fixed, revealing A's persistence and B's collapse.

nearest_priors.name: Domain randomization / invariant risk minimization, i.e. selecting predictors whose accuracy is invariant across environments that resample spurious features
nearest_priors.field: Machine learning (causal representation learning, out-of-distribution generalization, sim-to-real robotics)
nearest_priors.explains: Scoring by accuracy across many perturbed replicas rather than one environment. Pathways that rely on spurious correlation with nuisance variables collapse, while causally coupled predictors survive. Transfer to new environments with the same causal mechanism but different nuisance values. The observation that in-distribution accuracy cannot separate the two kinds of predictor, and only multi-environment evaluation can (the shortcut-learning signature).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The population-level prune, duplicate and mutate loop. IRM and domain randomization usually train a single model by gradient descent, not by evolutionary selection over a population.

nearest_priors.name: Evolutionary algorithm / genetic programming with fitness averaged over randomized environments (robust or noisy-fitness evolution)
nearest_priors.explains: A population of pathways, a per-individual fitness score, a survival threshold used to truncate, and survivors that are duplicated and mutated each generation. Parameters adapt under selection. Fitness evaluated over resampled test cases selects robust solutions over overfit ones.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The epistemic framing (truth-maker, Gettier cases). This prior does not by itself specify which variables must be held fixed and which resampled.

nearest_priors.name: Nozick's tracking / sensitivity condition, and Goldman's process reliabilism across relevant alternatives
nearest_priors.explains: The distinction between knowledge and a Gettier case: a belief-forming process counts as knowledge-conferring only if it would track the truth in nearby counterfactual situations. A stopped-clock style constant output is correct by accident and fails sensitivity. The minimal world is literally Russell's stopped clock.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Any computational update rule, population, mutation or pruning dynamics. It is a static criterion, not a run mechanism.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing substantive is new. There is an internal inconsistency, though. The statement says replicas hold the target truth fixed and resample only nuisance variables. Under that protocol a constant-output pathway such as B stays correct and is never pruned. The minimal world instead resamples H itself, which is a sensitivity or counterfactual test. For pathway B to collapse, the truth variable must vary across replicas, with nuisances decorrelated from it. The description conflates invariance to nuisance variables with sensitivity to the truth; both are covered by existing priors (IRM and Nozick's sensitivity respectively).
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the population in two conditions. In the first, the truth H is held fixed and only nuisance variables are resampled. In the second, H is resampled and nuisance variables are decorrelated from it. If pruning of constant pathways like B happens only in the second condition, the operative mechanism is standard sensitivity/IRM-style environment variation plus evolutionary truncation selection. That would confirm the composite prior. A mechanism that pruned B under the first condition would require something beyond known priors.

blind_text:
statement: Perturbations applied to [X] coefficients during exploration/learning are not isotropic random noise but are structured by which [X] relation currently has the highest violation rate: units contributing most to that relation's failure are perturbed preferentially. This makes the mutation operator itself a function of the transform algebra rather than a fixed noise process.
what exists: code coefficients a_i, per-unit contribution scores to each relation's violation (via gradient or ablation sensitivity), a relation-violation-rate tracker.
what changes: mutation variance per unit sigma_i is set proportional to that unit's sensitivity to the currently worst-violated relation, then noise ~N(0,sigma_i^2) is added before the next encode-update cycle.
what persists: the sensitivity-tracking [X] persist and slowly update across many cycles, forming a smoothed history rather than instantaneous noise.
what is selected: mutated codes that reduce the targeted relation's violation without increasing others are kept; other mutations are reverted.
what can reproduce: none directly, though favorable perturbations can be consolidated into the dictionary via subsequent gradient steps.
what can learn: the per-unit sensitivity map and, indirectly, a dictionary reshaped toward relation-robust configurations faster than uniform exploration would achieve.
what can transfer: sensitivity maps learned for one relation should partially transfer to a related relation sharing algebraic structure (e.g., shift-sensitivity map informing reverse-sensitivity search).
distinguishing observable: measure convergence speed (number of mutation-update cycles) to a target low-violation state for the relation-targeted mutation operator versus isotropic random mutation of equal total injected variance.
minimal world: World: fixed dictionary, [X] for short 1-D sequences, three relations with independently controllable violation-inducing noise sources. Intervention: apply relation-targeted mutation versus isotropic mutation with matched total variance budget. Null twin: mutation with per-unit variance shuffled randomly among units (same variance profile shape, same total budget) but not assigned according to actual relation-sensitivity, decoupling the targeting information from the noise magnitude.

blind_text:
statement: The sign of [X] modification is governed by a sliding modification threshold that rises and falls with a low-pass-filtered average of the unit's own past squared activity, so that activity above the neuron's recent norm produces potentiation and activity below it produces depression. This produces stable, self-referential selectivity without any externally fixed threshold.
what exists: postsynaptic activity y(t); input x(t); weight w; sliding threshold theta(t) as a running average of y(t)^2
what changes: dw = eta * x * y * (y - theta); theta updates as a low-pass filter of y^2 over a longer timescale than w
what persists: theta itself persists as a memory trace of recent activity history that biases future plasticity direction
what is selected: input patterns that drive activity above the adapting threshold are potentiated; more common/weaker patterns are suppressed, yielding selective tuning
what can reproduce: the resulting tuning curve can be re-instantiated in a naive unit exposed to the identical training distribution
what can learn: the unit acquires selectivity for the dominant recurring input pattern starting from an initially unselective state
what can transfer: acquired selectivity transfers as differential (sharper) response to inputs resembling the trained pattern versus others
distinguishing observable: swapping which of two input patterns is more frequent should reverse which pattern the unit becomes selective for; a fixed-threshold [X] rule exposed to the same [X] would show runaway potentiation or no differential selectivity
minimal world: single unit alternately driven by pattern A and pattern B at unequal exposure frequencies; intervention: swap the exposure frequencies of A and B partway through training; null twin: same [X] update but with theta fixed as a constant rather than history-dependent.

nearest_priors.name: BCM (Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro, 1982) synaptic modification rule with a sliding modification threshold (Intrator-Cooper 1992 variant: theta = E[y^2])
nearest_priors.field: computational neuroscience / theory of visual cortical plasticity
nearest_priors.explains: Nearly everything. The update dw = eta*x*y*(y - theta) is the BCM phi(y, theta) = y(y - theta) form. Theta is a low-pass filtered average of y^2 on a slower timescale than w, as in BCM. Activity above theta gives LTP and below gives LTD. The sliding threshold stabilises the rule, so no fixed threshold is needed. The unit develops selectivity starting unselective. A fixed-theta null gives runaway or non-selective behaviour, which is the textbook BCM argument. A naive unit trained on the same distribution re-develops the same tuning. Stronger response to inputs like the trained pattern is BCM orientation selectivity.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Standard BCM does not guarantee selectivity for the more frequent pattern. With theta = E[y^2], a unit selective for a pattern of probability p has a response scaling like 1/p. Both selective fixed points are stable, so which one is reached depends on initial conditions and basin sizes. Swapping frequencies mid-training need not reverse an already-established selectivity, which is hysteresis. The description is also internally inconsistent here: it says the unit selects the 'dominant recurring' pattern, yet also says 'more common/weaker patterns are suppressed'.

nearest_priors.name: Metaplasticity (Abraham & Bear 1996): activity-history-dependent shift of the LTP/LTD crossover point
nearest_priors.explains: Theta works as a persistent trace of recent postsynaptic activity that biases the sign of future plasticity. This is the 'what persists' clause, and it is the biological substrate proposed for the BCM sliding threshold.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It gives no explicit weight update equation. It does not derive how competitive selectivity between input patterns emerges.

nearest_priors.name: Stabilised Hebbian learning via normalisation or homeostasis (Oja's rule; Turrigiano synaptic scaling)
nearest_priors.explains: It prevents the runaway potentiation of plain Hebbian or fixed-threshold rules, using a slow activity-dependent regulatory variable. Oja's rule also yields tuning to the dominant input direction, the principal component, which matches 'selectivity for the dominant recurring pattern'.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It lacks the sign-reversing LTD region below a sliding threshold. It lacks the BCM-specific cubic (higher-order moment) nonlinearity, so it gives PCA-like tuning rather than BCM-like selective, sparse tuning.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the claimed behaviour under frequency swap is unexplained: that selectivity tracks the more frequent pattern and reverses when frequencies are swapped. Standard BCM analysis predicts bistable selective fixed points and history dependence, so reversal is not guaranteed. The rarer pattern, not the dominant one, can even yield the larger response. The rest is BCM with at most renaming.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Train a unit with theta = <y^2>_tau until it is fully selective for pattern A (frequency p_A > p_B). Then swap the frequencies and run for many theta time constants. Pure BCM predicts that selectivity for A persists, with only the response amplitudes rescaling. The described mechanism predicts a switch to B. Also vary the initial weights at fixed frequencies. If the selected pattern depends on initial conditions rather than only on frequency, the mechanism is BCM.

blind_text:
statement: A quad-tree refinement rule requires that a cell subdivide into four self-similar children only if its measured local sensitivity exceeds a threshold scaled by cell-size^alpha, coupling abstraction resolution to local Lipschitz sensitivity at every recursion depth. This produces, by construction, a fractal refinement partition rather than uniform grid refinement.
what exists: quad-tree partition to depth D_max; per-cell interval over-approximation box; per-cell sensitivity estimate sigma(cell); refinement threshold theta scaled by cell-size^alpha
what changes: a cell subdivides iff sigma(cell) > theta*size(cell)^alpha; children inherit parent's sound bound until refined
what persists: the final partition boundary between refined/unrefined regions is a fixed-point self-similar structure once refinement halts
what is selected: cells are selected for refinement (kept fine) or merged (pruned) based on the sensitivity/scale ratio, yielding a minimal sound partition
what can reproduce: the subdivision rule reproduces itself identically at every recursion level (literal self-similar reproduction of the operator)
what can learn: theta and alpha can be tuned from data to hit a target error budget while minimizing total cell count
what can transfer: a fitted (theta, alpha) pair transfers to but statistically similar functions, predicting required refinement depth without recomputation
distinguishing observable: log(depth) vs log(1/sigma) follows the imposed linear relation with slope alpha across the tree, versus no correlation under uniform fixed-depth refinement, whose resulting partition has box-counting dimension equal to ambient dimension
minimal world: World: a 2D rugged (Weierstrass-like) scalar function requiring sound interval bounding everywhere. Intervention: apply the sensitivity-scaled refinement rule and measure final partition's box-counting dimension and error-vs-cell-count curve. Null twin: same function, same total cell budget, but uniform-grid (or randomly placed, count-matched) cells ignoring sigma; matched mean cell size and total memory, but its partition dimension equals ambient dimension and error is not concentrated near true high-sensitivity zones.

blind_text:
statement: Alongside fast [X] (correlation-based) synaptic plasticity, each unit's total incoming synaptic weight is multiplicatively rescaled on a slow timescale to drive that unit's time-averaged firing rate toward a fixed homeostatic set-point. This scaling preserves the relative pattern of weights (hence learned selectivity) while correcting the overall gain, preventing runaway excitation or silencing that unconstrained [X] plasticity alone would produce.
what exists: recurrent network of units with firing rates r_i; target set-point rate r*; synaptic weights w_ij; fast [X] update; slow multiplicative scaling factor per unit
what changes: fast timescale: Δw_ij ∝ η_H · r_i · r_j ([X]); slow timescale: w_ij(t+1) = w_ij(t) · [1 + η_S·(r* - avg_r_i)] applied multiplicatively to all incoming weights of unit i
what persists: the relative ratios among a unit's incoming weights (its learned selectivity pattern) are preserved through scaling; only overall gain is corrected
what is selected: network configurations that remain within a bounded, functional dynamic range under continual [X] are the only ones that persist stably
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: the network can undergo continual [X] over long input sequences without catastrophic weight blow-up or unit silencing
what can transfer: after a perturbation (e.g., reduced input drive), the scaling mechanism restores functional activity levels and preserved selectivity, allowing continued task performance without relearning from scratch
distinguishing observable: under long-run continual [X] training, the network with scaling maintains bounded weight norms and firing rates near r*, while an otherwise identical network without scaling exhibits runaway weight growth or unit death; after an abrupt halving of input drive strength, the scaling network recovers firing rates toward r* within a bounded time window while the non-scaling network remains permanently at the perturbed rate
minimal world: A small recurrent network receiving a long sequence of correlated Poisson-like input patterns, trained continually with [X] plasticity. Intervention: at a fixed point mid-training, halve the input drive strength (simulating deafferentation) and track recovery. Null twin: identical network, initial weights, input sequence, and [X] rate, but with the slow multiplicative scaling factor fixed at 1 (no homeostatic correction).

nearest_priors.explains: The whole mechanism. Fast Hebbian correlation-based updates run alongside slow multiplicative scaling of all excitatory inputs to a neuron. The scaling is driven by the gap between the average firing rate and a target rate. It preserves relative weights, so stored information is kept. It prevents runaway potentiation or silencing. After activity blockade or deafferentation, firing rates recover to the set-point.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing substantive. The only extra details are the specific discrete-time update form and the null-twin experimental design, which are just parameterisation choices.

nearest_priors.name: Oja's rule / weight normalization in Hebbian learning (von der Malsburg 1973; Miller & MacKay 1994 multiplicative normalization)
nearest_priors.explains: Bounding Hebbian weight growth while keeping the relative weight pattern, through multiplicative normalization of each unit's incoming weights.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The firing-rate set-point target. These rules normalize weight norm, not activity. They therefore do not predict recovery of firing rate after input drive is halved, and they have no separate slow timescale.

nearest_priors.name: BCM rule with sliding modification threshold (Bienenstock, Cooper & Munro 1982)
nearest_priors.explains: Stabilization of Hebbian learning through slow, activity-dependent homeostasis that pushes the time-averaged activity toward a stable range, preventing runaway growth.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The global multiplicative rescaling that preserves weight ratios. In BCM, homeostasis acts synapse by synapse through the potentiation/depression threshold, not as a uniform gain factor. Its recovery from deafferentation also differs.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The mechanism is the standard 'Hebbian learning + multiplicative synaptic scaling' model. One minor point: the null twin's rates 'remain permanently at the perturbed rate' only approximately, because Hebbian drift would keep changing them.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Halve the input drive and then compare the weight distributions before and after recovery. Synaptic scaling predicts that all weights of a unit are rescaled by one common factor, so the rank order and ratios are preserved and the distribution is multiplicatively stretched. Oja/norm-based normalization predicts no firing-rate recovery at a fixed norm. BCM predicts synapse-specific, input-correlation-dependent changes rather than a uniform multiplicative factor.

blind_text:
statement: Perturbed variant datasets generated by sampling with replacement from an original dataset induce variation in fitted model parameters that approximates the true sampling distribution of an estimator. This variation can be used to estimate the estimator's variance without any analytic derivation, and is distinct from perturbing the estimate directly with unstructured noise.
what exists: original dataset D of size n; bootstrap replicate D* drawn with replacement from D; estimator theta(D)
what changes: each replicate D* induces a estimate theta*(D*); repeating this many times generates an empirical distribution of theta*
what persists: the empirical marginal distribution of the data is approximately preserved across replicates
what is selected: not applicable directly; in aggregation (bagging) replicate-derived models are retained and averaged
what can reproduce: dataset offspring D* are generated repeatedly from the parent dataset D
what can learn: the variance/uncertainty of the estimator theta, estimated from the spread of theta* across replicates
what can transfer: bootstrap-estimated variance transfers to guide sample-size or design choices on related future studies with similar data-generating structure
distinguishing observable: the distribution of bootstrap replicate [X] matches the analytically known sampling distribution (e.g., for the sample mean or median) even for skewed source distributions, whereas directly adding independent Gaussian noise to the point estimate misrepresents the true (often skewed) sampling variability
minimal world: a small sample drawn from a known skewed distribution, estimating the median; intervention: compare the bootstrap replicate distribution of the median to the true sampling distribution obtained by repeated simulation from the known generator; null twin: a mutation operator that instead adds independent Gaussian noise directly to the computed median with variance matched to the bootstrap's average spread.

nearest_priors.name: Nonparametric bootstrap (Efron 1979) for variance and standard-error estimation
nearest_priors.explains: Resampling D with replacement to form replicates D*, recomputing theta* on each, using the spread of theta* to estimate the estimator's variance without analytic derivation, approximating the sampling distribution including its skew, and preserving the empirical distribution across replicates
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The transfer to sample-size or design planning is an informal use, not part of the core method. The contrast with a Gaussian-noise null is a validation design, not a mechanism component.

nearest_priors.name: Bagging (bootstrap aggregating, Breiman 1996)
nearest_priors.explains: Keeping and averaging models fitted to bootstrap replicates (the 'what is selected' clause) to reduce variance
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Its goal is to reduce the variance of predictions, not to estimate the variance of an estimator or its sampling distribution

nearest_priors.name: Jackknife / subsampling / parametric bootstrap (Quenouille–Tukey, Politis–Romano)
nearest_priors.explains: Building perturbed datasets from the original data to estimate an estimator's variance and bias without analytic formulas
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The jackknife leaves observations out rather than resampling with replacement, and is known to be inconsistent for the median. The parametric bootstrap draws from a fitted model rather than the empirical distribution.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Almost nothing. The 'offspring / mutation / selection' framing is evolutionary relabelling. One caveat: the claim that the bootstrap median distribution 'matches' the true sampling distribution for small samples is overstated. The bootstrap median is discrete and lumpy at small n and converges only asymptotically (at a slow rate), so it matches only approximately.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Draw a small sample from a known skewed distribution (e.g. lognormal, n=15–50). Compute the bootstrap distribution of the median and the true sampling distribution from Monte Carlo draws of the known generator. Compare the two on variance, skewness and quantiles (e.g. Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance), and do the same for the Gaussian-noise null. Standard bootstrap theory predicts roughly correct variance, approximate skew, and discreteness at small n. Any behaviour beyond this, such as exact finite-sample agreement, would signal something other than the plain bootstrap.

statement: A sequential encoder compresses the history of observations into a low-dimensional code Z_t by minimizing mutual information between the code and the full past while maximizing mutual information between the code and a downstream future target, via an explicit rate-distortion objective (a past-future information bottleneck rather than a reconstruction-based [X] bottleneck). The bottleneck strength beta is annealed over training to trace out a rate-distortion tradeoff curve.
what exists: observation stream X_t; encoder producing code Z_t = f(X_{<=t}); future target Y_{t+k}; variational bound terms estimating I(X;Z) and I(Z;Y)
what changes: Encoder/decoder parameters updated to minimize I_hat(X_{<=t};Z_t) - beta * I_hat(Z_t;Y_{>t}) via a variational estimator (e.g. [X]-style loss); beta is annealed according to a schedule across training.
what persists: Only the future-predictive sufficient [X] of the past are retained in Z across the whole training run; nuisance variation not predictive of Y is progressively discarded as beta/rate constraint tightens.
what is selected: Codes that retain the maximal predictive mutual information per bit of rate are selected by the objective at each beta value.
what can reproduce: The trained encoder can be copied/reused across different downstream tasks sharing the same X-to-Y statistical structure.
what can learn: Which features of the observation history are relevant to predicting the future, as revealed by which information survives increasing compression.
what can transfer: The compressed code Z transfers to downstream readout tasks predicting different aspects of Y_{>t}, as long as those aspects are derivable from the same predictive-sufficient information, without retraining the encoder.
distinguishing observable: As the rate constraint on Z tightens, downstream predictive performance should remain flat across a plateau and then drop sharply at a critical rate (a knee in the rate-distortion curve reflecting the minimal sufficient [X] size); a reconstruction-based [X] bottleneck of matched code dimensionality (null, trained to reconstruct X_t rather than predict Y_{>t}) shows smooth, monotonic degradation in downstream predictive performance as its bottleneck tightens, without the plateau-then-collapse signature.
minimal world: A partially-observable sequential world (e.g. a hidden Markov process) where X_t is a noisy emission of a small latent state that itself evolves and determines a future observable Y_{t+k}; train a predictive-[X] encoder at several beta/rate levels and separately a reconstruction [X] at matched code sizes. Intervention: sweep code dimensionality/rate and measure downstream Y-prediction accuracy for both. Null twin: the reconstruction [X] trained to reconstruct X_t itself, matched in code dimensionality at each point on the sweep, evaluated on the same downstream Y-prediction probe.

statement: A downstream readout unit receives only a fixed small number k of samples from the avalanche activity pattern of an upstream [X]-like layer per event, and must reconstruct or classify the driving input location/magnitude from these k samples. Because avalanche size distributions at [X] span many scales, this bottleneck mechanism tests whether operating the upstream layer near [X] (versus far from it) maximizes the information recoverable through a fixed small channel, providing a task-relevant reason for the system to sit at the critical point.
what exists: an upstream [X]-like relaxation layer with a controllable dissipation/threshold parameter; a downstream readout limited to k random samples of the resulting avalanche activity pattern; known ground-truth drive location/magnitude for each event
what changes: Nothing changes dynamically within a trial; across trials the upstream dissipation parameter is varied experimentally, and for each setting the readout's reconstruction accuracy from k samples is measured.
what persists: The upstream parameter setting persists for a block of trials to gather [X]; the readout's linear/simple decoder weights persist within a block.
what is selected: The upstream operating point (dissipation/threshold value) is 'selected' post hoc as whichever value maximizes readout accuracy under the fixed bottleneck.
what can reproduce: N/A.
what can learn: The downstream readout learns a simple mapping (e.g., linear regression) from k samples to drive location/magnitude, using standard supervised training per upstream setting.
what can transfer: If [X] maximizes bottleneck-information, this maximum should transfer across different choices of k and different readout architectures (still peaking near the same upstream parameter value).
distinguishing observable: Readout accuracy from k samples, plotted against upstream dissipation parameter, peaks at or very near the parameter value that independently produces the broadest (most power-law-like) avalanche size distribution; if the mechanism is not actually connected to [X], readout accuracy would instead peak at a different, unrelated parameter value (e.g., maximum activity or minimum dissipation).
minimal world: [X] lattice as in mechanism 4, dissipation parameter f swept across a range; for each f, drive the system at randomized single-site locations/magnitudes, take k=5 random samples of the resulting activity field, and train a simple linear decoder to predict drive location from those samples; measure held-out decoding accuracy per f value. The null twin uses the same lattice and sampling procedure but replaces the true avalanche field with a shuffled (spatially permuted) version of the same activity values before sampling, preserving the marginal activity-value distribution at each f but destroying the spatial structure that would make sample position informative near [X].

If the accuracy peak stays at the f that maximizes avalanche broadness, that matches the generic criticality/dynamic-range prior. statement: System identification and controller synthesis are modeled as an adjoint pair of [X] L (Ident) and R (Synth) between a plant category and a controller category. Online adaptation implements running estimates of the unit and counit natural transformations, and the adaptation error is defined as the failure of the triangle identities, not raw prediction error. what is selected: parameter sets minimizing joint residual + tracking error, retained across episodes
what can reproduce: an established adjoint pair can be instantiated on a plant instance to bootstrap identification/control jointly
what can learn: the unit and counit maps themselves, learned incrementally from tracking data
what can transfer: rapid re-adaptation to a plant using only an updated unit map, without resynthesizing the controller from scratch
distinguishing observable: convergence speed and asymptotic bias of the adjoint-coupled scheme versus a decoupled certainty-equivalence pipeline (identify then separately synthesize) with matched compute
minimal world: A family of linear plants with unknown scalar gain; identification via recursive least squares, control via pole placement, coupled through the triangle-identity loss. Null twin: identical plants, identical L and R architectures and compute budget, but the triangle-identity coupling term ablated so identification and control adapt independently, matching total gradient steps.

blind_text:
statement: A system maintains a belief (mean and covariance) about a hidden state, propagates it forward through a known dynamics model, then corrects it using a gain-weighted innovation (observation minus prediction) where the gain is analytically set to minimize posterior variance. This produces optimal fusion of prediction and evidence while storing only a compressed sufficient [X], not the full observation history.
what exists: hidden state x_t; estimate x̂_t; covariance P_t; observation y_t = C x_t + noise; process noise Q; observation noise R
what changes: predict x̂⁻=A x̂, P⁻=A P A' + Q; gain K = P⁻C'(C P⁻ C' + R)^-1; update x̂ = x̂⁻ + K(y - C x̂⁻); P = (I-[X]) P⁻
what persists: the covariance P persists as a compressed summary of accumulated observation informativeness
what is selected: among all candidate gains, the [X] gain is selected as the minimizer of estimation-error covariance trace
what can reproduce: the recursive structure applies unchanged to any linear-Gaussian system given (A,C,Q,R), reproducible by reinitializing P
what can learn: Q and R can be estimated online from innovation [X], learning the model of uncertainty itself
what can transfer: a converged estimate/covariance can seed estimation in a related but non-identical system
distinguishing observable: estimation-error variance matches the exact Riccati recursion optimum and adapts when noise regime shifts; a fixed-gain low-pass filter with matched average gain shows systematically higher variance when the regime shifts
minimal world: A random-walk hidden variable observed through noisy sensor with a noise level that changes partway through the trial. Intervention A: full [X] recursion. Null twin B: fixed constant-gain low-pass filter tuned for average performance across the whole trial. Measure error variance before/after the noise-regime shift: A tracks the Riccati-optimal bound in both regimes; B is markedly worse after the shift despite matched average gain.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman filter (Kalman 1960; Kalman–Bucy), with [X] = sufficient statistic / Kalman / KC
nearest_priors.field: Estimation and control theory, signal processing
nearest_priors.explains: Everything in the core description. The Gaussian belief (x̂, P) is carried forward by the predict step x̂⁻ = A x̂ and P⁻ = A P A' + Q. The gain K = P⁻C'(C P⁻ C' + R)^-1 is the one that minimises trace(P). The update is the innovation-weighted correction, with P = (I - KC) P⁻. The mean and covariance are a sufficient statistic for the whole observation history under linear-Gaussian assumptions. The error covariance follows the Riccati recursion. The same recursion applies to any (A, C, Q, R).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Adapting to a noise-regime shift whose new level is not given to the filter. A standard Kalman filter with a fixed, misspecified R does not re-tune itself; it adapts only if the new R is supplied.

nearest_priors.name: Adaptive Kalman filter via innovation-based noise estimation (Mehra 1970/1972; covariance matching; Myers–Tapley)
nearest_priors.explains: The 'what can learn' clause: estimating Q and R online from innovation statistics, with [X] = statistics or sequence. It also explains why variance stays near the Riccati optimum after an unannounced change in sensor noise.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing beyond the Kalman core. It only adds the online estimation of the noise model; the recursion itself is the Kalman filter's.

nearest_priors.name: Steady-state Kalman / Wiener filter, alpha(-beta) filter, exponential smoothing
nearest_priors.explains: The null twin B, a fixed-gain low-pass filter. The steady-state Kalman filter is exactly the constant-gain limit of the Riccati recursion, and exponential smoothing is optimal only for a stationary random walk plus noise. This is why B loses when the regime shifts.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The time-varying covariance and gain, and optimality under nonstationary noise.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing. The only point needing a second prior is adaptation to a noise shift the filter is not told about, which requires innovation-based estimation of R (adaptive Kalman filtering). The 'transfer' clause is ordinary warm-start initialisation of the prior (x̂0, P0).
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run three filters on the random-walk-plus-sensor world where R shifts mid-trial without announcement: (a) a Kalman filter holding the pre-shift R; (b) a Kalman filter told the new R at the shift; (c) the described mechanism. If (c) matches (b) and beats (a) after a transient consistent with innovation-covariance estimation, it is an adaptive Kalman filter. If (c) matches (a), it is the plain Kalman filter, and the claimed adaptation requires the new R to be supplied.

statement: Each accepted hypothesis is stored with its accepting run (the certificate the model checker produced), and periodically the certificate is cheaply re-checked against fresh observations; on failure, only incremental re-verification of the affected certificate segment is triggered rather than full re-abduction, giving justification a decay-and-local-repair dynamic distinct from either permanent belief (foundationalism without decay) or constant full re-derivation.

what changes: certificate validity flag flips on decay-triggered mismatch; only the mismatched segment of the run is recomputed/repaired.
what persists: unaffected certificate segments across the repair event.
what is selected: hypotheses whose certificates require the fewest repairs over time (cheap-to-maintain justification).
what can reproduce: repaired certificates spawn updated hypothesis variants carrying forward unaffected segments.
what can learn: the system learns which certificate segments are volatile (environment-drift-prone) vs stable.
what can transfer: stable certificate segments transfer directly to structurally related hypotheses without re-verification.
distinguishing observable: repair time scales with the size of the drifted segment, not with total hypothesis size — a sublinear repair-cost signature absent in a full-reverification control matched for final correctness.
minimal world: A hypothesis about a periodic environment holds a 20-step accepting run; at step 500 one transition rule silently drifts. Intervention: drift a single local rule. Null twin: on any certificate failure, discard and fully re-run abduction+[X] from scratch (matched for eventual correctness); the twin's repair cost is constant/large regardless of drift locality, unlike the incremental mechanism's localized cheap repair.

statement: When the model checker returns a spurious counterexample (one that exists in an abstracted hypothesis but not the concrete environment), a state-splitting operator partitions the offending abstract state into refined substates, directly mutating hypothesis structure in response to a verification-derived signal rather than random or fitness-blind mutation.

what persists: the refinement history (which splits occurred and why), preventing re-splitting on the same distinction.
what is selected: refinements that eliminate the spurious counterexample without reintroducing previously eliminated ones.
what can reproduce: refined automata become parents for further abstraction/refinement cycles.
what can learn: the operator learns a reusable feature (the distinguishing predicate) that separated s1 from s2, applicable to future abstractions.
what can transfer: distinguishing predicates transfer to hypotheses sharing the same underlying variable.
distinguishing observable: hypothesis-size growth is driven exclusively by genuine counterexample elimination, with zero splits triggered by non-counterexample-derived signals, distinguishing it from random state-splitting mutation matched for final hypothesis size.
minimal world: An abstracted traffic-light controller hypothesis (3 abstract states) is checked against a concrete 12-state environment for a safety spec. Intervention: introduce a concrete edge case collapsed by the abstraction. Null twin: a random mutation operator that splits a randomly chosen state each time a check fails, matched for final automaton size; the twin requires many more cycles to eliminate the specific spurious counterexample and sometimes splits irrelevant states.

statement: Training jointly minimizes data-fit loss and an explicit description-length / complexity cost on the model's parameters, with the complexity weight increased over training, so the model is pressured toward the simplest representation still consistent with the data (an explicit minimum-description-length pressure rather than fit-only optimization). what exists: model parameters theta; data-fit loss D(theta); explicit complexity/code-length cost C(theta) (e.g. bits needed to specify theta at given precision); schedule lambda(t) increasing over training
what changes: theta <- theta - eta * grad(D(theta) + lambda(t) * C(theta)); lambda(t) increases according to a fixed schedule, progressively pruning/quantizing less-useful parameters.
what persists: The minimal sufficient parameter subset that survives increasing lambda persists as the compressed model.
what is selected: Parameter configurations with the best fit-per-bit ratio at each lambda level are retained; redundant/low-utility parameters are pruned.
what can reproduce: Compressed sub-modules can be extracted and reused/duplicated as building blocks in a larger composed model.
what can learn: Increasingly compressed, generalization-favoring representations as compression pressure ramps up.
what can transfer: A compressed representation should transfer to a low-data task better than an uncompressed model matched in training-loss, because it has discarded overfit-specific parameters.
distinguishing observable: As lambda increases, held-out generalization should improve (or degrade more slowly) up to a critical compression level, then collapse sharply past a description-length threshold — a non-monotonic/threshold generalization-vs-compression curve absent in a fit-only model (lambda=0 fixed) matched in final training loss, which shows a flat or monotonically worsening generalization curve as capacity is externally reduced without the joint fit/complexity optimization.
minimal world: A small regression task with a true low-complexity generator plus noise; train models under a schedule of increasing lambda vs a fixed lambda=0 control matched at each checkpoint for training loss via early stopping. Intervention: sweep lambda schedules and measure held-out loss and effective description length (e.g. number of non-negligible weights) at each checkpoint. Null twin: an unregularized model trained to the same training loss trajectory via early stopping alone (no explicit complexity term), matched in training-loss curve but with no code-length pressure, which should show no corresponding non-monotonic generalization-vs-complexity relationship.
