blind_text:
statement: A slow abiotic state variable (nutrient/detritus pool) integrates the history of fast species dynamics and thereby determines which successional trajectory is realized from a disturbance; identical instantaneous abundance vectors can yield different futures depending on this slow variable's value, producing genuine hysteresis.
what exists: fast species abundances x_i; slow nutrient/detritus pool D; timescale-separation parameter epsilon
what changes: x_{t+1}=g(x,D); D_{t+1}=D_t+epsilon*(mortality inputs - decay*D_t), with D updating far slower than x.
what persists: D persists across disturbance events even when x is reset near zero.
what is selected: none directly in this mechanism.
what can reproduce: species reproduce; D only accumulates/decays.
what can learn: the ecosystem trajectory encodes integrated disturbance history in D, biasing future successional pathway.
what can transfer: D-encoded legacy can transfer across patches via diffusion, testable by translocating soil/D values.
distinguishing observable: identical resets of x(0) but different D(0) histories should yield divergent long-run community attractors correlated with D(0); a memoryless system predicts convergence regardless of D(0).
minimal world: One patch, 3 species, one nutrient pool D; disturbance resets x to near-zero at two times with different pre-existing D. Null twin: replace slow D accumulation with instantaneous equilibration D=D_eq(x(t)) at every step (matched in steady-state mean/variance) — successional outcome should be history-independent in the null.

nearest_priors.name: Slow-fast (singularly perturbed) systems with a slow variable driving alternative stable states and hysteresis (Rinaldi & Scheffer 2000; Ludwig-Jones-Holling spruce budworm; Scheffer shallow-lake phosphorus)
nearest_priors.field: Theoretical ecology / dynamical systems (fast-slow systems, catastrophe/regime-shift theory)
nearest_priors.explains: The full structure: fast species dynamics x_{t+1}=g(x,D) and a slow pool D relaxing at rate epsilon. D sets which fast attractor basin is realized, so identical x(0) with different D(0) diverge. Hysteresis follows from D integrating the history of x. The quasi-steady-state null (D=D_eq(x)) is the standard adiabatic-elimination comparison.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. Cross-patch diffusion of D and the soil-translocation test are applied extensions of this framework rather than part of it.

nearest_priors.name: Ecological memory / legacy effects and plant-soil feedback (Peterson 2002; Bever; Johnstone et al. 2016)
nearest_priors.explains: Disturbance legacies carried in an abiotic pool (soil, detritus, nutrients) bias the successional pathway after x is reset. Soil translocation is a standard test. It also covers legacy transfer between patches.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It is usually stated verbally or empirically. It does not supply the explicit epsilon timescale separation or the matched-null construction.

nearest_priors.name: Priority effects / historical contingency with a resource-mediated state (Tilman resource competition; Fukami community assembly)
nearest_priors.explains: Which species dominates depends on the resource level at the time of establishment. This gives divergent community outcomes from the same starting abundances.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It typically treats the resource as fast or externally supplied. It lacks the slow integrating variable that makes history carry across disturbances.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is unexplained. One caveat: the claim of 'long-run' divergent attractors requires the fast-slow coupled system itself to be multistable. If D has a unique global equilibrium, the effect is a long transient that eventually converges, not true hysteresis. The description does not specify which case holds.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Clamp D experimentally (for example with a nutrient-buffered chemostat or continual soil amendment) at a range of fixed values after identical resets of x, then release the clamp. Genuine slow-variable bistability shows two separate branches over a range of D that persist indefinitely after release. A pure slow-transient legacy shows trajectories converging on a timescale of about 1/epsilon. Varying epsilon while holding steady-state D fixed should rescale the duration of divergence exactly as fast-slow theory predicts.

what can transfer: the core interaction pattern transfers across domains that share no mode-values but share the same underlying interaction structure.

blind_text:
statement: Controller parameters are updated using a gradient computed from a positive-definite Lyapunov function of tracking error and parameter error, so parameters change only in directions that provably decrease a stored energy-like quantity. This drives an unknown plant toward matching a specified reference model's behavior without explicit plant identification; the law is derived from stability requirements, not searched for by trial and error.
what exists: unknown plant parameters theta*; estimate theta_hat; tracking error e = plant output - reference model output; adaptation-rate matrix Gamma
what changes: theta_hat_dot = -Gamma * regressor * e, derived so the Lyapunov function's time-derivative is negative semi-definite
what persists: theta_hat persists, integrating the history of correlated error-times-regressor products
what is selected: only parameter trajectories consistent with Lyapunov-decrease are dynamically realized; all others are excluded
what can reproduce: the same adaptation law structure attaches to any plant of matching parametric form
what can learn: theta_hat converges to theta* under persistent excitation, i.e. the true plant parameters are learned online
what can transfer: a converged theta_hat can seed adaptation for a similar plant, speeding future convergence
distinguishing observable: tracking error decays toward zero over time under persistent excitation, unlike a fixed non-adaptive controller with matched initial gains whose error remains proportional to the plant-reference mismatch indefinitely
minimal world: unknown-gain scalar plant x_dot = a*x + b*u versus reference model x_dot_m = -lambda*x_m + r, with a,b varied across trials. Intervention A: Lyapunov-based [X]. Null twin B: fixed controller pre-tuned to the average expected a,b with identical initial transient. Vary a,b: A's error shrinks toward zero after transient in every trial; B's error remains bounded away from zero proportional to the mismatch.

nearest_priors.name: Lyapunov-based Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC; Parks 1966, Narendra, Landau), with Barbalat-lemma error convergence and parameter convergence under persistent excitation
nearest_priors.explains: The whole mechanism. The Lyapunov function V = e^2/2 + (theta_tilde^T Gamma^-1 theta_tilde)/2 is standard. So is the update law theta_hat_dot = -Gamma*phi*e (sign-adjusted by sgn(b)), chosen so that V_dot = -lambda*e^2 <= 0. MRAC also gives tracking-error convergence to zero, and parameter convergence to theta* under persistent excitation. The scalar plant against a first-order reference model is the textbook example. The fixed-gain null twin shows the familiar steady-state mismatch error.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. 'Transfer' is only warm-starting theta_hat from a previous run. The description ties error decay to persistent excitation, but standard MRAC gives e -> 0 even without PE; only parameter convergence needs PE.

nearest_priors.name: MIT rule (gradient-based MRAS, Whitaker 1958)
nearest_priors.explains: It uses the same structure: model-reference adaptation, a gradient update of the form parameter_dot proportional to -error*sensitivity, and online adjustment without explicit plant identification.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Its update comes from the gradient of the squared error, not from a Lyapunov stability argument. So it gives no guaranteed stability, and it can go unstable at high adaptation gain or high reference amplitude.

nearest_priors.name: Indirect adaptive control / self-tuning regulator using recursive least-squares or gradient identification (certainty equivalence)
nearest_priors.explains: It also estimates parameters online, converges to the true parameters under persistent excitation, and adapts the controller to an unknown plant.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It identifies the plant explicitly and then redesigns the controller. The described mechanism is direct: it adjusts controller parameters from tracking error, with the law derived from a Lyapunov function.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The 'transfer' claim (seeding from a converged estimate) is ordinary warm-starting. The mechanism overstates PE as a requirement for tracking-error convergence, which holds via Barbalat's lemma without PE.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the scalar plant with a high adaptation gain Gamma and a large-amplitude reference signal. Also compare a non-exciting constant reference with a sinusoidal reference. Lyapunov MRAC stays stable for every Gamma > 0 and drives e -> 0 in both cases; parameters converge only under the sinusoid. An MIT-rule implementation can go unstable at high gain. If the described mechanism showed any behaviour beyond this Lyapunov-MRAC signature, it would differ from MRAC.

what changes: On entering a overlap, [X]-check the gluing formula; on [X] extend the colimit; on [X] use the core to identify and regenerate the faulty patch, then retry.

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Continuous tracking dynamics. The adaptive-control loop. Duplication of patches for state-space symmetry. The observable of tracking-error localization.

parsed.unexplained_residual: No listed prior on its own couples an SMT/unsat-core blame loop over gluing constraints with an online adaptive reference model. parsed.discriminating_intervention: Perturb the dynamics of one interval so that it stays locally consistent with each neighbour on separate overlaps but is globally inconsistent (a cyclic/cocycle obstruction), or corrupt two patches at once. The described mechanism should return a minimal core pointing at specific patches, regenerate only those, and keep the error confined to the flagged seams. Also measure whether regeneration is triggered by a gluing failure rather than by the residual magnitude.

statement: A small fixed set of 'axiom states' is model-checked once against raw sensor primitives and never revisited; every higher hypothesis must route its justification through a provable reduction chain to this axiom set, exactly mirroring foundationalism but only enforceable because [X] can certify the reduction chain exhaustively. Hypotheses that cannot be reduced are rejected regardless of explanatory fit.
what exists: axiom-state set A (fixed, size k); candidate hypotheses H; reduction proof objects (sequences of verified implications); raw sensor primitive stream
what changes: candidate H's status flips from unjustified to justified when a reduction proof from H to A passes [X]; A itself never changes.
what persists: A and all certified reduction proofs.
what is selected: hypotheses possessing a complete, checkable reduction chain to A.
what can reproduce: justified hypotheses can be recombined into compound hypotheses that inherit justification if the compound reduction chain still checks.
what can learn: the agent learns which hypothesis templates tend to admit short reduction proofs (proof-search heuristics).
what can transfer: the axiom set A and its certified proofs transfer unchanged to domains sharing the same primitive alphabet.
distinguishing observable: justification rate collapses sharply as hypothesis distance-to-axiom (graph distance in the reduction lattice) increases, producing a step-function acceptance curve absent in a coherentist control where distance to axioms is irrelevant.
minimal world: A grid world where 8 base percepts (wall/no-wall in 4 directions at 2 resolutions) are the axiom set A, pre-verified against ground truth. Intervention: introduce hypotheses about a hidden 'trap tile' that require increasingly long reduction chains to A. Null twin: replace the reduction-chain requirement with a raw similarity-to-A score computed without [X] (matching acceptance rate on average) — the twin fails to show the sharp distance-dependent cliff because it lacks exhaustive chain verification.

nearest_priors.name: Axiomatic deductive system with an LCF-style trusted proof-checking kernel (Hilbert/Frege foundationalism mechanised; proof-carrying justification)
nearest_priors.field: Mathematical logic / interactive theorem proving (LCF, HOL, Coq, Metamath)
nearest_priors.explains: A fixed axiom set that is never revised. Theorems (hypotheses) count as justified only if a checkable derivation reaches the axioms. The checker [X] is the trusted kernel. Certified proofs persist and are reusable. Compound statements inherit justification when the combined derivation checks (conjunction introduction, lemma composition). Underivable statements are rejected whatever their explanatory appeal. Axioms and proofs transfer to any domain with the same signature (primitive alphabet).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Grounding of the axioms by one-time model checking against sensor data. Learning of search heuristics. The specific step-function acceptance curve, which comes from resource-bounded search rather than from the logic itself.

nearest_priors.name: Forward/backward chaining over ground facts in logic programming (Prolog SLD resolution, Datalog) with depth-bounded search
nearest_priors.explains: Ground percept facts act as the base (EDB). Hypotheses are goals proved by chaining rules back to those facts. Unprovable goals fail (negation as failure / rejection). With a depth or resource bound, acceptance falls off sharply with derivation length, giving the distance-dependent cliff. The null twin, a similarity score with no derivation, lacks that cliff.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Explicit persistent proof objects and exhaustive certification. The learned template heuristics.

nearest_priors.field: Machine learning for automated theorem proving
nearest_priors.explains: The agent learns which hypothesis templates admit short proofs. This improves search without changing what counts as justified, because the checker remains the arbiter.

One-time model checking of the axioms against sensor primitives is ordinary sensor-grounded fact assertion.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Keep the checker fixed but remove the resource bound (unbounded proof search, or supply the proofs as oracles). If the step-function cliff disappears and acceptance simply equals derivability, the behaviour is fully explained by a depth-bounded axiomatic prover. Also inject a derivable but long-chain hypothesis together with a pre-supplied proof. If it is accepted, the cliff is a search-cost artifact, not an intrinsic property of foundationalist justification.

statement: A fixed-capacity buffer of K slots stores compressed encodings, with a learned gate deciding what to write (overwriting the least task-relevant slot) and what to read (retrieving the best-matching slot) based on a relevance signal rather than recency. This lets task-relevant information persist across arbitrarily long irrelevant intervals within a bounded-capacity system.
what exists: K memory slots; relevance-scoring gate network; current input encoding; read/write pointers
what changes: at each timestep, gate scores relevance of current input vs. existing slots; if above threshold, writes by overwriting the lowest-relevance slot; read retrieves nearest-matching slot content for downstream use
what persists: slot contents persist unchanged until judged less relevant than an incoming candidate
what is selected: high-relevance information is retained; low-relevance content is preferentially overwritten
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: the gating policy (what counts as relevant) is learned end-to-end from task reward/loss
what can transfer: retained content bridges long temporal gaps within a trial; the learned gating policy transfers to delay lengths
distinguishing observable: accuracy on a delayed-recall task as delay length and number of distractors increase beyond K: gated buffer maintains accuracy for relevant items while a matched-capacity [X] buffer (overwrite by recency only) degrades once distractors exceed K and evict the relevant cue
minimal world: Sequence task: present a cue, then a variable number of distractors, then query the cue after a variable delay; only the cue is task-relevant. Intervention: increase distractor count beyond buffer capacity K. Null twin: identical buffer size K with [X] overwrite (no relevance gating), matched capacity and update rule — expected to lose the cue once distractors exceed K, unlike the gated version.

nearest_priors.explains: Fixed number of K slots, a learned gate that decides whether to write, overwriting the least-useful slot, content-addressed (nearest-match) read, gating policy learned from task reward or loss (PBWM uses reinforcement learning), and persistence of a cue across distractors. blind_text:
statement: The joint distribution over k discrete variables is defined by a [X]-decomposed natural-parameter tensor, P(x) ∝ exp(Σ_r λ_r Π_i φ_r^{(i)}(x_i)), rather than a raw log-linear tensor or a moment-constrained MaxEnt model. This forces every higher-order interaction visible in the log-probability to be built additively from R independent rank-1 causes, a joint restriction on entropy structure and interaction order that neither pure tensor factoring nor pure moment-based MaxEnt imposes alone.
what exists: k [X] variables with small alphabets; [X] factor vectors φ_r^{(i)} per rank component and mode; scalar weights λ_r; an explicit partition function Z computed by brute-force summation.
what changes: Factors and weights are updated by gradient ascent on log-likelihood (or [X] to a target with known marginals), rank R held fixed within a run.
what persists: Rank R and the mode-to-variable assignment persist across optimization; the additive rank-1 interaction structure persists.
what is selected: Components r whose gradient most reduces [X] are reinforced; negligible-λ_r components are effectively pruned.
what can reproduce: A converged rank-1 component can be duplicated and perturbed as a template for a candidate component when growing rank.
what can learn: The factor set learns to match arbitrary target low-order marginals, effectively learning which interaction orders are representable at given R.
what can transfer: A factor fit for one variable's role can seed the same variable's factor in a different tensor sharing that alphabet.
distinguishing observable: The empirical third-order log-linear interaction coefficient is pinned to a low-dimensional algebraic function of the rank-1 factors (Kruskal-rank bound) even when all pairwise marginals are matched exactly, whereas a full-rank moment-based MaxEnt model matching the same pairwise marginals attains the generic (unconstrained) value for that coefficient.
minimal world: Three binary variables (8-cell joint). Fit (a) the [X]-rank-1 natural-parameter model and (b) a null twin that is the standard full moment-based MaxEnt solution to the same six pairwise marginals (intervention: enforce exact marginal matching in both). Measure the emergent third-order coefficient in each; the [X] model's value is analytically constrained by its factors while the null twin's is the generic MaxEnt value, and the gap between them is the mechanism's signature.

nearest_priors.name: CP/PARAFAC-factored log-linear model: a low-rank natural-parameter tensor in an exponential family (as in factored higher-order Boltzmann machines and low-rank tensor MRFs)
nearest_priors.field: statistical machine learning / probabilistic graphical models
nearest_priors.explains: Covers the form P(x) ∝ exp(Σ_r λ_r Π_i φ_r^(i)(x_i)) exactly. With [X]=CP, it explains the exact partition function over small alphabets, gradient ascent on log-likelihood at fixed rank, and pruning of negligible λ_r. It also explains why all interaction orders are tied to shared rank-1 factors, which is Kruskal-rank structure in the log-probability.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Rank growth by duplicating and perturbing a converged component is a heuristic add-on, not part of the canonical model. So is transferring factors across tensors that share an alphabet.

nearest_priors.name: Maximum-entropy / log-linear models with pairwise sufficient statistics (Ising or Potts model fit by iterative proportional fitting or moment matching)
nearest_priors.explains: This is the null twin: the MaxEnt solution that matches all pairwise marginals, with its three-way coefficient set by construction. It also explains the log-linear parameterization and fitting a model to target marginals.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It imposes no low-rank tensor constraint, so it cannot account for the algebraically pinned third-order coefficient.

nearest_priors.name: Exponential-family PCA / low-rank tensor factorization of natural parameters (Collins-Dasgupta-Schapire), together with Legendre decomposition (Sugiyama et al.)
nearest_priors.explains: Covers low-rank structure placed on natural parameters rather than on raw data. It also covers fitting by likelihood or KL projection and the information-geometric reading of which interaction orders a restricted model can represent.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It is usually applied to observation matrices rather than to one joint distribution over k variables. It also lacks the component-template growth and selection language.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the evolutionary-style extras remain unexplained: duplicating and perturbing components to grow rank, and seeding a variable's factor from another tensor. Both are routine heuristics (greedy rank growth and warm starts). The minimal world is also internally strained. A single rank-1 component over three binary variables has roughly 4 free parameters, but exactly matching six pairwise 2x2 marginals needs 6 constraints. So 'enforce exact marginal matching' generally cannot be achieved at R=1 and requires a larger R. In a single rank-1 term, the main, pairwise and triple effects are all products of the same factors, and that coupling is the known signature.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: On three binary variables, sweep R from 1 to 4 and fit each model to the same targets. Compare the three-way interaction coefficient to the pairwise-MaxEnt value (which has zero three-way term) and to the coefficient from a CP-factored Boltzmann machine at the same rank. If the described mechanism is just a CP-factored log-linear model, its coefficients will match the factored model's at every R. The two will also converge once R reaches full CP rank (at most 4 for 2x2x2), and that convergence point is where the gap to MaxEnt should close. Any gap to MaxEnt that persists above full rank would indicate something beyond the known model.

blind_text:
statement: A signal's represented content is fixed not by its current statistical correlation with the world but by the environmental condition that explains why the sender-receiver disposition was selectively retained over the population's history. Two signals with identical present-day [X] can carry different content if their selective histories differ, and a signal can misfire (be tokened falsely) while still retaining its historically fixed content.
what exists: population of sender-receiver agent pairs; internal signal token s; environment state X that varies over time; fitness from receiver's correct action conditional on X; a genealogical record of past selection events
what changes: Population composition updates via selection proportional to fitness; each lineage carries a record of which X the signal covaried with during the selection episodes that fixed its current disposition.
what persists: The historically fixed content assignment X* persists even after the environment shifts and the signal begins misfiring relative to current [X].
what is selected: Sender-receiver pairs whose signal usage produced correct receiver action under X are differentially retained; content is a residue of this selection history.
what can reproduce: Agent pairs reproduce proportional to fitness, passing down signal dispositions with mutation.
what can learn: Within-lifetime associative recalibration of signal-to-action mapping can occur atop the slower, selection-fixed content.
what can transfer: Signal dispositions transfer across generations (heredity) and can be horizontally borrowed by other lineages via mimicry.
distinguishing observable: After an environmental perturbation decouples the old cue from the target while a correlate arises, measure whether misfire errors are diagnosable relative to the historical cue (teleosemantic prediction) versus whether behavior instantly re-correlates with the cue (pure-correlational null).
minimal world: Agents in a two-state (predator/no-predator) environment evolve an alarm signal over many generations under a stable cue-to-danger mapping. Intervention: perturb the environment so the original cue decouples from actual danger while a cue becomes the true correlate. Null twin: a population whose signal-action mapping is recomputed each generation purely from current correlation [X] (no selective-history dependence), which re-aligns to the cue immediately, unlike the selection-history-bound population which shows persistent, diagnosable misfiring tied to the old cue.

nearest_priors.name: Teleosemantics (Millikan's biosemantics / Dretske's indicator-function account of misrepresentation)
nearest_priors.field: philosophy of mind / philosophy of biology
nearest_priors.explains: Content fixed by the selectional history (proper function / Normal conditions) rather than current correlation. Misrepresentation as tokening under abnormal conditions. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not by itself give the population-dynamic simulation machinery (replicator update, mutation, horizontal mimicry) or the within-lifetime learning layer.

nearest_priors.field: evolutionary game theory / philosophy of language
nearest_priors.explains: Population of sender-receiver pairs, a two-state environment and fitness-proportional selection with mutation. Emergent alarm-call conventions. nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Skyrms assigns content by current mutual information, not history, so on its own it gives the null rather than teleosemantic content attribution.

nearest_priors.name: Evolutionary mismatch / evolutionary trap and Baldwin-effect layering (genetic assimilation plus individual learning)
nearest_priors.explains: Maladaptive persistence of cue-response after an environmental decoupling of cue and target, such as ecological traps. Slow selection-fixed dispositions overlaid with fast within-lifetime associative recalibration. Batesian-mimicry-style horizontal borrowing of signals.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little. The operationalization of 'diagnosable misfire' as a measurable observable in simulation is a methodological addition, not a new mechanism. The null twin is simply a correlational-content (Skyrms/Dretske-informational) baseline. Minor incoherence: blanks make the post-perturbation 'a cue becomes the true correlate' ambiguous, but it is recoverable.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run Lewis signaling games with replicator dynamics and perform the cue-danger decoupling. Then compare two content-attribution rules applied to the same trajectories: history-indexed (etiological) versus current mutual information. If misfire patterns are fully predicted by replicator lag alone, with no difference in behavior, the 'mechanism' reduces to standard replicator dynamics plus a teleosemantic labeling convention. A genuine behavioral difference would require lineages with identical current dispositions but different histories behaving differently under a further perturbation, which standard models predict they will not.

blind_text:
statement: A ledger records every (transform, expected relation, observed violation magnitude) tuple encountered during operation, and this ledger is used to nonparametrically estimate process/measurement noise covariances (Q, R) by mapping violation-frequency [X] to variance estimates, replacing a hand-supplied noise model with a relation-history-derived one.
what exists: a growing ledger L={(T_k, v_k, t_k)}, running histograms of violation magnitude per transform type, current Q,R estimates.
what changes: Q and R are recomputed periodically as a function of ledger [X] (e.g., variance of violation magnitudes for relations diagnostic of process vs. measurement noise).
what persists: the ledger accumulates indefinitely (with optional decay), providing a persistent memory trace distinct from the filter's instantaneous state.
what is selected: no explicit selection among alternatives; but noise estimates that better predict future violation [X] persist longer before being revised.
what can reproduce: none.
what can learn: the noise covariance matrices Q,R, learned purely from relation-violation history rather than from labeled ground-truth state error.
what can transfer: a ledger built in one noise regime should let the filter adapt Q,R quickly (few entries needed) when deployed in a related but non-identical regime, versus a filter with no ledger needing full re-tuning.

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Why the message should be a tensor factor. The claimed exact threshold at R* set by the tensor rank of the joint occupancy.

nearest_priors.name: Variational mean-field / structured mean-field and mixture-of-products (low nonnegative rank) approximation in graphical models; distributed / consensus tensor factorization
nearest_priors.explains: A joint distribution over agents' states is approximated by a sum of R product distributions. Rank 1 is naive mean field. Accuracy improves with R and is exact at the nonnegative rank. Each factor can be updated locally from local statistics, and a shared summary can be recomputed across nodes.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The control objective and the cost-reduction selection of updates. The link to maxent policy optimality.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little that is new. The claim that low rank makes the maxent joint policy 'exactly factorizable into local terms' is overstated. A rank-R CP structure gives a sum of R products, not a product. Each agent therefore needs the component weights, i.e. the broadcast b, to recover its conditional, and this is just a mixture-of-products conditional. The paired claim that a mean or histogram summary shows a persistent gap is a standard sufficiency argument: the factor loadings are sufficient statistics for the mixture component, while marginal histograms are not.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Build a joint cost whose optimal occupancy has low CP rank but high TT or Tucker rank, and a second cost with the reverse. If the gap closes exactly at the CP rank R*, the specific factor-broadcast claim is supported. If it tracks another rank notion, or whether R equals the number of mixture components of a latent coordination variable, the mechanism reduces to a latent-variable (mixture-of-products) decentralized policy. As a further test, give the null baseline a learned, not hand-crafted, R-dimensional message at the same bit budget. If it also closes the gap at R*, the factor derivation adds nothing beyond learned communication.

Top-down predictions are compared against bottom-up signals at each level, and only the residual (surprise) drives further updating. Over time this yields internal states that anticipate incoming data rather than merely reacting to it.

what persists: The learned generative mapping g and precision-weighting scheme persist across trials and occlusions.
what is selected: Internal hypotheses/states that minimize long-run weighted prediction error are retained over alternative hypotheses that produce more surprise.
what can reproduce: Generative model parameters can be copied wholesale into agent instances.

what can transfer: The learned hierarchical generative model transfers to environments sharing the same generative [X] but different surface appearance.

minimal world: A 1D grid world with a periodically moving dot observed by a two-layer predictor (position layer, velocity/period layer). Intervention: occlude the dot for several steps and check whether the internal position estimate keeps evolving along the learned periodic trajectory. Null twin: a feedforward filter with matched parameter count and identical steady-state output [X] but no top-down generative loop; during occlusion its estimate simply freezes/decays instead of continuing the predicted trajectory.

blind_text:
statement: Distinctness between two inputs is represented not by a static encoded value but by the rate at which two trajectories started from those inputs diverge under the shared dynamical law—the finite-time Lyapunov exponent between them. Inputs that are functionally similar produce slowly diverging (or converging) trajectory pairs; inputs that are functionally different produce rapidly diverging pairs, making divergence rate itself the readable representation.
what exists: shared dynamical map f; two states x_A, x_B initialized from inputs A and B; separation distance d_t = |x_A,t - x_B,t|
what changes: x_A,t+1 = f(x_A,t), x_B,t+1 = f(x_B,t); d_t tracked and log(d_t/d_0)/t computed as the readout
what persists: the map f is fixed across all input pairs being compared
what is selected: no selection; this is a pure readout mechanism
what can reproduce: not applicable directly
what can learn: a downstream classifier can learn a threshold on divergence rate to categorize input-pair similarity
what can transfer: the divergence-rate readout transfers to any input pair embeddable into the same state space
distinguishing observable: correlate finite-time Lyapunov exponent with ground-truth input similarity across many pairs; a true divergence-based representation shows monotonic relationship even when final state positions x_A,T and x_B,T are similar, distinguishing it from a simple 'final distance' representation that would fail when trajectories cross paths
minimal world: A chaotic map (e.g., tent map or logistic map at r=4) fed pairs of inputs with known similarity labels; measure divergence rate over a fixed horizon. Intervention: construct input pairs where final-state distance is small but divergence rate is large (trajectories that diverge then happen to re-converge) and test whether divergence-rate-based classification outperforms final-distance-based classification on the similarity labels. Null twin: replace the chaotic map with a contracting (non-chaotic) map matched in output range, where divergence rate is uninformative because all pairs converge regardless of input similarity.

nearest_priors.name: Finite-time Lyapunov exponent between two trajectories (Benettin-style twin-trajectory divergence estimation, sensitive dependence on initial conditions)
nearest_priors.explains: All of the machinery: a fixed map f, two copies iterated in parallel, separation d_t, and the readout log(d_t/d_0)/t. Using a chaotic map such as the tent map or the logistic map at r=4 is the textbook setting. The null twin of a contracting map with negative exponents is also standard.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not treat the exponent as a learned similarity code for inputs. It also highlights a flaw in the description. As defined, log(d_T/d_0)/T depends only on the final distance and d_0, so it cannot beat final distance when trajectories re-converge unless a running or maximal divergence is used instead. In a uniformly chaotic map, the finite-separation FTLE is largest for the most similar inputs (small d_0, long growth before saturation), which inverts the claimed monotonic relationship.

nearest_priors.name: Separation property of liquid state machines / echo state networks (reservoir computing at the edge of chaos)
nearest_priors.explains: A fixed shared dynamical system maps inputs into trajectories. Distinctness of inputs shows up as separation of reservoir trajectories, and a trained downstream linear readout or threshold classifies them. Transfer to any input embeddable into the reservoir state space is also covered. Kernel-quality and separation measures, including Lyapunov-based ones, are used to tune reservoirs.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Reservoirs usually read out states or state distances, not a divergence-rate statistic. Reservoir theory also favours near-critical rather than fully chaotic dynamics.

nearest_priors.name: FTLE fields / Lagrangian coherent structures
nearest_priors.explains: Pairs of initial conditions are labelled by how fast their trajectories separate over a finite horizon. FTLE ridges partition initial conditions into dynamically distinct classes. This matches 'divergence rate as the readable representation of functional distinctness.'
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not include pairwise input-similarity labels or a learned classifier threshold.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the framing is new: calling pairwise FTLE a 'representation' of input similarity with a learned threshold. The claimed advantage over final distance under re-convergence does not follow from the stated readout, which is a function of d_T and d_0 only. It would require a path-dependent statistic such as max_t log(d_t/d_0)/t or a time-averaged log-growth rate.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Use the logistic map at r=4 with input pairs of known similarity. Compute three readouts: (a) the endpoint FTLE log(d_T/d_0)/T as stated, (b) final distance d_T, and (c) the maximal or time-averaged running log-divergence. Test on pairs constructed to diverge and then re-converge. If (a) and (b) give identical rank orderings given d_0, the mechanism reduces to plain FTLE/final distance. Only (c) outperforming both, together with a monotonic relation to ground-truth similarity rather than the inverse d_0 dependence, would show anything beyond standard FTLE.

statement: A trophic cascade following perturbation can constitute an active error-correcting loop when the network contains a threshold-gated indirect negative-feedback path that engages only above a perturbation-size threshold, returning the state toward the pre-perturbation attractor faster than linear relaxation predicted by the dominant eigenvalue alone.

what changes: standard dynamics plus a threshold-gated extra term engaging strong negative self-limitation only when herbivore density exceeds a resource-depletion threshold.
what persists: the [X] enabling the secondary corrective pathway persists as fixed structure whether or not currently active.
what is selected: none directly here; such corrective topologies could plausibly be targets of longer-run selection (mechanism 4).
what can reproduce: species reproduce per standard growth terms.
what can learn: none intrinsically; the system exhibits a measurable recovery function characterizable by an external model.
what can transfer: the corrective circuit should confer accelerated recovery when transplanted as a motif into different larger network contexts.
distinguishing observable: recovery-time-vs-perturbation-size curve should show a qualitative bend/discontinuity at the threshold, unlike smooth monotonic scaling from linear relaxation alone.
minimal world: 4-species community (predator, herbivore, primary resource, secondary regulatory resource) with the threshold-gated feedback term; intervention applies graded predator-removal fractions f and measures recovery time. Null twin: identical network but the threshold-gated term replaced by a smooth linear analog tuned to match integrated corrective magnitude over the trajectory ensemble; the null should produce a smooth monotonic recovery-time curve lacking the threshold-induced bend.

blind_text:
statement: Beyond first-order state representations tracking the world, the system maintains a distinct second-order representation that takes first-order states as its object, tagging each with a confidence estimate produced by a separate monitoring process. Reportability and [X] (opt-out, help-seeking) are driven by this second-order representation rather than directly by the first-order state.
what exists: a first-order state vector S; a second-order monitor module M(S) producing a scalar confidence c; a report/action channel gated by c; ground-truth outcomes for calibration
what changes: S updates from sensory input each timestep; M updates via a separate recurrent process comparing S's predictions to outcomes, adjusting c.
what persists: The calibration function learned by M persists across trials, decoupled from S's moment-to-moment content.
what is selected: Episodes where high-c judgments are rewarded reinforce the monitor's calibration; low-c-triggered opt-outs are reinforced when they avoid errors.
what can reproduce: The monitor module's parameters can be copied into a first-order module (a transplant test) to check whether calibration transfers.
what can learn: M learns to predict S's own error probability from internal dynamical features (e.g., evidence conflict), not merely from raw stimulus.
what can transfer: A monitor trained on one task-domain can be transplanted onto a structurally different first-order module and retain above-chance calibration if it learned domain-general error signatures.
distinguishing observable: Ablate the monitor module while leaving first-order performance intact; a dissociation where accuracy is unchanged but opt-out behavior collapses (or a blindsight-like pattern of accurate S with low reported c) is only possible under the two-level architecture, unlike a null that gates opt-out directly off first-order signal magnitude.
minimal world: A noisy two-alternative perceptual classifier paired with a small recurrent net M reading the classifier's internal activations (not the stimulus) to predict trial-wise error probability and gate an opt-out action. Null twin: a single-level agent thresholding its own decision-variable magnitude for opt-out. Both matched on easy-trial accuracy; tested on trials with induced overconfidence (biased evidence) where only the two-level system's opt-out tracks the decoupled calibration signal.

nearest_priors.name: Higher-order representation / metacognition networks (Rosenthal's Higher-Order Thought theory as implemented in Cleeremans/Pasquali 'second-order network' wagering models; Lau's higher-order signal-detection models)
nearest_priors.field: cognitive science / consciousness science / connectionist modelling
nearest_priors.explains: A distinct second-order network that reads first-order hidden activations, not the stimulus, and outputs a confidence or wager. Reportability and awareness are tied to the second-order level. The blindsight-like dissociation between intact first-order accuracy and low reported confidence. Ablation of the monitor as the diagnostic test. Learning of the wager through reward.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The explicit parameter-transplant test across structurally different first-order modules is not a standard part of these models. Domain-general error signatures are discussed in the literature but not built in.

nearest_priors.name: Second-order (post-decisional) confidence models: Fleming & Daw 2017 second-order computation; Insabato/Deco two-network confidence attractor model; the Kiani & Shadlen opt-out paradigm
nearest_priors.explains: A separate monitor that estimates the probability the first-order decision is wrong. Opt-out (uncertainty response) gated by confidence. Dissociation from the single-level null, which thresholds decision-variable magnitude (Kiani & Shadlen's balance of evidence). Behaviour under biased or overconfident evidence conditions.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Transplantation of the monitor across domains. The ablation-based architectural claim is only implicit in these models.

nearest_priors.name: Learned error predictors / confidence calibration heads (introspective failure prediction, ConfidNet, selective classification with a reject option, performance monitoring via error-related negativity / anterior cingulate)
nearest_priors.explains: A separate head trained on the base network's internal features to predict per-trial error. A reject option (abstain) that is rewarded when it avoids errors. Calibration against ground truth. Transfer tests of the failure predictor across tasks.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The link to reportability, awareness, and the blindsight framing.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little remains unexplained. The cross-architecture monitor transplant is a specific experimental proposal rather than a new mechanism. Metacognitive domain-generality is already studied, e.g. by Fleming and colleagues.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Train the Cleeremans-style second-order wagering network and the described system on the same classifier. Then transplant each monitor onto a structurally different first-order net and compare type-2 calibration (meta-d′ or AUROC2). If both perform equally, the description is just the prior renamed. Separately, induce overconfidence with biased evidence and test whether opt-out tracks the monitor's output rather than decision-variable magnitude. Compare against the Kiani & Shadlen single-level threshold null.

blind_text:
statement: A recursive bottleneck allocates bits per subdivision cell under a hard constraint that bit-depth vs scale follows a single global power law (one parameter gamma) rather than free per-cell allocation, with allowed distortion at each level set by locally measured sensitivity, producing a fractal ([X]-like) code whose scaling exponent matches the environment's own sensitivity exponent.
what exists: recursive spatial partition; per-cell bit budget b(l)=b_0*gamma^l; per-cell sensitivity sigma(l); rate-distortion loss with hard self-similarity constraint
what changes: gamma and b_0 are optimized to minimize total rate-distortion loss given observed sigma(l) profile; per-instance allocation follows the fixed gamma
what persists: gamma persists as the code's structural constant, defining scale-to-precision relationship across all inputs of that environment class
what is selected: among candidate codes (different gamma,b_0), the one minimizing total loss on training instances is retained
what can reproduce: the single-gamma allocation rule is reapplied identically at every recursion level
what can learn: gamma is learned from data, effectively learning the fractal dimension of the environment's necessary-precision structure
what can transfer: gamma transfers to compress instances from the same/related environment class at near-optimal rate-distortion without per-instance re-optimization
distinguishing observable: on held-out instances and unseen scales, the fixed-gamma code generalizes rate-distortion performance with one parameter, while a free per-level bit-allocation scheme (matched total bits and training-set distortion) overfits and degrades on unseen scales
minimal world: World: a fractional-Brownian self-affine signal (Hurst H) encoded via a recursive quad/binary partition with sound per-cell interval quantization. Intervention: fit single gamma tied to a sensitivity profile matching H, test on held-out instances and finer unseen scales. Null twin: unconstrained per-level bit lookup table, matched in total bits and average training-set distortion; predicted to match or beat mechanism on training scales but generalize worse to unseen finer scales/instances.

nearest_priors.name: Rate-distortion optimal bit allocation across wavelet scales for 1/f (fBm) processes (reverse water-filling on a power-law spectrum; Wornell's wavelet models of 1/f processes; Berger's R(D) for Gaussian processes)
nearest_priors.explains: Recursive dyadic partition of a self-affine signal. Precision per level is set by the variance or sensitivity at that scale, and it follows a closed-form rule parameterised by the spectral or Hurst exponent. Optimal allocation is therefore a scale-invariant rule tied to H, so it transfers to other instances of the same fBm class. In practice, estimating H is equivalent to 'learning gamma'.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Reverse water-filling on a power-law variance gives bits that are affine in level (a log-variance slope), not geometric b_0*gamma^l. It also does not frame the constraint as a hard, learned, single-parameter self-similarity prior chosen by empirical loss.

nearest_priors.name: Parametric (low-dimensional) versus nonparametric bit-allocation models: model-based bit allocation in transform or subband coding, regularised by MDL / bias-variance
nearest_priors.explains: A one- or two-parameter allocation law fitted to training data generalises to held-out instances and to scales extrapolated beyond training. A free per-level lookup table with matched bits can fit the training data as well or better, but it overfits and cannot extrapolate to unseen levels. Choosing (gamma, b_0) by minimising training loss is ordinary empirical risk minimisation over a small model class.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not by itself supply the recursive fractal structure or the link between the fitted exponent and the environment's sensitivity or Hurst exponent.

nearest_priors.name: Embedded or hierarchical wavelet coders with scale-dependent quantisation (EZW/SPIHT zerotrees, perceptually weighted quantisation matrices), and fractal/IFS coding (Barnsley–Jacquin)
nearest_priors.explains: The code is recursive and quadtree-based. The same allocation or quantisation rule is reapplied at every level, and step sizes are weighted by measured sensitivity per band. The resulting code is self-similar ('fractal-like'), and the rule is reused across images of a class.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: These coders do not explicitly constrain bits to a global power law in scale, and they do not learn an exponent matched to the source's sensitivity exponent.

parsed.unexplained_residual: The one small residual is the choice of a geometric (power-law) bits-versus-level law, b_0*gamma^l, rather than the affine-in-level law that reverse water-filling gives for power-law variance. This is a reparameterisation choice, and possibly a suboptimal one; it is not a new mechanism. Describing gamma as 'learning the fractal dimension' is a renaming of estimating the spectral or Hurst exponent.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: On fBm with known H, compare three coders on held-out instances and on finer unseen scales: the learned geometric-gamma coder, the analytic reverse-water-filling allocation (affine bits per level, slope set by H), and the free lookup table. If the analytic R(D) allocation matches or beats the learned gamma everywhere, the mechanism reduces to the known prior. Also vary H and check that the fitted gamma tracks the water-filling slope rather than an independent 'fractal' quantity.

blind_text:
statement: Internal belief states evolve continuously via gradient descent on a variational [X] functional that combines precision-weighted sensory prediction error with a complexity cost on deviation from prior beliefs. what persists: attractor structure/fixed points of the belief dynamics and the generative model g across trials
what is selected: belief trajectories that reduce [X] persist; higher-F trajectories are damped out by the gradient flow
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: slow adaptation of g's parameters to reduce long-run average [X] (learning the generative model)
what can transfer: learned prior/generative structure transfers to environments sharing the same hidden-cause [X]
distinguishing observable: under ambiguous or bistable stimuli, the gradient-flow model shows hysteresis (percept depends on recent history) and characteristic relaxation time scaling with precision, unlike a reactive controller
minimal world: A 1D hidden oscillatory phase generates noisy sensory readings; the model infers phase via gradient descent on F. Intervention: introduce an ambiguous/bistable stimulus segment and a sudden phase jump. Null twin: a [X]-like controller that minimizes instantaneous error only (no inferred hidden state, no complexity term), matched steady-state error — predicted to lack hysteresis and the characteristic gradual relaxation curve.

nearest_priors.name: Variational free-energy minimisation / predictive coding (Friston's Free Energy Principle; Rao & Ballard predictive coding; Bogacz's tutorial formulation)
nearest_priors.explains: Belief state mu updated by gradient descent on variational free energy F. F combines a precision-weighted squared sensory prediction error with a prior (complexity/KL) term. The generative mapping g is learned slowly by descending the time-averaged F. Learned priors transfer across environments that share the same hidden causes. It also gives relaxation time constants that scale with precision (the local curvature is roughly pi*g'(mu)^2), and hysteresis in multistable landscapes, as in predictive-coding accounts of binocular rivalry (Hohwy, Roepstorff & Friston 2008).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. The 'selection' of trajectories is a relabelling of dissipative gradient flow, not a separate mechanism.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman-Bucy filter / generalized filtering (Friston's DEM, generalized coordinates of motion)
nearest_priors.explains: Continuous-time inference of a hidden (oscillatory) state from noisy observations. Correction steps are weighted by precision. The inference is recursive and history-dependent. Parameters can be learned via EM.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The linear-Gaussian Kalman filter has a single posterior mode, so it gives no bistability or hysteresis. It also does not use explicit gradient descent on a nonconvex energy.

nearest_priors.name: Energy-based attractor networks / gradient dynamical systems (Hopfield networks; double-well models of perceptual bistability and hysteresis)
nearest_priors.explains: Gradient flow on a Lyapunov function produces fixed-point attractors. Hysteresis and critical slowing arise under ambiguous input. Relaxation rate is set by landscape curvature.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It lacks the probabilistic interpretation: a generative model of hidden causes, precision as inverse variance, and a complexity cost relative to a prior.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The null twin, a reactive error-minimising controller without inferred state, is a standard comparison. The claimed hysteresis depends on F being nonconvex (a multimodal prior or nonlinear g), which the free-energy framework already accommodates.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Manipulate the precision pi and the prior strength independently during the ambiguous segment and the phase jump. Measure the relaxation time constant, which should approach 1/(pi*g'^2 + prior curvature), and the width of the hysteresis loop. Standard predictive coding predicts both exactly. A deviation, such as hysteresis that persists when the prior term is removed or relaxation times that do not track precision, would indicate a mechanism beyond the canonical free-energy gradient flow.

blind_text:
statement: A learning system is pressured by an explicit two-term objective to minimize mutual information between its input and internal representation while maximizing mutual information between that representation and the output it must predict. This forces the [X] of a maximally compressed sufficient [X] of the input for the task, rather than a representation that retains incidental input detail.
what exists: input variable X; encoder producing representation Z; predictor mapping Z to Y; estimators of I(X;Z) and I(Z;Y); trade-off parameter beta
what changes: Encoder and predictor weights update via gradient descent on L = I(Z;Y) minus beta*I(X;Z), with beta annealed from low to high over training.
what persists: The effective dimensionality/entropy of Z at convergence, reflecting the compression-prediction trade-off point selected by beta.
what is selected: Representations that discard input variance uncorrelated with Y are favored over those retaining it, at fixed predictive performance.
what can reproduce: The trained encoder parameters can be copied to instantiate agents with the same compressed code.
what can learn: The encoder learns the minimal sufficient [X]; the predictor learns to use it.
what can transfer: The compressed Z transfers to tasks that depend on the same predictive information Y' predictable from the original Y-relevant structure.
distinguishing observable: Plotting I(X;Z) vs training epoch shows a non-monotonic compression phase (rise then fall) after I(Z;Y) saturates; a null twin trained with a fixed [X] weight-penalty of matched final parameter norm instead of the [X] term shows I(X;Z) that only rises or plateaus, without a distinct post-fit compression phase.
minimal world: World: synthetic X = task-relevant signal s plus independent nuisance noise n; Y is a deterministic function of s only. Intervention: train encoder/predictor under the [X] objective with annealed beta and measure I(X;Z), I(Z;Y), and I(n;Z) via binned/kNN estimators across training. Null twin: same architecture, same task loss, but regularized by weight-decay ([X]) tuned to match final test accuracy and final parameter-norm scale; measure whether I(n;Z) is driven toward zero in the [X] run but remains substantially above zero in the [X]-matched null twin.

nearest_priors.name: Information Bottleneck method (Tishby, Pereira & Bialek 1999), trained via the Deep Variational Information Bottleneck (Alemi et al. 2017)
nearest_priors.explains: The whole mechanism with only renaming. The Lagrangian I(Z;Y) - beta*I(X;Z) trades compression against prediction. It yields an approximately minimal sufficient statistic. An encoder and decoder are trained by gradient methods using estimators or variational bounds on the mutual informations. The rate-distortion-like trade-off point set by beta fixes the entropy and dimensionality of Z. Nuisance variance uncorrelated with Y is discarded, and the compressed code transfers to Y-relevant tasks.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Nothing central. The specific beta-annealing schedule (low to high) and the exact nonparametric binned/kNN estimator choice are implementation details, not new mechanism. The sign convention is slightly off: 'gradient descent on L' should read ascent on L, or descent on -L.

nearest_priors.name: Information-plane dynamics / two-phase fitting-then-compression account of deep learning (Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby 2017), with the Saxe et al. 2018 critique
nearest_priors.explains: The distinguishing observable. I(X;Z) rises and then falls after I(Z;Y) saturates, tracked across training epochs with binned or kNN MI estimators. The critique supplies the reason a null twin is needed: whether compression appears depends on the estimator, the activation saturation and the regularizer, not on SGD alone.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not by itself use an explicit IB objective. In the original claim, compression emerges implicitly from SGD noise rather than from a beta*I(X;Z) term.

nearest_priors.name: Minimal sufficient statistics and nuisance-invariant representation learning (Fisher; Achille & Soatto 2018 'Emergence of invariance and disentanglement')
nearest_priors.explains: The target object: a minimal sufficient statistic of X for Y. The mechanism drives I(n;Z) toward zero for nuisance n. The contrast with weight decay reflects Achille & Soatto's link between information in the weights and invariance in the representation.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not give the specific annealed training procedure or the epoch-wise compression-phase signature.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially none. The weight-decay-matched null twin is a standard ablation. The only open question is empirical: whether an explicit I(X;Z) penalty, rather than L2, uniquely produces the post-fit compression phase. That is contested in the literature (estimator artifacts, dependence on activation functions) but is not mechanistically novel.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Train the same architecture on the synthetic s+n task in three conditions: (a) the explicit IB/VIB objective with annealed beta; (b) an L2 weight-decay twin; (c) a VIB run with beta fixed at its final value, no annealing. Use both ReLU and tanh activations. Measure I(X;Z), I(Z;Y) and I(n;Z) with several estimators (binning, kNN, variational upper bounds). If (a) and (c) reach the same converged I(n;Z), and the compression phase in (a) is only the schedule tracking the moving beta optimum, the mechanism is exactly standard IB. The description would add something beyond IB only if (a) shows estimator-robust, activation-independent post-fit compression that (c) lacks.

blind_text:
statement: Each site enters a strict refractory state for a fixed number of timesteps immediately after toppling, during which it cannot topple again regardless of accumulated excess, forcing excess to queue or diffuse elsewhere. This mechanism caps the maximum local toppling frequency and reshapes the upper tail of the avalanche-size/duration distribution by preventing runaway repeated local cascades, serving as a built-in negative-feedback correction against local instability.
what exists: sites with scalar state, threshold, and a refractory countdown timer
what changes: A site whose timer is nonzero cannot topple even if above threshold; its excess simply accumulates until the timer reaches zero, at which point it topples (possibly by a large amount) and the timer resets.
what persists: The refractory timer value persists per site as a hidden state variable across steps.
what is selected: N/A directly; refractory period length is a fixed world parameter being tested.
what can reproduce: N/A.
what can learn: N/A in minimal form.
what can transfer: The relationship between refractory period length and the upper cutoff/shape of the avalanche duration distribution should be a transferable quantitative curve.
distinguishing observable: As refractory period length increases from 0, the avalanche duration distribution should show an increasingly sharp cutoff at a duration scale set by the refractory period, while avalanche size distribution at fixed duration bins should show characteristic bursty/quantized jumps corresponding to queued excess release; a system without refractory dynamics shows no such duration-quantization signature.
minimal world: Base [X] lattice with an added per-site refractory countdown as described; sweep refractory period from 0 to several multiples of the mean inter-toppling interval and measure avalanche duration distributions. The null twin instead adds a fixed additive delay to the drive clock itself (globally slowing down drive) chosen to produce the same mean avalanche rate, without any per-site refractory suppression — matching overall event rate but not reproducing the duration-quantization or size-queuing signature.

nearest_priors.name: Sandpile (BTW) model with refractory period / dead time — e.g., refractory sandpiles and neuronal avalanche models (Levina–Herrmann–Geisel style, integrate-and-fire with absolute refractoriness)
nearest_priors.explains: Per-site threshold toppling on the base [X]=BTW/Abelian sandpile lattice plus a per-site refractory countdown during which the site cannot fire. This caps local firing rate, accumulates excess, and releases it when the timer expires. The model is known to alter the avalanche size and duration cutoffs.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific claim that duration quantization and bursty size jumps scale with refractory length as a transferable curve is a prediction, not an established result. The null-twin design is also experiment-specific.

nearest_priors.name: Greenberg–Hastings / excitable-medium cellular automaton
nearest_priors.explains: Its discrete states are excited, refractory for a fixed number of steps, then resting. The refractory period suppresses immediate re-excitation and shapes wave propagation and timing.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It has no accumulating scalar excess or queued release. It also lacks conservative sandpile redistribution and slow-drive avalanche statistics.

nearest_priors.name: Olami–Feder–Christensen / Burridge–Knopoff with healing time or stick-slip dead time
nearest_priors.explains: Threshold relaxation with a post-slip locking interval that limits repeated local failure. It modifies the tail of the event-size distribution.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It is typically non-conservative. It does not frame the effect as queued excess released in quantized bursts, or as a duration-cutoff scaling with the timer length.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Two predicted signatures are not established results of any listed prior: the duration quantization at multiples of the refractory period, and the specific size-jump structure within fixed duration bins. The comparison against a global drive-delay null twin is methodological rather than a new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run a BTW sandpile with refractory period T swept from 0 upward. Compare it against an integrate-and-fire neuronal avalanche model with an absolute refractory period of equal T. Measure (1) the avalanche duration histogram for peaks or cutoffs at multiples of T, and (2) the conditional size distribution per duration bin. If both models match, the mechanism is just the refractory sandpile. Also compare with the global drive-delay null to confirm that the signature requires per-site suppression.

blind_text:
statement: Network connectivity itself is mutable: after each block of avalanches, an edge is randomly added if the recent measured branching ratio was below 1, or randomly removed if it was above 1, with mutation probability proportional to the magnitude of deviation from 1. This structural mutation operator tests whether adjusting [X] (rather than thresholds) is sufficient to self-tune a network toward the critical branching point.
what exists: directed graph with binary/continuous nodes; measured branching ratio over a sliding window; edge set that can grow or shrink
what changes: After each measurement window: if branching ratio < 1, add a random edge with probability proportional to (1 - branching_ratio); if > 1, remove a random existing edge with probability proportional to (branching_ratio - 1).
what persists: The evolving edge set persists and accumulates structural changes across windows, forming the network's connectivity history.
what is selected: Edges are added/removed based on global branching-ratio feedback rather than any node-level selection; effectively the [X] as a whole is selected toward a branching-ratio-1 configuration.
what can reproduce: N/A - edges are added/removed, not literally reproduced with inheritance.
what can learn: The network [X] 'learns' a connectivity density that yields near-critical branching, which is a structural analogue of parameter learning.
what can transfer: The final converged edge density (average degree) as a function of node count and activation-propagation probability should follow a predictable transferable relationship if this mechanism, rather than initial density, determines the outcome.
distinguishing observable: Networks starting from very different initial edge densities (sparse vs dense) converge to statistically indistinguishable branching ratios (~1) and avalanche exponents after sufficient mutation rounds; a network with fixed [X] (no mutation) instead retains branching ratios that differ systematically with initial density.
minimal world: A random directed graph (100 nodes) with activation propagation probability p per edge; implement the described edge add/remove mutation operator based on measured branching ratio over sliding windows of activity, starting from several different initial densities. Measure convergence of branching ratio and final degree distribution. The null twin uses random (non-feedback) edge rewiring at a matched overall rate of edge changes (same number of add/remove events per window) chosen independently of the measured branching ratio, preserving [X] change rate but not its direction relative to [X].

nearest_priors.name: Activity-dependent rewiring toward self-organized criticality (Bornholdt & Rohlf 2000 adaptive Boolean networks; Bornholdt & Röhl 2003)
nearest_priors.explains: Edges are added or removed based on activity statistics, and connectivity converges to a critical average degree regardless of initial density. Topology serves as the self-tuned parameter, and the converged degree has a predictable dependence on system parameters.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The original rule is local. It uses node frozen/active status, adding an edge to a frozen node and removing one from an active node. The described rule uses the global measured branching ratio instead, with probability proportional to the deviation.

nearest_priors.name: Homeostatic structural plasticity / synaptic scaling toward branching ratio 1 (Levina-Herrmann-Geisel dynamic synapses; homeostatic SOC, e.g. Zierenberg et al. 2018, Tetzlaff/van Ooyen structural plasticity)
nearest_priors.explains: Negative feedback on measured branching ratio or activity drives the network to sigma≈1. Avalanche exponents become near-critical from any starting point, and the fixed-parameter null retains its initial-condition dependence.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It usually adjusts weights, thresholds or local synapse counts rather than randomly adding or deleting edges under a single global feedback signal.

nearest_priors.name: Stochastic approximation / integral controller on mean degree (Robbins-Monro set-point control of the branching parameter sigma = p·<k>)
nearest_priors.explains: Edge changes have a probability proportional to the error (sigma - 1), which gives a noisy proportional controller whose fixed point is <k> ≈ 1/p. This predicts the transferable relation between converged degree, N and p. The unbiased-rewiring null lacks the restoring drift.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It says nothing about avalanche statistics or the degree-distribution shape, which come from branching-process theory.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little. The only differences from known priors are that the feedback is a global branching-ratio estimate rather than a local activity signal, and that it applies random edge addition and deletion. The result is essentially mean-field SOC by feedback on the control parameter (the 'sweeping instability' of self-organized criticality).
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare two versions of the rule. The global version adds and removes edges at random positions based on the network-wide branching ratio. The Bornholdt-Rohlf-style version is local: it adds or removes edges at specific nodes based on each node's own activity. Test both on heterogeneous networks, for example with degree-correlated p or modular structure. The global rule should only fix the mean degree at about 1/p and leave local heterogeneity untouched, so node-level branching ratios still vary. The local rule should also equalize node-level branching. Separately, check whether the converged <k> tracks 1/p exactly, including with finite-window noise, as the controller view predicts.

blind_text:
statement: Each neuron tracks its own long-run average firing rate and periodically multiplies all of its incoming synaptic weights by a scaling factor equal to the ratio of a target rate to the observed average rate, operating on a timescale much slower than [X]/[X] plasticity. This preserves the relative pattern of learned weights while preventing runaway excitation or silencing.
what exists: neuron with a slow firing-rate trace; vector of incoming synaptic weights; target firing rate set-point; scaling timescale parameter
what changes: weights are periodically rescaled: w_i ← w_i·(target_rate/observed_rate_avg), applied uniformly across all of a neuron's inputs
what persists: the relative ratios among a neuron's synaptic weights (its selectivity pattern) are preserved across scaling events
what is selected: not selection-based; the set-point and scaling timescale parameters could themselves be varied and selected across agents for stability-performance tradeoffs
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: the network can continue [X]/[X] learning over indefinitely long experience streams without weight saturation, enabling continual learning
what can transfer: preserved relative selectivity patterns remain stable and usable across contexts with different overall input drive (e.g., after partial deafferentation)
distinguishing observable: drive one input pathway with sustained elevated activity for an extended period: the mechanism predicts stable output rates and preserved relative ranking of synaptic weights across the perturbation, whereas a model with [X] plasticity alone (no scaling) shows weight saturation/runaway and loss of relative selectivity ranking.
minimal world: A single model neuron receives inputs from two populations, one of which is artificially driven to elevated sustained activity for an extended period while [X] plasticity continues. The mechanism model applies periodic multiplicative rescaling of all weights based on the neuron's own average rate; the null twin has plasticity only, no rescaling. The diagnostic is whether relative selectivity (weight ranking) and output rate remain stable (mechanism) or diverge/saturate (null) despite identical input drive [X].

nearest_priors.name: Homeostatic synaptic scaling (multiplicative synaptic scaling; Turrigiano et al. 1998; van Rossum, Bi & Turrigiano 2000)

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Biological scaling is usually modeled as a continuous integral controller (dw/dt ∝ w·(target−rate)) rather than a periodic one-shot ratio update. nearest_priors.name: Weight normalization in Hebbian learning (von der Malsburg 1973; Oja's rule; multiplicative normalization in Miller & MacKay 1994)
nearest_priors.explains: Multiplicative rescaling of an incoming weight vector that preserves relative ratios and prevents unbounded Hebbian growth, enabling stable ongoing learning.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It normalizes to a fixed weight norm, not to a target firing rate measured by a slow activity trace. It is not driven by the neuron's observed output activity or set-point error.

nearest_priors.name: BCM sliding-threshold metaplasticity (Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro 1982)
nearest_priors.explains: A slow average of postsynaptic activity regulates plasticity to stabilize firing rates and avoid runaway Hebbian dynamics.

blind_text:
statement: A set of general rules and a set of particular case-judgments are iteratively adjusted toward mutual consistency: whichever side (a rule or a conflicting judgment) has lower confidence yields to the other at each mismatch, until a fixed point of mutual coherence is reached. This produces a rule set shaped jointly by principle and case rather than by either alone.
what exists: a set of general rules R with confidences; a set of particular case-judgments J with confidences; a consistency-checker comparing R applied to case inputs against stored J verdicts
what changes: At each mismatch between R's verdict and J's stored judgment for a case, the lower-confidence side is adjusted toward the higher-confidence side; iterate until mismatches fall below tolerance.
what persists: The fixed point (a mutually consistent R,J configuration) persists as a stable attractor once reached.
what is selected: Rule-judgment configurations that are mutually consistent are retained; inconsistent configurations are progressively eliminated over iterations.
what can reproduce: N/A.
what can learn: Both R and J are adjusted through the process; a meta-parameter governing which side yields under conflict can itself be tuned from long-run predictive success.
what can transfer: The converged rule set R transfers to judge cases outside the original J set.
distinguishing observable: Bidirectional mutual adjustment reaches a configuration with fewer residual mismatches and better held-out generalization and noise-robustness than either a pure top-down control (rules always overwrite judgments) or a pure bottom-up control (judgments always overwrite rules), given identical case sets and iteration budgets.
minimal world: 30 labeled particular cases (feature vector plus judgment label, some mislabeled/noisy) and 3 candidate threshold-classifier rules initialized arbitrarily; run the mutual-adjustment loop for T iterations and evaluate held-out accuracy. Null twins: (A) rules fixed, only judgments adjusted to match rule outputs; (B) judgments fixed, only rules adjusted to match given labels; compare held-out generalization and robustness to label noise across all three variants.
