blind_text:
statement: The sparsity threshold applied to each coefficient is not fixed but scaled by that coefficient's own [X] variance: high-certainty coefficients require larger residual evidence to stay active (aggressive pruning), while high-uncertainty coefficients are retained with weaker evidence. This makes sparsification itself a function of epistemic state rather than of coefficient magnitude alone.
what exists: coefficient x_i; variance P_ii; per-unit adaptive threshold theta_i = f(P_ii); activation indicator
what changes: theta_i rises as P_ii falls (confidence increases), so the effective [X] penalty tightens as uncertainty shrinks
what persists: the functional form f mapping variance to threshold
what is selected: coefficients that survive precision-scaled thresholding versus fixed-threshold pruning
what can reproduce: the variance-to-threshold mapping can be copied across different noise regimes
what can learn: the shape of f can be tuned to minimize a joint cost of reconstruction error and active-unit count
what can transfer: the mapping generalizes across observation noise levels without retuning fixed thresholds
distinguishing observable: under increasing observation noise, precision-gated thresholding keeps more units active (correctly reflecting rising uncertainty) whereas a fixed-magnitude threshold prunes at a constant rate regardless of noise
minimal world: A fixed sparse generative process is observed under three noise regimes (low, medium, high). Intervention: sweep noise variance and record active-unit count under precision-gated thresholding. Null twin: identical filter but with a fixed magnitude threshold independent of P_ii, matched to produce the same average sparsity at the medium noise level, which will show flat (not increasing) active-unit count as noise rises.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman-filtered compressed sensing (KF-CS / modified-CS residual support detection, Vaswani) with covariance-dependent add/delete thresholds
nearest_priors.explains: The core setup: a recursive filter tracks sparse coefficients x_i with error covariance P, and support is decided by thresholding residual or filtered evidence. Also covers the sweep of active-support size against observation noise, and tuning the thresholds to trade reconstruction error against support size.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Standard KF-CS uses fixed or noise-scaled global thresholds. It does not set a per-coefficient threshold that rises as P_ii falls.

nearest_priors.name: Sparse Bayesian learning / Automatic Relevance Determination (Tipping RVM, Bayesian compressive sensing)
nearest_priors.explains: Pruning becomes a function of each coefficient's posterior variance and precision rather than its raw magnitude. Uncertainty-dependent retention shifts with noise level, so no hand-set magnitude threshold needs retuning across noise regimes.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: ARD prunes through evidence maximisation over hyperparameters, not an explicit tunable map theta_i = f(P_ii). Its direction also differs: it prunes coefficients whose precision diverges to prior-dominated values, rather than pruning confident coefficients more aggressively.

nearest_priors.name: Variance-scaled significance thresholding (Wald/z-test pruning, SNR-based pruning as in variational-dropout or Fisher/OBD saliency)
nearest_priors.explains: It fits the per-coefficient threshold defined as a function of that coefficient's own estimated variance. It also fits a learned or tuned mapping from variance to keep/prune decisions.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The monotonicity is inverted. These methods demand more evidence from high-variance coefficients and so prune them first. The described mechanism instead retains high-uncertainty coefficients on weaker evidence.

parsed.unexplained_residual: The specific monotone direction is the only non-standard element. Threshold decreasing in P_ii means uncertainty protects a coefficient from pruning, which is an exploration-like 'keep while unsure' rule. It is grafted onto a Kalman/sparse-recovery filter, and no single prior uses this direction as a support-selection rule. Everything else is Kalman filtering plus adaptive thresholding.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Sweep observation noise while holding the sparse generative process fixed, and compare three rules: (a) the described rule with theta_i decreasing in P_ii; (b) a Wald/SNR rule keeping |x_i|/sqrt(P_ii) > c; (c) KF-CS with a fixed threshold. As noise rises, (a) should give an increasing active count, including false positives on true-zero coefficients. Rule (b) should give a decreasing active count, and (c) a roughly flat one. Also inject a coefficient with a large magnitude but a very small P_ii whose residual support is weak. Only (a) prunes it.

statement: Each site in a lattice accumulates a scalar quantity from a slow, uniform, random drive; when a site's value exceeds a fixed threshold it relaxes by transferring a fixed fraction of its excess to its neighbors, which can push those neighbors over threshold in turn. No external parameter is tuned; the separation between slow driving and fast relaxation alone produces a stationary state with scale-free avalanche sizes.

what changes: Drive increments a random site each slow tick; any site above threshold topples, redistributing its excess to neighbors on the fast clock until no site exceeds threshold, then the slow clock advances again.
what persists: The subcritical/marginal distribution of z across sites between drive events; no long-term memory beyond current field configuration.
what is selected: Nothing is selected across runs; within a run, configurations that are stable under the local threshold rule persist longer.
what can reproduce: N/A - no reproduction, only state propagation.
what can learn: Nothing learns in this minimal version; it is a pure physical relaxation process.
what can transfer: The statistical shape of avalanches (size, duration exponents) transfers across different lattice sizes/topologies if the mechanism is the true cause.
distinguishing observable: Avalanche size distribution follows a power law with a size-independent exponent as system size grows, versus an exponential/characteristic-scale distribution if a smaller alternative (e.g., independent random topplings, no redistribution) generates similar mean activity.
minimal world: A 1D or 2D grid of ~100-1000 cells with integer heights, slow random single-cell increments, and threshold-triggered redistribution to nearest neighbors; measure avalanche size/duration histograms across increasing grid sizes. The null twin drives each cell independently and lets it 'topple' by resetting to zero without transferring mass to neighbors, matching mean activity and firing rate but destroying the spatial redistribution that produces scale invariance.

blind_text:
statement: A network's global connectivity is controlled by a single parameter (edge probability or rewiring probability) and exhibits a sharp percolation [X] at a critical value, below which the network fragments into small disconnected components and above which a giant component spans most nodes. Only above this threshold can information injected at one node reliably reach distal nodes, gating whether the network functions as an integrated computational substrate.
what exists: set of nodes; edges added according to control parameter p; signal injected at a source node; measurement of information/activity at distal nodes
what changes: Edges are added/removed as p is swept; network [X] (giant component size, path lengths) changes correspondingly; a fixed dynamical process (e.g., diffusion or spiking) runs on top of the current [X].
what persists: Once p exceeds the critical value, the giant component persists as the dominant structural feature across further small perturbations to p.
what is selected: Not applicable directly; the law is purely structural/dynamical, though it gates which downstream learned functions (needing global integration) are achievable.
what can reproduce: Not applicable.
what can learn: A readout trained to use distal-node activity only succeeds in learning integrative tasks when p is above the percolation threshold.
what can transfer: Signal correlations between distant node pairs, once established, transfer information regardless of specific task, but only in the connected regime.
distinguishing observable: Mutual information between a fixed source node and a distal node, measured as a function of p, shows a sharp transition near p_c with finite-size scaling exponents matching percolation theory; a null twin with the same average degree but a regular lattice [X] (no random rewiring) shows a smooth, gradual increase in mutual information with p and no sharp threshold or scaling collapse.
minimal world: World: N nodes, edges added at random with probability p (Erdos-Renyi); a diffusive/relay dynamic propagates an injected signal from a fixed source node. Intervention: sweep p across the theoretical percolation threshold p_c = 1/N for this [X], measuring giant-component size and source-to-distal mutual information at multiple network sizes to test finite-size scaling. Null twin: same N and same average degree achieved instead by a ring lattice with local rewiring limited to nearest neighbors plus the same number of total edges added deterministically (not randomly), preserving average degree and edge count but lacking random long-range shortcuts; compare the sharpness/threshold behavior of source-to-distal mutual information between the two.

nearest_priors.name: Erdős–Rényi giant component phase transition (random graph percolation)
nearest_priors.explains: The sharp emergence of a giant component at p_c = 1/N (mean degree 1). Fragmentation into small components below it and a spanning component above it. Persistence of the giant component under small perturbations of p. Finite-size scaling exponents in the mean-field percolation class. The gating of source-to-distal reachability, since a signal can only reach nodes in the same component.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not by itself specify the mutual-information readout, the dynamics running on the graph, or the downstream learning claim. These are consequences of connectivity rather than part of the theorem.

nearest_priors.name: Epidemic/diffusion spreading on networks (SIR–bond percolation mapping; signal propagation on graphs)
nearest_priors.explains: A fixed diffusive or relay process on the graph whose global reach tracks the percolation transition. Source-to-distal correlation or mutual information jumps near p_c because outbreak or reach size maps onto cluster size.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The trained-readout learnability claim. The specific lattice null-twin comparison.

nearest_priors.name: Watts–Strogatz small-world model vs. regular ring lattice
nearest_priors.explains: Motivates the null twin: a ring lattice without random long-range shortcuts, where path lengths and integration change smoothly rather than through a sharp connectivity transition. Also covers the 'rewiring probability' variant of the control parameter.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: WS rewiring starts from an already-connected lattice, so it has no giant-component percolation transition. The sharp threshold comes from ER, not WS.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the loose claim that a trained readout 'succeeds in learning integrative tasks' only above p_c. This is a direct corollary of reachability, as in reservoir computing on graphs, not a new mechanism. There is also a minor inconsistency: the statement conflates edge probability, which has a percolation threshold, with rewiring probability, which does not produce one. In addition, the 1D ring-lattice null trivially lacks a finite-p percolation transition.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Measure source-to-distal mutual information and giant-component fraction versus p at several N. Collapse the curves using mean-field percolation exponents (β=1, ν such that the window scales as N^{-1/3}). If the MI transition exactly tracks the giant-component emergence and collapses with standard percolation exponents, it is plain ER percolation. A distinct mechanism would require the MI threshold or exponents to deviate from the connectivity transition, for example an MI onset at a p different from 1/N, or non-percolation scaling.

blind_text:
statement: Each avalanche of size s carries a probability, increasing with s, of nucleating a domain of a competing phase at a random site within its footprint. Domain growth then follows standard phase-ordering dynamics until it either dies or spans the system. This produces punctuated, avalanche-triggered symmetry breaking rather than either continuous, driven phase ordering or ordinary undirected [X].
what exists: [X] heights h_i; binary phase label φ_i per site; domain boundaries; avalanche size counter s
what changes: after each avalanche completes, with probability f(s)=min(1,s/s0) a seed domain of the opposite phase is planted at a random avalanche site; domains then evolve by majority-rule relaxation between avalanches.
what persists: the phase configuration persists between avalanches except at nucleation events; [X] drive continues uninterrupted.
what is selected: no selection among agents; nucleation events are selected in the sense that only avalanches exceeding a size threshold can trigger a phase flip.
what can reproduce: domains can 'reproduce' by growing and splitting via majority-rule dynamics, but this is growth not replication with heredity.
what can learn: not applicable.
what can transfer: the statistical relationship between avalanche-size distribution and inter-nucleation waiting-time distribution should transfer across system sizes as a scaling relation.
distinguishing observable: a power-law relationship between avalanche size distribution and phase-flip waiting-time distribution (punctuated equilibrium signature); null twin nucleates phase flips at a rate matched in mean but independent of avalanche size, producing exponential (Poisson) waiting times instead.
minimal world: 2D [X] [X] with an overlaid Ising-like phase field; intervene by making nucleation probability depend on avalanche size s versus a null twin where nucleation is a fixed-rate Poisson process with the same overall nucleation frequency; compare waiting-time distributions and cross-correlation between avalanche size and subsequent domain size.

nearest_priors.name: Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld sandpile (self-organized criticality) with avalanche-driven coupling to a secondary field
nearest_priors.explains: The redacted [X] is almost certainly the sandpile: heights h_i, slow uninterrupted drive, avalanches of size s with power-law statistics, and a 2D lattice as the minimal world. It provides the heavy-tailed trigger process.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The overlaid binary phase field, nucleation of opposite-phase seeds, and majority-rule domain coarsening are not part of the sandpile.

nearest_priors.name: Zero-temperature Glauber / majority-rule Ising coarsening (phase-ordering kinetics) with nucleation of droplets
nearest_priors.explains: It covers the binary phase label, domain boundaries, and majority-rule relaxation of seeded droplets that either shrink and die or grow to span the system. This is classical nucleation-and-growth / Allen-Cahn-type domain dynamics.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Here nucleation is triggered by an external avalanche process with a size-dependent probability, rather than by thermal fluctuations at a fixed rate.

nearest_priors.name: Bak-Sneppen model / punctuated equilibrium; avalanche-triggered (marked point process) events
nearest_priors.explains: It accounts for the framing of intermittent, avalanche-triggered macroscopic transitions and the punctuated-equilibrium signature. The size-dependent triggering is a thinning of a marked point process.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It has no explicit Ising phase field or coarsening dynamics, and no sandpile height variables.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing mechanistically novel remains. The model is a sandpile driving a thinned nucleation process into Ising coarsening. One caveat about the predicted signature: BTW avalanche sizes are nearly independent from one avalanche to the next, and each avalanche triggers nucleation independently with probability f(s). The inter-nucleation waiting time counted in avalanches is therefore approximately geometric with mean 1/E[f(s)]. That means the claimed power-law waiting times versus Poisson null may not actually differ. Only the avalanche-size–domain-size cross-correlation (seed footprint) reliably distinguishes the model from the null.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the sandpile with Ising overlay under two conditions. In the first, nucleation probability is f(s). In the second, nucleation is a Poisson process with a matched mean rate and seeds of matched size. Measure the waiting-time distribution in drive units, which tests for non-Poisson structure beyond what avalanche temporal correlations produce. Also measure the correlation between the triggering s and the resulting domain survival and spanning probability. Further, shuffle the avalanche order: if the waiting-time statistics are unchanged, the 'punctuated' signature is just thinning of an i.i.d. process and reduces to the composite prior.

statement: Controller gains are stored as a precomputed function (table or interpolant) of a directly measurable scheduling variable, computed offline for a grid of operating points; online, the controller simply reads the current scheduling variable and looks up or interpolates the corresponding gain, performing no online estimation or error-driven update whatsoever. Adaptation here is a static stored mapping rather than a learning process.
what exists: scheduling variable s(t); precomputed gain table K(s); controller state
what changes: K(t) = K(s(t)) via table lookup/interpolation each step; the table K(.) itself never changes online
what persists: the table K(.) itself, fixed for the duration of operation
what is selected: not applicable online (the table was fixed by prior offline design, not selected during operation)
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: nothing online; all adaptation knowledge is baked in at design time
what can transfer: the table transfers unchanged to any plant instance whose operating-point-to-dynamics relationship matches the design assumptions
distinguishing observable: controller gain depends only on the instantaneous scheduling variable s(t), with zero dependence on the history of tracking error, whereas a true online-adaptive controller's gain at the same s can differ depending on past error trajectory -- measuring whether K(t) is a deterministic, memoryless function of s(t) alone (versus depending on error history) distinguishes gain scheduling from online adaptation
minimal world: Plant whose true dynamics parameter depends on a measurable exogenous variable s(t) (e.g., an inertia that varies with s); gain-scheduled controller K(s) is precomputed optimal at a grid of s values. Intervention: inject an unmodeled disturbance uncorrelated with s while sweeping s across its range. Null twin: a single fixed-gain controller (no scheduling) tested on the same trajectory. The scheduled controller's gain changes with s but shows zero corrective response to the disturbance (since it never reads error), which is exactly the signature distinguishing it from a true adaptive controller that would react to the disturbance-induced error regardless of s.

statement: A population of noisy units independently estimates the same variable; a robust consensus aggregate (e.g., trimmed mean) is computed from all estimates for downstream use, and each unit slowly recalibrates its own bias toward reducing its residual from the consensus. what changes: Each step, unit i outputs y_i = v + noise_i + bias_i; consensus c = robust_aggregate(y_1..y_M); bias_i updates slowly toward reducing (y_i - c).
what persists: The redundancy factor M and the calibrated bias configuration persist as the stable operating point of the ensemble.
what is selected: Units with smaller systematic bias (more consistent with consensus) contribute more reliably; in a competitive variant, low-reliability units can be pruned and replaced.
what can reproduce: The whole ensemble configuration (biases, count M) can be copied into a instance to bootstrap error-corrected coding immediately.
what can learn: Each unit's bias parameter is learned online from consensus residuals; the ensemble learns a self-consistent calibrated code.
what can transfer: A calibrated ensemble can be transplanted into a related context with similar noise [X] requiring minimal re-calibration.
distinguishing observable: Decoding accuracy degrades gracefully (roughly linearly) as an increasing fraction of units is lesioned, rather than failing abruptly.
minimal world: M=20 noisy sensors reporting a scalar v(t) plus independent noise and slowly drifting unit-specific bias; consensus readout via trimmed mean drives a steering task. Progressively lesion increasing fractions of units and measure the performance decay curve. Null twin: a single unit with noise variance equal to 1/M of the ensemble's effective noise (matched aggregate accuracy when undamaged), which fails completely upon its own lesion instead of degrading gracefully.

The claimed contrast with state mutation is also standard: attractors are robust to initial conditions, but not near basin boundaries or in multistable or chaotic regimes, which the null twin avoids by construction.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare the distribution of phenotype change against |delta theta| for ES Gaussian parameter mutation and for this operator, on the same logistic map. If they are identical, the mechanism is just ES mutation plus a bifurcating genotype-phenotype map. A genuinely novel operator would need to use the known bifurcation boundaries, for example by biasing or scaling mutations relative to r*. Test whether offspring period-change frequency depends only on distance to r* and sigma, as Gaussian mutation predicts, or on some boundary-aware rule.

blind_text:
statement: An agent's model must predict the outcome of its own interventions using structural equations, and is penalized whenever its interventional prediction P(Y | do(X=x)) disagrees with the actually observed post-intervention outcome, even when a purely correlational predictor P(Y|X=x) fits observational data equally well. This forces retention of only those cause-effect mechanisms that remain invariant when the agent actively changes X, rather than merely correlated features.
what exists: structural causal model with exogenous noise and parameterized mechanisms; agent's learned mechanism parameters; intervention actions do(X=x); an observational-correlation baseline predictor for comparison
what changes: Agent selects intervention x, observes outcome y; mechanism parameters updated to reduce |predicted P(Y|do(X=x)) - observed y| via gradient descent, distinct from and compared against updates to a correlation-only predictor trained solely on observational (non-interventional) (x,y) pairs.
what persists: Mechanism parameters corresponding to true causal edges remain stable/invariant as the exogenous distribution of X is varied across contexts; spurious correlational parameters do not.
what is selected: Structural edges whose predicted interventional outcomes match observed outcomes across many different intervention/context distributions are retained with high confidence; edges that fail under some context are down-weighted/pruned.
what can reproduce: A validated causal-mechanism module can be copied into a environment instance with a different exogenous-input distribution.
what can learn: To distinguish genuine causal effects from confounded correlations purely by comparing intervention outcomes to correlational predictions across shifting contexts.
what can transfer: The causal model learned under one distribution of exogenous causes correctly predicts outcomes of interventions under a context/shifted exogenous distribution without retraining.
distinguishing observable: Under a deliberate shift in the environment's exogenous input distribution (context shift), the causally-constrained model maintains prediction accuracy on interventions, while a correlation-only model matched in observational-fit accuracy on the original context shows a sharp accuracy drop after the shift — this differential robustness under distribution shift is the key signature, not in-context accuracy which is matched by construction.
minimal world: A 3-variable causal chain (confounder C -> X -> Y, C -> Y) where the agent can either passively observe (X,Y,C) or actively intervene do(X=x); train an interventional model on a mix of intervention and observation data, and a correlation-only model on observation data alone, matched in observational fit. Intervention: shift the distribution of C (the confounder/context) between train and test and compare both models' accuracy predicting do(X=x) outcomes in the context. Null twin: the correlation-only model, matched in R^2 on original observational data, tested identically under the context shift.

nearest_priors.name: Invariant Causal Prediction (Peters, Bühlmann & Meinshausen 2016) / Invariant Risk Minimization (Arjovsky et al. 2019), combined with Pearl's structural causal models and do-calculus
nearest_priors.explains: Keeping only the mechanisms (edges or predictors) whose conditional stays invariant across environments or interventions, and pruning spurious ones. Robustness of the invariant model under distribution shift while a correlational model fails. Transfer of learned mechanisms to new exogenous distributions. Separating P(Y|do(X)) from P(Y|X) under confounding, which is Pearl's SCM and backdoor adjustment.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: ICP and IRM are usually passive, pooling given environments. Here the agent chooses its own do(X=x) and updates by gradient descent on interventional prediction error. The prediction error is written as |P - y|, loosely mixing a distribution with a sample.

nearest_priors.name: Independent Causal Mechanisms / Sparse Mechanism Shift and meta-transfer learning of causal structure (Schölkopf et al. 2021; Bengio et al. 2019, 'A Meta-Transfer Objective for Learning to Disentangle Causal Mechanisms')
nearest_priors.explains: Mechanism parameters are learned by gradient descent. Correct causal factorizations adapt or stay stable under shifts in the cause distribution while wrong ones do not. Edge confidence is scored by performance across shifted distributions. Modules are reused and copied into new environments.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It uses observed shifts rather than explicit agent-chosen interventions. It does not include a matched-R^2 correlational null twin.

nearest_priors.name: Active causal learning / interventional structure learning with causal reinforcement learning (Eberhardt experiment design; Tong & Koller active Bayesian network learning; causal model-based RL, Dasgupta et al. 2019)
nearest_priors.explains: The agent selects interventions, compares observed outcomes with the model's predictions, and uses the discrepancy with observational correlations to detect confounding.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not in itself emphasize the invariance-across-context test or the matched-fit shift-robustness comparison.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing novel. There are two minor inconsistencies. First, the 'causal chain' is actually a confounded triangle. Second, shifting P(C) also changes the marginal P(Y|do(X)) = Σ_c P(Y|x,c)P(c). The causal model therefore stays accurate only if it models C explicitly, i.e. uses the invariant mechanism P(Y|x,c) and re-weights by the new P(C). Neither point is a new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare against an ICP/IRM learner given the same set of observational environments (different P(C)) but no interventions. If it matches the interventional agent's shift robustness, then active intervention adds nothing beyond standard invariance learning. Also test whether the agent's advantage survives when C is unobserved. Only true interventional data identifies P(Y|do(X)) in that case, whereas invariance across environments may not.

statement: The environment alternates between sparse-observation epochs (favoring generation of many candidate explanations, i.e. abduction-heavy allocation) and dense-verification epochs (favoring exhaustive checking of few candidates); organisms that develop an internal switch reallocating compute between abduction and [X] based on a running estimate of observation density outperform organisms with a fixed allocation.
what exists: observation-density estimator; compute allocator (fraction to abduction vs checking); candidate hypothesis pool; epoch signal (hidden, inferred from density)
what changes: allocator fraction shifts continuously as the density estimator updates; more compute flows to whichever process is currently informative.
what persists: the estimator's running [X] across epoch transitions.
what is selected: organisms whose allocator correlates allocation shifts with true (hidden) epoch identity.
what can reproduce: successful allocator policies are copied with mutation into offspring organisms.
what can learn: the mapping from observed density [X] to optimal allocation ratio is learned online.
what can transfer: the learned density-to-allocation policy transfers to environments with differently timed but similarly structured epoch alternation.
distinguishing observable: task performance of adaptive-allocator organisms remains flat across epoch transitions while fixed-allocation organisms (matched for total compute) show performance dips exactly at transitions.
minimal world: A world alternates every ~50 steps between epochs where observations are 90% missing (sparse) versus fully logged with a complex spec (dense). Intervention: randomize epoch lengths to prevent simple clock-based prediction. Null twin: an organism with a fixed 50/50 abduction/checking compute split, matched for total compute; it underperforms at transitions relative to the adaptive-allocator mechanism.

nearest_priors.name: Adaptive exploration–exploitation control under nonstationary regimes (regime-switching / hidden-Markov environment with belief-state-driven policy, e.g. adaptive epsilon/temperature, Yu & Dayan expected/unexpected uncertainty)
nearest_priors.explains: running estimate of a hidden epoch inferred from observations; continuous shift of allocation between generating candidates (explore) and checking few (exploit); flat performance across transitions vs fixed-policy dips; randomized epoch lengths defeating clock prediction
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: evolutionary copying of allocator policies with mutation; framing as abduction vs verification specifically

nearest_priors.name: Evolution of phenotypic plasticity / bet-hedging vs conditional strategies in fluctuating environments (Baldwin effect, evolved learning rules)
nearest_priors.explains: selection favouring organisms with a cue-driven internal switch over fixed strategies; heritable policies with mutation; online learning of cue-to-response mapping; transfer to differently timed but similarly structured fluctuations
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: the specific compute-allocation content (hypothesis generation vs checking) and the density estimator mechanics

nearest_priors.name: Metareasoning / rational allocation of computation (Russell & Wefald value of computation; algorithm portfolios and adaptive operator selection)
nearest_priors.explains: dividing a fixed compute budget between hypothesis generation and verification according to the estimated marginal value of each process under current conditions
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: hidden epoch inference, evolutionary reproduction, transfer across epoch timings

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little: the pairing of abduction-vs-verification as the two arms is a domain-specific relabelling of explore/exploit or generate/test; evolution + online learning of a cue-conditioned policy is the standard Baldwin/plasticity combination.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Decouple observation density from which process is actually informative (e.g. sparse epochs where verification pays off). A pure density-cue plasticity mechanism would keep shifting on density and fail; a value-of-computation / belief-state controller tracking marginal returns of each process would reallocate correctly.

blind_text:
statement: A relay stage between high-dimensional sensory channels and cortical readout applies per-channel gain controlled by a context/attention signal, so that only task-relevant channels pass through with high fidelity while others are attenuated. The relay's effective information capacity is thus context-dependent rather than fixed.
what exists: multiple independent input channels; thalamic-like relay units with per-channel gain; a context/attention control signal; cortical readout receiving only gated output
what changes: Relay output per channel equals gain(channel, context) times raw input; gain weights are updated by task feedback (reward) to increase for channels predictive of reward in the current context and decrease for irrelevant channels.
what persists: Learned mapping from context to channel-gain pattern (the routing policy).
what is selected: Gain patterns that route task-relevant information through the bottleneck while suppressing irrelevant channels are reinforced by task performance feedback.
what can reproduce: Not applicable.
what can learn: The system learns which input dimensions are relevant per context, effectively learning context-dependent feature selection.
what can transfer: The learned gain-routing policy transfers to tasks sharing relevant-feature structure, enabling rapid re-weighting rather than relearning full representations.
distinguishing observable: Mutual information between full input and cortical readout is context-dependent, tracking task relevance (relevant-channel information preserved/amplified, irrelevant-channel information selectively suppressed), unlike a fixed uniform-attenuation bottleneck that reduces information equally across all channels regardless of task context.
minimal world: Several independent input feature streams, only one relevant per trial given a context cue, feeding a trainable gain layer before a readout trained via reward. Intervention: switch which channel is relevant across blocks and measure gain adaptation and per-channel mutual information. Null twin: a fixed bottleneck applying equal, context-independent attenuation to all channels, tuned to match the same overall output information rate/variance, tested on the same switching task; compare task performance and channel-specific mutual information between the two.

nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Földiák's network learns its lateral weights anti-Hebbianly rather than having them fixed. Explicit overcompleteness and a reconstruction-error objective are not central to it.

nearest_priors.name: Sparse coding via locally competitive algorithm (Olshausen & Field 1996; Rozell et al. 2008 LCA)
nearest_priors.explains: Overcomplete dictionary, inhibition proportional to co-active units' outputs, thresholding, kurtotic activity, edge-like receptive fields, low reconstruction error, and generalization within image statistics.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Olshausen–Field and LCA update all active coefficients by a reconstruction gradient rather than applying Hebbian/Oja updates only to winners.

nearest_priors.name: k-Winners-Take-All competitive learning / Kohonen-style vector quantization (incl. SAILnet, Zylberberg et al. 2011)
nearest_priors.explains: Only winning units update toward inputs, poorly matching units stagnate (dead units), and a sparse set of prototypes forms. SAILnet combines local Oja-like learning with inhibitory competition.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Pure k-WTA or VQ gives a hard assignment with no graded inhibition proportional to activity, and weaker reconstruction by linear superposition.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing. The only open detail is whether the lateral weights are fixed or learned, which is a parameterisation choice within the Földiák/SAILnet family. The PCA-like dense encoder comparison and the divisive-normalization null are standard controls.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Freeze the lateral inhibitory weights versus allow anti-Hebbian lateral learning (Földiák), and swap winner-only Oja updates for a full reconstruction-gradient update (Olshausen–Field/LCA). If the dictionary, kurtosis and reconstruction efficiency stay unchanged, the mechanism is indistinguishable from these priors. Dead-unit rates under the winner-only rule would separate it from LCA.

what is selected: the end candidate minimizing total wedge-violation across all contexts (the universal-property winner)

statement: Synaptic weight changes depend on the precise relative timing of pre- and postsynaptic spikes: potentiation occurs when presynaptic firing reliably precedes postsynaptic firing within a short window, depression occurs for the reverse order. what changes: After each spike pair, weight is incremented or decremented by a kernel value depending on the sign and magnitude of the timing difference (post minus pre).
what persists: The resulting weight matrix, encoding learned temporal/causal precedence relationships.
what is selected: Synapses whose timing pattern is consistent with the neuron predicting the input's causal source are strengthened; anti-causal synapses weaken.
what can reproduce: None; the local rule is applied identically at every synapse in the network.
what can learn: Sequence and causal-order structure in temporally patterned input, enabling prediction of upcoming events.
what can transfer: Learned temporal/causal weight structure supports prediction and pattern completion on sequences sharing the same temporal [X].
distinguishing observable: Weight change sign flips when the order of a fixed spike pair is reversed (timing-order dependence), unlike a rate/correlation-based [X] rule whose weight change depends only on co-firing rate and is insensitive to which spike came first.
minimal world: Two spiking units A and B with a controllable interspike latency; synapse A→B updated via an [X] kernel. Intervention: force A-before-B vs B-before-A timing across trials while holding overall co-firing rate fixed. Null twin: a symmetric [X] rule that updates the same synapse using only the co-occurrence rate of A and B (order-blind), matched in total spike counts and correlation magnitude but producing no order-dependent weight asymmetry.

blind_text:
statement: Each parameter carries an importance trace that accumulates based on how much it has contributed to recent error reduction; mutation noise applied to that parameter is scaled inversely with its importance, so consolidated parameters become resistant to further change. This produces selective protection of previously useful structure during continued mutation/learning.
what exists: parameter vector theta; importance trace c_i per parameter; mutation noise scaled by 1/c_i
what changes: theta_i += noise * g(1/c_i); c_i updated upward when parameter i contributed strongly to recent loss reduction
what persists: high-c_i parameters remain frozen across subsequent mutation rounds
what is selected: mutated variants that reduce loss are retained by an outer hill-climbing/evolutionary loop
what can reproduce: an agent's (theta, c) pair can be copied to offspring, inheriting the importance trace
what can learn: which parameters matter for which task, forming a soft task-relevance mask that guides future plasticity allocation
what can transfer: protection of task-1-relevant parameters transfers to reduce forgetting when learning task 2
distinguishing observable: after sequential training on task A then task B, retention of task-A performance should correlate with parameters' pre-existing c_i and show shallower forgetting than uniform-noise mutation of equal total variance
minimal world: two sequential regression/classification tasks sharing partial structure, evolved via mutate-and-select; intervention: train A, record c_i, train B, retest A; null twin: identical evolutionary loop but with uniform (non-curvature-scaled) mutation noise of equal total variance, matched on task-B learning speed but compared on task-A forgetting.

nearest_priors.name: Synaptic Intelligence (Zenke, Poole & Ganguli 2017): path-integral per-parameter importance for continual learning
nearest_priors.explains: A per-parameter importance trace that accumulates each parameter's contribution to recent loss reduction. Parameters with high importance become consolidated. This selectively protects task-A-relevant weights while task B is learned, which reduces catastrophic forgetting. Retention of task A should correlate with the pre-existing importance values.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: SI protects parameters through a quadratic penalty on gradient-based updates. It does not scale stochastic mutation noise by 1/c_i. It also has no outer mutate-and-select loop and no inheritance of (theta, c) by offspring.

nearest_priors.name: Elastic Weight Consolidation (Kirkpatrick et al. 2017) / Fisher-curvature-weighted consolidation, incl. Laplace-posterior / variational continual learning (VCL, Bayes-by-backprop style posterior variance)
nearest_priors.explains: Importance acts as a precision or curvature measure. In variational continual learning, the per-parameter posterior variance is inversely related to importance. Sampling perturbations with variance proportional to 1/importance is therefore close to sampling from a Laplace or variational posterior. This matches the 'curvature-scaled' language used for the null twin and the soft relevance mask.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: EWC importance is Fisher information, not an accumulated contribution to loss reduction. EWC and VCL are gradient- or ELBO-trained, not hill-climbing evolution. Neither includes heritable importance traces.

nearest_priors.name: Self-adaptive evolution strategies with per-parameter mutation step sizes (Rechenberg/Schwefel (1+1)-ES, sigma-self-adaptation, CMA-ES diagonal; Lamarckian inheritance of strategy parameters)
nearest_priors.explains: An outer mutate-and-select hill-climbing loop in which each parameter has its own heritable mutation scale. Strategy parameters are copied to offspring together with the object parameters. Mutation variance is shaped per coordinate.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: In standard ES, step sizes adapt to maximise progress rate. They are not consolidated toward zero on the basis of past-task contribution for the purpose of anti-forgetting. ES carries no explicit multi-task retention objective.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the specific combination is not covered by any single prior: SI-style contribution-to-loss-reduction importance used as an inverse per-parameter mutation scale inside a mutate-and-select loop, with the importance trace inherited. This splice has been explored in neuroevolution and continual-evolution work, for example importance-weighted mutation in evolved networks. Credit assignment of loss reduction to individual parameters under simultaneous random mutation is not specified; it could plausibly be done by the per-coordinate product of delta-theta and delta-loss. There is a minor inconsistency: the null twin is called 'non-curvature-scaled', but c_i is contribution-based rather than curvature-based.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Build two variants of the same evolutionary loop and match them on total noise variance and task-B learning speed. In the first, compute c_i as the SI path integral, i.e. the accumulated per-parameter product of delta-theta_i and delta-loss. In the second, compute c_i as diagonal Fisher or curvature at the task-A optimum. Also run a third arm that uses SI importance but applies it as a quadratic penalty inside the selection fitness instead of as noise scaling. Then look for parameters where contribution-based and curvature-based importance diverge: high curvature but small traversed path, or large path but flat final basin. If task-A retention tracks path-integral c_i rather than curvature, and noise scaling beats penalty-based protection at equal variance, the mechanism is the described SI-in-ES composite rather than EWC/Laplace posterior sampling.

statement: Two adaptive controllers track the same underlying plant through different reference models; instead of each minimizing only its own tracking error, adaptation is driven additionally by the pullback mismatch: the disagreement between their state estimates once mapped into a shared comparison space via fixed projection maps. This mismatch term couples the two adaptation laws, producing consensus dynamics absent from independently tuned controllers.
what exists: shared plant; controller_1 with reference model_1; controller_2 with reference model_2; fixed projection maps p1, p2 into a comparison space
what changes: each controller's adaptation law updates on its own tracking error plus the term p1(x1)-p2(x2) computed at each step
what persists: the fixed comparison-space projections across the run
what is selected: controller pairs that reduce pullback mismatch fastest are retained/propagated in an ensemble setting
what can reproduce: a converged pair can spawn a merged controller whose parameters are the pullback (limit) of the two
what can learn: the projection maps themselves, if adapted slowly when persistent mismatch remains despite individual convergence
what can transfer: the merged/limit controller generalizes more robustly to plant instances than either individual controller alone
distinguishing observable: convergence speed and noise robustness of the pullback-coupled pair versus a post-hoc simple average of two independently adapted controllers given identical sensor information
minimal world: Two noisy sensors of the same 1D linear plant expressed in different reference-model units, each driving its own adaptive controller. Null twin: identical sensors, plant, and noise, but each controller's adaptation uses only its own tracking error with no cross pullback term, matching total information available while removing the coupling.

statement: A fast, one-shot [X] associative matrix stores each experience immediately and decays quickly, while a slow network is trained only via periodic replay of buffered experiences and changes little per step. experiences are thus available for immediate recall via the fast store, and only become part of the slow store's generalizable [X] after repeated interleaved replay.
what exists: fast weight matrix W_fast; slow weight network W_slow; replay buffer of stored (input,target) patterns with priority tags; decay rate for W_fast
what changes: On each experience (x,y): W_fast <- W_fast + eta_fast * outer(y,x) (one-shot); pattern added to buffer with priority (e.g. surprise/reward); W_fast decays each step: W_fast <- (1-delta)*W_fast; periodically, batches sampled from buffer are used for small gradient updates to W_slow.
what persists: Statistical regularities embedded in W_slow persist indefinitely; individual episodic traces in W_fast persist only transiently.
what is selected: Buffer sampling priority selects which experiences get replayed and thus which patterns are consolidated into W_slow.
what can reproduce: The consolidated W_slow can be copied wholesale into a agent instance as a pretrained initialization.
what can learn: Both immediate one-shot recall (fast store) and slow cross-episode generalization (slow store).
what can transfer: W_slow generalizes to instances of previously-seen categories; W_fast supports recall of the exact specific episode but does not generalize — this dissociation is directly testable.
distinguishing observable: After learning many items sequentially, retention of early items measured via the slow store should remain high (protected by interleaved replay) while a single-weight-matrix online learner without a fast/slow split and without replay (null, matched in total parameter count and per-step update cost) shows sharp catastrophic forgetting of early items as ones are learned.
minimal world: A sequence of pattern-association tasks (e.g. paired associates) presented one at a time; the dual-store model learns each via W_fast immediately and consolidates via periodic replay into W_slow. Intervention: measure recall accuracy on early-learned pairs after many subsequent pairs, with and without replay enabled. Null twin: a single associative matrix updated online on each pair with no replay and no fast/slow split, matched in total learnable parameters and per-example update magnitude, tested identically for retention of early pairs.

blind_text:
statement: An agent's model is trained on both passively observed transitions and transitions it itself causes via action (interventions), with a separate latent flag distinguishing intervention-generated data from observation-generated data during training. This lets the model learn which variable dependencies are merely correlational (only appear in observational data) versus causal (persist when the agent intervenes), enabling correct prediction under interventions never observed passively.
what exists: a set of variables with a true causal graph; an agent that can either observe (do-nothing) or intervene (do(X=x)); a model conditioned on a do/observe flag
what changes: model parameters update via supervised prediction loss over both observational and interventional (state, flag, outcome) triples
what persists: the subset of learned dependencies that hold under do(X=x) for all x, i.e. the true causal parents of each variable
what is selected: predictive submodels that remain accurate specifically on held-out interventions, not just held-out observations
what can reproduce: the causal submodel for one variable can be reused unchanged when composing a graph that shares that variable's parents
what can learn: a structural mapping from parent variables to child variable that is invariant to which distribution (observational or interventional) generated the training data
what can transfer: the learned causal submodel transfers correctly to entirely intervention values not seen during training, and to graphs sharing the same local structure
distinguishing observable: prediction accuracy under a intervention value (not seen in training) should remain high for the flagged causal model, while a purely correlational model trained only on observational data (or trained without the do/observe flag distinguishing the two data sources) should show accuracy collapse specifically on interventional test cases despite matching observational accuracy
minimal world: A 4-variable synthetic causal graph (e.g. A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D) generates observational data plus data from randomized interventions on single variables. Intervention: train two models — one with the do/observe flag and interventional training data, one purely observational — then test both on prediction under a held-out intervention value on B. Null twin: a model trained on a mixture of observational and interventional data but [X] the do/observe flag (data pooled indistinguishably, matched sample count and variable coverage) — this null twin will fit spurious correlations between B and its non-descendant C that the flagged model correctly avoids, producing systematically worse held-out interventional accuracy despite identical training data content.

blind_text:
statement: The control parameter that sets a trophic module's qualitative regime (fixed point, limit cycle, chaos) is not an externally imposed constant but is itself the instantaneous ecosystem energy input rate propagated through conversion efficiencies. As flux crosses thresholds implied by the module's Jacobian, eigenvalues cross the unit circle and true bifurcations occur, so resource pulses are bifurcation forcings rather than mere state perturbations.
what exists: basal energy pool E(t); population states x_i; interaction coefficients a_ij; conversion efficiencies c_ij; energy-dependent growth function r_i(E)
what changes: x_i(t+1)=x_i(t)+x_i(t)[r_i(E(t))-sum_j a_ij x_j(t)]; E(t+1)=E(t)+input(t)-uptake(t); r_i(E) continuously reshapes the community Jacobian, crossing bifurcation thresholds at specific E* values.
what persists: the [X] of the interaction network across the experiment.
what is selected: none; this is a pure forced dynamical law, not a selection process.
what can reproduce: populations via standard density-dependent growth.
what can learn: nothing adapts; the mechanism is purely dynamical.
what can transfer: the bifurcation-threshold structure should transfer across different network topologies sharing the same E(t) schedule.
distinguishing observable: the largest local Lyapunov exponent should show a sharp, theory-predicted discontinuity precisely at E* values derived from linearization, not a smooth drift.
minimal world: A 3-node chain (basal resource, herbivore, predator) with a stepwise input(t) schedule; intervention manipulates input(t) directly while holding A fixed, recording Lyapunov exponent and regime before/after threshold. Null twin: identical equations but r_i held constant while growth rate receives injected noise matched in variance/autocorrelation to the real E(t) trace; the null should show gradual, unthresholded changes in dynamics uncorrelated with the theoretical E* values.

nearest_priors.name: Paradox of enrichment (Rosenzweig–MacArthur) and nutrient-driven bifurcations in chemostat food chains (e.g. Hastings–Powell chaos, Gragnani/Kuznetsov bifurcation analysis of nutrient-prey-predator chains)
nearest_priors.explains: Energy or nutrient supply acting as the bifurcation parameter of a trophic module. Enrichment moves a food chain from a stable equilibrium through Hopf or Neimark–Sacker bifurcations to limit cycles and then to chaos. Thresholds come from the Jacobian of the chain. It also covers the 3-node basal–herbivore–predator minimal world.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The time-varying, pulsed E(t) schedule. The explicit claim that pulses act as bifurcation forcings rather than state perturbations. The proposed transfer of threshold structure across topologies.

nearest_priors.name: Discrete-time Lotka–Volterra / Ricker-type maps with a route to chaos (May 1974/1976; logistic-map period doubling)
nearest_priors.explains: The update rule x_i(t+1) = x_i + x_i[r_i − Σ a_ij x_j]. Growth-rate increases drive eigenvalues across the unit circle, giving flip and Neimark–Sacker bifurcations and chaos. The Lyapunov exponent changes sign at threshold r values.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Why r is a function of a dynamic energy pool rather than a fixed constant. Why the dynamics are coupled to energy input and uptake.

nearest_priors.name: Slowly varying / non-autonomous parameter drift: dynamic (delayed) bifurcations and bifurcation- or rate-induced tipping (quasi-static bifurcation analysis, Scheffer-style regime shifts)
nearest_priors.explains: Treating an internally driven slow variable, E(t), as a moving control parameter. This makes regime changes occur when the frozen-parameter system crosses E*. It also underlies the distinction from matched-noise forcing, which gives no threshold.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It predicts delays or overshoot past the static E*, not a crossing at exactly E*. It does not predict a sharp discontinuity in the Lyapunov exponent: at a Hopf or Neimark–Sacker bifurcation the leading exponent typically passes through zero continuously.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Two predictions go beyond the priors, and both are dubious rather than novel. First, the claim of a sharp discontinuity in the Lyapunov exponent exactly at the linearization-derived E*: exponents generally vary continuously at local bifurcations, and with a moving E(t) the transitions are delayed. Second, the claim that threshold structure transfers across network topologies: Jacobian thresholds depend on topology. Also, because E is a state variable coupled through uptake, the 'bifurcations' are strictly bifurcations of the frozen subsystem, not of the full autonomous system.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Hold input(t) at a sequence of constant levels long enough to reach the attractor, then repeat with ramps at several rates through the predicted E*. Next, test transforms whose rho(T) falls outside the dictionary's represented orbit (e.g. scales with no corresponding atoms). The projection scheme must then either fail or reveal how it defines rho. That separates a true structural law from a finite-orbit approximation.

what changes: R is swept as an experimental parameter; for each R the occupancy tensor is projected onto its best rank-R [X] approximation and the corresponding maxent policy is computed and executed

This follows from capacity-limited channels, where the optimal input becomes discrete and its support shrinks with noise (Smith 1971).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Has no spatial reaction-diffusion substrate. Has no morphogen production/degradation kinetics. Has no developmental copying of the code.

blind_text:
statement: Dictionary atoms are updated by a [X]-style rule whose learning rate is scaled by the inverse of the current [X]-estimated variance of the corresponding coefficient: atoms tied to confidently-estimated coefficients change slowly, atoms tied to uncertain coefficients change quickly. This ties representational plasticity directly to epistemic state rather than to a fixed or error-magnitude-only rate.
what exists: dictionary atom d_i; coefficient variance P_ii; reconstruction residual; learning rate eta_i = g(1/P_ii)
what changes: d_i += eta_i * residual * x_i, with eta_i rising as P_ii rises
what persists: the functional mapping g from variance to learning rate
what is selected: which atoms are actively reshaped at a given time (those tied to uncertain coefficients)
what can reproduce: the variance-gated plasticity rule copies to any dictionary size
what can learn: the dictionary itself, plus the shape of g, via minimizing long-run reconstruction error
what can transfer: the rule transfers across generative processes with differing noise structure without retuning a fixed learning rate
distinguishing observable: when a subset of latent causes becomes noisy, precision-gated learning shows rapid atom reorganization confined to the coefficients whose variance rose, while a fixed-rate [X] rule shows uniform, slower reorganization across all atoms
minimal world: A dictionary-learning task where five of twenty latent causes abruptly become noisier partway through training. Intervention: measure atom drift rate for noisy versus stable causes before and after the change. Null twin: identical [X] update with a fixed global learning rate tuned to match total drift over the whole run, which cannot selectively accelerate drift for the noisy subset.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman-filter learning of weights with Kalman-gain-style adaptive learning rates (Dayan & Kakade Kalman learner; Kalman TD; volatility-sensitive Bayesian learning rates, Behrens et al. 2007)
nearest_priors.explains: Per-parameter step size set by posterior variance, so uncertain quantities update fast and confident ones slowly. Explains faster learning after noise or volatility rises and that no fixed rate needs retuning.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: In standard Kalman learning the gain comes from the variance of the parameter being updated (the atom). Here it comes from the variance of the associated coefficient. The learned monotone mapping g is also not part of it.

nearest_priors.name: Precision-weighted prediction-error learning in hierarchical predictive coding (Rao & Ballard; Friston free-energy / hierarchical Bayesian filtering, Mathys HGF)
nearest_priors.explains: Plasticity of generative weights is gated by precision or variance estimates, and residual × cause-activity is used as a Hebbian-like weight update. Ties learning to epistemic state.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It usually weights by inverse variance, so high-precision errors drive more learning. That sign is opposite to the described 'uncertain → faster' rule, and it does not frame this as selective atom drift.

nearest_priors.name: Olshausen–Field sparse coding / MOD–K-SVD dictionary learning with per-atom adaptive step sizes (RLS-DLA, online dictionary learning of Mairal et al., Adagrad/Adam-style per-coordinate rates)
nearest_priors.explains: The base update d_i += eta * residual * x_i. RLS-DLA and Mairal's method use second-order, covariance-based per-atom scaling. Covers the dictionary-size-independent rule.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Per-atom rates there come from accumulated coefficient energy or gradient statistics, not from a filtered posterior variance of the coefficient. They do not predict selective acceleration for newly noisy causes.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Two minor points. (1) The atom's learning rate is keyed to the coefficient's posterior variance P_ii rather than to the atom's own parameter uncertainty. (2) The mapping g is meta-learned. The description also says 'inverse of variance' while requiring eta to rise with P_ii. That only works if g is decreasing in its argument, which is a wording inconsistency rather than a new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the task with a full Kalman/Bayesian dictionary learner that tracks each atom's own covariance. Make five causes noisier without changing their atoms. The described rule predicts accelerated drift of those atoms because coefficient variance rose. A proper Kalman atom learner predicts slowed atom learning, since noisier coefficients carry less information about the atom. Separately, perturb atoms of stable-variance causes. The Kalman atom learner speeds up after the surprise, while the described rule does not.

blind_text:
statement: Mutation rate applied to each genome parameter is scaled inversely to that parameter's measured phenotypic sensitivity (how much small changes to it perturb fitness-relevant output), producing mutational canalization: high-sensitivity parameters are protected from mutation while low-sensitivity ones are freely explored.
what exists: genome vector g; per-parameter sensitivity estimate s_i (from phenotype simulation); per-parameter mutation rate mu_i
what changes: each generation, s_i is re-estimated by perturbing g_i alone and measuring phenotype output change; mu_i is set as mu0 / (1 + s_i); mutation applied stochastically per-parameter using mu_i
what persists: the genome's underlying causal structure (which parameters map to which phenotype outputs) persists across generations
what is selected: individuals with higher fitness are selected to reproduce; over generations this indirectly selects for genomes whose high-sensitivity parameters have converged to good values
what can reproduce: genomes reproduce with the sensitivity-scaled mutation operator applied to offspring
what can learn: the population as a whole 'learns' (over generations) which parameter regions to protect, encoded implicitly in the converged s_i profile
what can transfer: a canalized genome transplanted into a but related fitness landscape retains protection on its previously-high-sensitivity parameters, biasing subsequent [X]
distinguishing observable: compare rate of fitness loss under random single-parameter knockout between populations evolved with sensitivity-scaled mutation versus uniform mutation rate; canalized populations should show lower fitness variance under knockout despite equal total mutational input
minimal world: A toy genome of 30 parameters mapping through a fixed nonlinear function to a scalar fitness; intervention knocks out (zeroes) one random parameter after 200 generations of [X] and measures fitness drop. Null twin: identical evolutionary setup with uniform per-parameter mutation rate calibrated to produce the same total expected number of mutations per generation, so mutational load is matched but the sensitivity-targeting is absent.

nearest_priors.name: Safe mutation through output sensitivity (Lehman et al. 2018, SM-R / SM-G)
nearest_priors.explains: Nearly all of the update rule. That method estimates, per parameter, how strongly perturbing it changes the phenotype's outputs (by a perturbation probe or by output gradients). It then scales each parameter's mutation magnitude inversely to that sensitivity: high-sensitivity parameters are protected and low-sensitivity ones are explored freely. The sensitivity is recomputed every generation from the current genome, as here. Here the scaling mu0/(1+s_i) is applied to mutation rate rather than step size, which is only a reparameterisation.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The framing as biological 'canalization'. The specific prediction of lower fitness variance under single-parameter knockout, compared against a null with matched mutational load.

nearest_priors.name: Importance-weighted parameter protection (Fisher-information / Elastic Weight Consolidation-style consolidation; natural-gradient step scaling)
nearest_priors.field: Machine learning / continual learning / information geometry
nearest_priors.explains: Protecting parameters in proportion to a measured sensitivity or importance. The transfer claim: when moved to a related landscape, formerly important parameters stay protected, which biases subsequent adaptation.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The population-level, stochastic, selection-based reproduction loop. These methods are gradient- or penalty-based, not driven by mutation rate.

nearest_priors.name: Evolution of mutational robustness / canalization (Waddington; Wagner, Booth & Bagheri-Chaichian 1997; evolvability via self-adaptive per-locus mutation rates, as in ES / CMA-ES self-adaptation)
nearest_priors.explains: The vocabulary and the predicted phenotype: reduced sensitivity to perturbation at important loci, and bias in future exploration. Per-coordinate adaptation of mutation rates is standard in evolution strategies (ES).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: In biology and self-adaptive ES, mutation rates are heritable and shaped by selection. Here they are computed directly from a sensitivity probe, so nothing about protection is genetically inherited or 'learned' by the population.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is mechanistically new. The main residual is a questionable claim rather than a novel mechanism. Because mu_i is recomputed from the genome each generation and is not inherited, the claim that the population 'learns' which regions to protect depends only on where the genome sits on the landscape. Also, sensitivity-scaled mutation does not obviously select for knockout robustness; it may simply let high-sensitivity parameters sit at sharp optima. The predicted lower knockout fitness variance is therefore an empirical conjecture that no prior guarantees. It could even reverse, since uniform mutation imposes stronger selection for mutational robustness (the 'survival of the flattest' effect).
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run three arms with matched total mutational input: sensitivity-scaled mutation, uniform mutation, and uniform mutation with heritable, self-adaptive per-locus rates. After 200 generations, measure (a) fitness variance under random single-parameter knockout and (b) local curvature at the evolved optimum. Safe-mutation theory predicts faster convergence but no built-in reduction in knockout sensitivity. Robustness-evolution theory predicts the uniform arm evolves the flatter optima. If the sensitivity-scaled arm alone shows reduced knockout variance and flatter phenotype maps, the canalization claim goes beyond the safe-mutation prior.

what is selected: Experts that reduce loss for the input cluster routed to them continue to receive that cluster (a self-reinforcing selection loop between router and experts).

blind_text:
statement: A population of agent policies reproduces proportionally to a fitness score computed from lifetime resource accumulation, with offspring inheriting a mutated copy of the parent's parameters; no gradient information is used at all, only differential survival and copying. Adaptive structure accumulates purely from variation plus differential retention, independent of any individual learning within a lifetime.
what exists: a population of N agents each with a parameter vector θ; a fitness score per agent measured over its lifetime; a mutation operator adding Gaussian noise to θ
what changes: each generation, agents are ranked by fitness; top fraction reproduce with mutation, bottom fraction are removed; population size held constant
what persists: parameter subvectors that recur across many independently-mutated high-fitness lineages
what is selected: agents whose θ yields above-median lifetime fitness in the current environment
what can reproduce: any agent above the survival threshold produces 1+ mutated offspring; this is the core reproduction operator
what can learn: the population as a whole 'learns' an environment-appropriate policy across generations; no individual agent updates θ within its own lifetime
what can transfer: a population evolved in one environment, when moved to a structurally similar environment, should show faster re-adaptation than a freshly initialized population (evolved priors transfer)
distinguishing observable: fitness improvement over generations should track a horizontal (population) timescale set by generation count, and re-adaptation speed after an environment shift should be predicted by the ancestral environment's similarity structure — this should occur even when within-lifetime behavior is entirely fixed (no learning), distinguishing it from any within-lifetime learning mechanism which would show improvement within a single agent's lifetime
minimal world: A foraging grid where agent policy is a fixed (non-learning) lookup table mapping local observation to action, fitness = food collected over T steps. Intervention: run N generations of select-mutate-reproduce and measure population-average fitness over generations, then shift the food layout and measure re-adaptation speed relative to a population with shared mutation-rate but randomized (non-inherited) initialization each generation. Null twin: identical selection and mutation machinery but offspring parameters are drawn fresh at random each generation instead of inherited from the parent (i.e., selection without heredity) — if fitness still increases over generations in the null twin, the observed improvement is not due to the mechanism of heritable variation but to some artifact of the selection procedure alone.

parsed.discriminating_intervention: No mechanism beyond a mutation-only truncation GA is claimed. To confirm the heredity attribution, compare three conditions: (a) the GA with inheritance; (b) the null twin, where offspring are drawn fresh at random, which reduces to repeated random search with max-of-N selection each generation, so the population mean should stay flat; and (c) a within-lifetime learning variant, which should improve within a single episode. Any within-lifetime fitness gain in the fixed lookup-table condition would falsify the pure-selection account.

blind_text:
statement: Forcing a [X] solution into [X] format with a fixed variable ordering imposes a Markov-chain conditional independence structure consistent with that order; scanning orderings and recording achievable entropy at fixed bond dimension reveals which ordering aligns with the true generative causal chain, since the true order requires the least bond capacity.
what exists: k discrete variables; a permutation defining [X] mode order; a [X]-MaxEnt model under that ordering at fixed bond dimension; a shared, ordering-independent target constraint set.
what changes: For each candidate permutation, the [X]-format dual-ascent solver is run to convergence, producing an entropy/violation pair.
what persists: The constraint set and bond dimension budget persist identically across all tested permutations.
what is selected: The permutation achieving lowest violation/highest entropy at fixed bond dimension is selected as the inferred causal order.
what can reproduce: The winning ordering seeds a local-search round of neighboring permutation swaps.
what can learn: The procedure learns an ordering hypothesis purely from the entropy-compressibility interaction, with no explicit temporal labels.
what can transfer: An inferred good ordering can be tested as a prior ordering when variables are inserted into an extended chain.
distinguishing observable: Achieved entropy at fixed bond dimension peaks at (or near) the true generative order with a measurable gap to other orderings; a purely correlational criterion (total matched pairwise mutual information) fails to single out the true order distinctly, since many permutations can match the same pairwise correlations without matching chain compressibility.
minimal world: Six binary variables generated by a true Markov chain [X]→...→[X]. Intervention: for many/all permutations, fit [X]-MaxEnt at fixed bond dimension 2 to shared marginal constraints, recording entropy per permutation and checking whether the true order is the maximizer. Null twin: matched-marginal data drawn from a fully symmetric, order-invariant interaction structure; the identical permutation scan should show a flat entropy landscape with no distinguished maximizer.

nearest_priors.name: Mode/orbital ordering optimization for tensor trains (MPS/DMRG site ordering by entanglement or mutual information, e.g. Fiedler-vector or genetic ordering in quantum-chemistry DMRG, and TT-cross variable reordering)
nearest_priors.field: Tensor networks / quantum chemistry / numerical multilinear algebra
nearest_priors.explains: The core idea that a fixed bond dimension makes the achievable fidelity or entropy depend on how variables are ordered along the chain. The best ordering is the one that minimises cut entanglement, which for a true Markov chain is its generative order (up to reversal). Also explains the local-search refinement by swapping neighbouring sites, and why an order-symmetric null gives a flat landscape.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Reading the winning ordering as a causal or generative order, and the explicit comparison against a pairwise mutual-information criterion. Standard DMRG ordering is about computational efficiency, not structure inference, and it does not use a MaxEnt dual-ascent fit to marginal constraints.

nearest_priors.name: Order-based Bayesian network structure learning (Teyssier–Koller ordering search, order-MCMC, Chow–Liu and chain seriation)
nearest_priors.explains: Scoring each variable permutation under a model class tied to that order, picking the best, and refining by swapping neighbouring variables. Also explains inferring order without temporal labels, and inserting new variables into an existing order.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Using the entropy of a tensor-train-constrained MaxEnt fit at fixed bond dimension as the score. Also, Markov-equivalence means a chain is identifiable only up to reversal, a point the description does not state.

nearest_priors.name: Maximum-entropy fitting to marginal constraints by dual ascent / iterative scaling within a restricted model class (Jaynes MaxEnt, Darroch–Ratcliff IPF, low-rank tensor MaxEnt)
nearest_priors.explains: The inner solver: dual ascent on the constraint Lagrange multipliers, and the entropy/violation trade-off when the model class (here bond dimension 2) is too restrictive to satisfy the constraints.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The outer permutation scan and the causal interpretation of the result.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is unexplained. The novel part is repurposing the ordering sensitivity of MPS/tensor-train bond dimension as a causal-order score inside MaxEnt fitting. Two caveats are left unaddressed. First, the score cannot distinguish a chain from its reversal, or tell causal from merely sequential Markov structure. Second, if the constraints are only pairwise marginals, the gap between orderings may come from the model class rather than from the data.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the identical permutation scan with two scores: (a) the tensor-train MaxEnt entropy at fixed bond dimension, and (b) a standard ordering criterion from the priors, namely the sum of adjacent-pair mutual information (Fiedler/seriation) or a BIC order score for a Markov chain. Use data with a chain structure whose pairwise statistics are ambiguous, e.g. a chain that also has a matched-pairwise but non-chain higher-order dependence. If only the bond-limited MaxEnt entropy isolates the true order (and its reversal) while the MI/BIC scores tie, the mechanism adds something beyond ordinary order search. If the scores agree, it reduces to MPS ordering optimisation.

blind_text:
statement: Restricting a model class to those whose joint distribution over a sequence is invariant under permutation of indices forces the representation to factor through a latent parameter with an order-independent mixing distribution (de Finetti representation). This constraint guarantees that inference and prediction from any reordering of the same multiset of observations are identical.
what exists: sequence of observations x_1..x_n assumed exchangeable; latent parameter theta; mixing distribution pi(theta)
what changes: the model is constrained so that p(x_1,...,x_n) is invariant to any permutation of the indices, i.e. it factors as the integral over theta of the product of iid likelihoods weighted by pi(theta)
what persists: the mixing distribution pi(theta), independent of the order in which data arrived
what is selected: models whose joint distribution is order-dependent are excluded from the exchangeable hypothesis class
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: the posterior over theta from any ordering of a fixed multiset converges to the identical result
what can transfer: the learned mixing distribution pi(theta) transfers to predicting exchangeable sequences of different lengths from the same source
distinguishing observable: permuting the order of the same set of observations leaves the exchangeable model's posterior and predictions unchanged, while an order-sensitive alternative (e.g., recency-weighted updating) produces different predictions for permuted versus original orderings of the identical multiset
minimal world: a sequence of coin flips fed into two models: a Beta-Bernoulli exchangeable mixture and a recency-weighted (exponentially discounted) updater; intervention: shuffle the flip order while holding the multiset fixed; null twin: the recency-weighted model, which is the matched non-exchangeable alternative producing order-dependent output on identical data.
