nearest_priors.explains: Nearly all of it. Some nodes are clamped to observed values and reset each iteration. Unclamped nodes update as a weighted average of their neighbours. Clamped nodes are never overwritten by propagation. The clamp set is fixed. Edge weights can be learned to fit the labeled values (Zhu et al. learned the weight hyperparameters by entropy minimization). Clamped values stay exact while unclamped ones drift under perturbed edges.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The epistemological framing (basic vs inferred belief). The time-varying noisy sensor feed, which is a streaming variant of fixed labels. Transfer of the sensor mapping across agent instances is not part of the classic formulation.

nearest_priors.name: Clamped visible units in Boltzmann machines / Hopfield-style constraint satisfaction networks with external input clamping
nearest_priors.explains: Visible units are clamped to data while hidden units settle to a coherent state under weighted connections. Weights are learned so the free-running network matches the clamped statistics. The same architecture can be copied across instances.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Here the update is a deterministic weighted average rather than a stochastic or energy-minimizing settling. Learning here is predictive weight fitting among inferred nodes, not the contrastive clamped/free phases.

nearest_priors.name: Foundationalism vs coherentism, operationalized as Thagard's ECHO explanatory-coherence network (evidence units linked to a privileged clamped unit) versus Haack's foundherentism
nearest_priors.explains: The basic/inferred asymmetry within a single substrate. Coherence pressure propagates over support edges. The contrast with a symmetric coherentist network where observations can be overridden. The null twin is the pure coherentist network.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: ECHO gives evidence units only priority, not strict immunity from revision. The strict architectural clamp and the learned edge weights are not part of ECHO.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing mechanistic. The only additions are that clamped values stream from a noisy sensor rather than being fixed labels, and that the architecture and mapping can be replicated across agents; both are trivial extensions. The distinguishing observable holds by construction, since clamped nodes cannot drift.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Replace the hard clamp with a soft prior: add a strong self-edge or sensor-edge weight to node0 and let it be updated like the others, as in ECHO or regularized label propagation (Zhou et al. local-global consistency). Then scale the injected contradictory edge strength. The described mechanism predicts node0 stays within epsilon regardless of attack strength. Soft-anchoring priors predict node0 deviation that grows smoothly with attack strength relative to the anchor weight.

blind_text:
statement: Each belief-forming process carries a trust score updated by exponential moving average of verified accuracy, and only beliefs from processes above an adaptive trust threshold are admitted into the belief store. This implements reliability tracking of sources rather than reliance on mutual agreement among sources.
what exists: multiple belief-forming processes each with a source id; a trust score per process; a hidden ground-truth generator revealed with delay; an admission threshold
what changes: After each verified outcome, trust_j updates toward 1 if process j was correct and toward 0 if incorrect ([X]); beliefs from j are admitted to the store only while trust_j exceeds the threshold.
what persists: Trust scores persist across episodes as slowly-varying state encoding accumulated track record.
what is selected: Processes with sustained poor track records are progressively excluded from contributing admitted beliefs.
what can reproduce: High-trust processes can be cloned with perturbed parameters to seed a population of candidate heuristics.
what can learn: Both the trust scores and, in an extended version, the internal parameters of each process adapt via the same feedback.
what can transfer: A process's trust score carries over to tasks sharing the same source identity, functioning as a transferable reliability prior.
distinguishing observable: When a block of mutually correlated but jointly biased sources agree with each other against one independently accurate source, the reliabilist agent's admitted-belief accuracy still tracks the independently accurate source over time (trust of biased block decays), whereas an agreement-weighting (coherence-only) agent's accuracy stays anchored to the majority-wrong block.
minimal world: Four sensors report a hidden binary state: three share a correlated bias and one is independently reliable; ground truth is revealed every 10 steps. Introduce the biased block at t=30. Null twin: identical sensor [X] but trust weights fixed at 1 (no update), which is fooled by majority-agreement indefinitely while the reliabilist version's admitted accuracy recovers as biased-block trust decays.

blind_text:
statement: A strongly connected keystone node projects high-dimensional community dynamics onto a low-dimensional attractor manifold, whose effective dimension (participation ratio of Jacobian eigenvalues) is set by the keystone's coupling strength; this compressed representation is causally load-bearing, collapsing when the keystone is removed rather than being a mere statistical artifact.
what exists: N-species state x; interaction matrix A with a designated keystone node; Jacobian J(x) eigenvalue spectrum; effective dimensionality d_eff(t)
what changes: standard dynamics x_{t+1}=x_t+x_t*(r-Ax_t); d_eff(t)=(sum lambda_i)^2/sum(lambda_i^2) is tracked continuously from J(x(t)).
what persists: the low-rank structure of effective community dynamics persists while keystone edges remain intact.
what is selected: none; this is a representation, not a selection process.
what can reproduce: standard population reproduction.
what can learn: an external predictor can reconstruct the trajectory from d_eff-many coordinates while the keystone is present but requires many more after removal.
what can transfer: a predictor trained on pre-removal low-dimensional trajectory should fail to generalize post-removal without retraining/expanding dimensionality.
distinguishing observable: rank-r reconstruction error at fixed r should sharply increase upon keystone removal but not upon removal of a high-biomass, dynamically peripheral decoy node.
minimal world: 8-species community with one strongly-coupled keystone and one high-biomass but weakly-coupled decoy; intervention removes each separately, recomputing d_eff and reconstruction error. Null twin: removal of the biomass-decoy node (matched in biomass/abundance-variance to the keystone) — negligible d_eff change should occur in this null.

nearest_priors.name: Haken's slaving principle (synergetics) and slow/center-manifold reduction, applied to a strongly coupled hub
nearest_priors.explains: Explains how a strongly coupled mode or node enslaves the fast degrees of freedom, so a high-dimensional system collapses onto a low-dimensional attractor manifold. The manifold dimension is controlled by coupling strength. Removing the order-parameter source destroys the reduction, which makes the low-dimensional structure causal rather than merely statistical.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not specify the ecological keystone framing. It also does not supply the particular participation-ratio estimator computed on Jacobian eigenvalues.

nearest_priors.name: Discrete-time generalized Lotka-Volterra dynamics with keystone-species removal (Paine; community-matrix stability analysis in the tradition of May and Levins)
nearest_priors.explains: Supplies the exact update rule x_{t+1} = x_t + x_t(r - A x_t) and the Jacobian/community-matrix analysis. It also supplies the keystone-versus-dominant-biomass contrast: a keystone's effect is disproportionate to its abundance. The removal experiment is standard.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not by itself frame the keystone's role as dimensionality compression or low-rank predictability.

nearest_priors.name: Participation-ratio effective dimensionality with PCA / rank-r reconstruction (neural-population dimensionality; Koopman/DMD low-rank modelling)
nearest_priors.explains: Explains the d_eff = (Σλ)² / Σλ² metric. It also covers the rank-r reconstruction error and the failure of predictors trained on one low-rank regime to transfer after a structural perturbation.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It is normally computed on covariance eigenvalues, not Jacobian eigenvalues. It gives no causal account of why one node sets the rank.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is left unexplained. The combination is gLV dynamics, a keystone knockout, and participation-ratio or PCA dimensionality, read as slaving by a hub. There is one technical wrinkle. A participation ratio computed on Jacobian eigenvalues, which can be negative or complex, is ill-behaved: Σλ can cancel toward zero. It is also not the same quantity as the trajectory rank tested by rank-r reconstruction. Relating the two, for example through the separation between slow and fast eigenvalues, requires an extra assumption. That assumption is standard, not novel.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Vary the keystone's coupling strength continuously instead of removing it. Compare three quantities: (a) the Jacobian-eigenvalue participation ratio, (b) the covariance participation ratio of the trajectory, and (c) the spectral gap between slow and fast eigenvalues. Slaving/center-manifold theory predicts that the reconstruction rank tracks the spectral gap, and hence the trajectory covariance participation ratio. If instead the Jacobian participation ratio independently predicts the rank-r error when the gap is held fixed, the described mechanism adds something beyond the prior. Run a matched-degree hub with weak coupling as a further control.

blind_text:
statement: When an executed concrete perturbation trial produces a sensitivity value that falls outside the sound bound predicted by [X], this soundness violation is treated as a signal that the abstraction is either buggy or the misspecification set is too narrow. The mechanism locally refines the abstract domain (splitting the offending box) until the concrete observation is provably contained, in the style of counterexample-guided abstraction refinement applied to sensitivity bounds rather than program correctness. Refinement is spatially localized to the region of violation, not global.
what exists: a program under [X] with a current partition into boxes; a stream of concrete perturbation trials sampled online; a violation counter per box
what changes: on each violation (concrete sensitivity outside abstract bound), the violating box is split along its widest dimension and re-propagated; non-violating boxes remain unchanged
what persists: the invariant that after refinement, all previously observed concrete trials remain contained within their box's abstract bound
what is selected: refinement targets are selected by violation frequency, concentrating resolution where soundness fails most
what can reproduce: no reproduction; this is a within-lifetime correction process
what can learn: the partition granularity adapts to the true nonlinearity structure of the program, becoming fine where curvature is high and coarse where the program is locally linear
what can transfer: the learned partition can seed the initial partition for a but related program, reducing refinement steps needed
distinguishing observable: the number of refinement steps required to reach zero violations correlates with local curvature of the true function, a relationship undetectable from either [X] alone (no violations to trigger refinement) or [X] alone (no sound bound to violate)
minimal world: A 1D program that is piecewise linear with one hidden high-curvature region unknown to the abstract interpreter's initial coarse box; intervention: sample perturbation trials preferentially near vs. far from the hidden region and compare refinement step counts; null twin: a fixed uniform grid refinement schedule that splits boxes on a timer regardless of violations, matched in total number of splits, which wastes refinement on already-sound linear regions.

nearest_priors.name: Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) combined with input-space box splitting in abstract interpretation (as in branch-and-bound neural network verifiers such as ReluVal, Neurify and alpha-beta-CROWN)
nearest_priors.explains: The partition of the input into boxes. Interval or zonotope propagation of sensitivity or Lipschitz bounds. The loop where a counterexample triggers refinement. Splitting the box along its widest (or most influential) dimension and re-propagating. Localized refinement that leaves other boxes untouched. Finer partitions where the function is more nonlinear.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: In classical CEGAR, refinement is triggered by spurious abstract counterexamples, meaning the abstraction is too coarse. It is not triggered by a concrete observation falling outside a supposedly sound bound. Such a violation signals unsoundness, and splitting a box only tightens the bound, so splitting cannot restore containment. Classical CEGAR also has no online stochastic trial stream, no per-box violation counters, and no transfer of partitions between programs.

nearest_priors.name: Error-driven adaptive mesh refinement / adaptive piecewise-linear approximation (adaptive quadrature, a posteriori error estimation, kd-tree splitting)
nearest_priors.explains: This reading takes the per-box 'bound' as a local linear or Lipschitz model whose error is checked against samples. Under that reading it explains why splitting concentrates where curvature is high and stays coarse where the function is locally linear. It explains why step counts correlate with local curvature. It explains the null twin: uniform refinement wastes splits in linear regions. It explains warm-starting the mesh on a related problem.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The claim of formal soundness. The framing as abstract-interpretation verification of sensitivity.

nearest_priors.name: Falsification-guided / test-guided refinement (property-based or adversarial testing coupled with a verifier, e.g. SYNERGY/DASH, or adversarial-attack-guided splitting in NN verification)
nearest_priors.explains: Using concrete executed perturbation trials to direct where the abstract analysis should refine. Concentrating effort where tests reveal problems. The complementarity of testing and static analysis, where neither alone yields the observable.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific per-box violation-frequency counters. The claimed relation between refinement steps and curvature.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is novel. The main residual is an internal tension rather than new machinery. If the abstract bound is genuinely sound, concrete trials can never violate it, so refinement never fires. If a violation does occur, it reflects a bug or a too-narrow perturbation set, and splitting boxes, which only tightens bounds, cannot restore containment. The mechanism only works if the per-box 'bound' is actually a non-sound local model. In that case it is error-driven adaptive refinement relabelled as CEGAR. Seeding the partition on a related program is ordinary warm-starting.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Inject a controlled unsoundness bug into the abstract transformer in one region, and separately use a correct sound transformer on a function with a high-curvature region. The described mechanism claims that refinement both repairs the bug region and tracks curvature. The CEGAR/adaptive-mesh priors predict two things instead. First, splitting never resolves the bug-induced violations, because tightening cannot contain an out-of-bound point, so refinement diverges there. Second, with the sound transformer, no violations occur and no curvature-correlated refinement appears unless a non-sound local-linear error criterion is used. Observing curvature-proportional, terminating refinement with a verified-sound transformer would indicate something beyond the priors.

blind_text:
statement: A stochastic encoder maps input X to representation Z that is optimized to minimize mutual information I(X;Z) while maximizing I(Z;Y) for a target Y, via a tunable tradeoff parameter beta. This yields a minimal sufficient [X] of X for predicting Y, discarding task-irrelevant variation.
what exists: input X; target Y; stochastic encoder producing Z; decoder predicting Y from Z; tradeoff parameter beta
what changes: Encoder/decoder parameters are updated by gradient descent on L = I(Z;Y) - beta*I(X;Z) (variational bound); beta may be annealed over training.
what persists: The converged encoder mapping, i.e., the learned sufficient-[X] structure of X relevant to Y.
what is selected: Features of X that carry information about Y are retained in Z; nuisance features are selected against.
what can reproduce: Encoder/decoder weights can be cloned onto task instances sharing X,Y structure.
what can learn: A compressed mapping from raw X to task-relevant Z that generalizes across nuisance variation.
what can transfer: Z generalizes to targets Y' depending on the same relevant subset of X.
distinguishing observable: As beta increases, measured I(X;Z) decreases while held-out accuracy on Y plateaus until a critical beta (a rate-distortion curve); a plain [X] trained to reconstruct X shows no such compression-accuracy tradeoff and retains nuisance information regardless of beta-like penalties.
minimal world: X = (relevant_bit, k nuisance_bits), Y = f(relevant_bit). Intervention: vary beta and separately corrupt nuisance bits at test time. Null twin: same architecture trained to reconstruct X ([X]) rather than predict Y, matched capacity, which retains nuisance bits and is disrupted when nuisance [X] shift, unlike the [X]-trained Z.

nearest_priors.name: Variational Information Bottleneck (Alemi et al. 2017), built on the Information Bottleneck method (Tishby, Pereira & Bialek 1999)
nearest_priors.explains: Nearly all of it. It covers the stochastic encoder p(z|x) and the decoder q(y|z). It covers the objective I(Z;Y) - beta*I(X;Z), optimised by gradient descent on a variational bound, with optional beta annealing. It covers minimal sufficient statistics as the ideal solution, the beta-sweep information plane, the phase transition at a critical beta, and robustness to nuisance variation compared with a reconstruction-trained autoencoder.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The 'reproduce' clause (cloning weights onto new task instances) is ordinary weight reuse, not part of IB. 'Accuracy plateaus until a critical beta' is a qualitative claim about behaviour on a sweep, not a theorem.

nearest_priors.name: Beta-VAE / rate-distortion autoencoder (Higgins et al. 2017; Alemi et al. 2018, 'Fixing a Broken ELBO')
nearest_priors.explains: It has the same variational rate term, with beta trading rate I(X;Z) against distortion, and the same annealing. It traces a rate-distortion curve and is structurally the unsupervised twin of VIB.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It uses reconstruction of X as its distortion, so it keeps nuisance bits. That makes it the null twin in the description, not the mechanism itself. It gives no supervised selection toward Y.

nearest_priors.name: Minimal sufficient statistics (Fisher) and invariant/nuisance-free representation learning (Achille & Soatto 2018)
nearest_priors.explains: It explains the target object: the coarsest function of X that preserves all information about Y. It also explains why discarding nuisance information yields invariance to test-time shifts in the nuisance bits, and why the representation transfers to any Y' that depends on the same relevant subset.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It gives no training dynamics, no beta tradeoff and no stochastic encoder.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Essentially nothing. The blanked [X] terms are 'statistic' and 'autoencoder'/'reconstruction'. Weight cloning and transfer to Y' are generic consequences of learning a sufficient statistic, not new mechanism.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Sweep beta on the toy world X=(relevant_bit, k nuisance bits) and estimate I(X;Z) exactly. Standard IB/VIB predicts a specific shape for the information-plane curve: it jumps discretely at a critical beta, with I(X;Z) settling at 1 bit and I(Z;Y) settling at H(Y). If the described mechanism deviated from IB, for example by keeping partial nuisance information at the optimum or by having no discrete transition, that would separate it. Also check that the curve does not change when the variational bound is replaced with exact mutual information.

blind_text:
statement: A token's referent is fixed at an initial contact event ('baptism') with an object and preserved through a causal chain of subsequent uses, independent of any user's current descriptive beliefs about the object. Downstream agents inherit reference by intending to use the token as their source used it, not by matching current properties to a description.
what exists: tokens (names); baptism events linking a token to an object; a transmission graph of agent-to-agent uses; each agent's private, possibly false, property-beliefs about the referent
what changes: Token usage propagates along the transmission graph; property-beliefs update independently within each agent and can drift or become false without breaking the reference chain.
what persists: The reference link (token to originally baptized object) persists through the chain regardless of property-belief drift.
what is selected: Which chains propagate is determined by communicative utility/success, not by descriptive accuracy.
what can reproduce: Tokens replicate via agent-to-agent copying, with associated property-beliefs subject to mutation.
what can learn: Agents can update their descriptive beliefs about the referent from evidence without altering the underlying reference chain.
what can transfer: Reference itself transfers along the social chain even when accompanying descriptions become false or incomplete.
distinguishing observable: Corrupt descriptive beliefs partway through the chain and test joint-reference success in a point-to-referent cooperative task; the causal-chain mechanism predicts continued success despite false beliefs, while a descriptivist null (reference computed fresh from best-matching current description) predicts reference failure once descriptions stop fitting.
minimal world: Simulated agents pass a name-token for object O along a communication chain; a baptizer links the token to O. Later agents receive progressively corrupted descriptions of O but keep using the same token in a joint pointing game. Null twin: agents that recompute the referent each time by matching their current description to candidate objects (no causal chain retained); under description corruption, the causal-chain system maintains successful reference while the descriptivist system's success degrades, isolating the mechanism.

blind_text:
statement: When the empirical cost-to-go deviates from its rank-R tensor reconstruction, the residual is projected onto the rank-1 direction that would most reduce the maxent-regularized control loss (a matching-pursuit step), and this component is appended to the factorization. This differs from generic residual fitting because the direction chosen is constrained to be a valid additional natural-parameter direction for the maxent policy, not merely a variance-maximizing direction.
what exists: current rank-R reconstruction V_R, empirical V_true (sampled), residual tensor E = V_true - V_R, candidate rank-1 direction (u,v)
what changes: a rank-1 term is appended when ||E|| exceeds threshold τ; (u,v) chosen by one step of power iteration on E weighted by the control-loss gradient
what persists: existing components remain frozen once appended, only residual-driven components are added
what is selected: the single rank-1 direction maximizing control-loss reduction per unit added complexity
what can reproduce: components can be merged if their reconstructed contributions overlap beyond a similarity threshold
what can learn: the growing component set is the learned object

statement: An encoder compresses full ecosystem state into a low-dimensional code under a loss requiring the code to support accurate prediction of held-out do-intervention outcomes, not merely next-state prediction. what persists: encoder/decoder weights persist and evolve across training/generations
what is selected: encoders generalizing to held-out do-queries at smaller code size than next-state-only encoders of equal capacity
what can reproduce: the bottleneck architecture and its code-size budget are heritable across organism lineages
what can learn: within-lifetime encoder refinement via gradient descent on causal-sufficiency loss using self-generated do-samples from the organism's own simulator
what can transfer: the compressed causal code transfers to control tasks in modified ecosystems, e.g. a web with an added invasive species
distinguishing observable: at matched code size, causal-sufficiency-trained code predicts held-out do-query outcomes better than next-state-only code, despite equal accuracy on passive factual trajectory prediction
minimal world: A 6-species web with full state observability; two identically-sized encoders are trained on the same trajectory data, one with a do-query prediction loss term and one without. The intervention evaluates both on held-out do-queries. The null twin is the next-state-only encoder, matched exactly in architecture, code size, and training data volume.

statement: Neurons release a diffusible corrective signal proportional to the deviation of their firing rate from a target set-point; this signal diffuses locally and multiplicatively rescales the [X] rate, down where local activity is too high and up where too low. what exists: firing-rate deviation e(x,t) = r(x,t) - r_target; corrective field C(x,t); weight field w(x,t)
what changes: dC/dt = kappa*e - beta*C + D*Laplacian(C) ; dw/dt = eta*(1 - gamma*C)*[X]_term
what persists: the characteristic homeostatic domain size sqrt(D/beta), stable across different [X] rates
what is selected: none — continuous negative feedback, not discrete selection
what can reproduce: the domain-size [X] re-forms identically under resampled activity with the same underlying [X]
what can learn: the network keeps firing-rate deviation bounded while still permitting local [X] differentiation within each domain
what can transfer: the diffusion-length-set domain scale transfers across different target activity levels or input [X]
distinguishing observable: spatial autocorrelation of firing-rate deviation shows a characteristic correlation length matching sqrt(D/beta) independent of input strength, versus a null model using purely local (non-diffusive) synaptic scaling, which shows no spatial correlation structure in deviations beyond single-neuron scale
minimal world: A 2D sheet of neurons receives spatially patchy input drive of varying strength; [X] runs alongside the corrective field. Intervention: C diffuses per the [X] above. Measure spatial autocorrelation length of firing-rate deviation at steady state across different D values. Null twin: same total corrective 'budget' per neuron and same target rate, but corrective scaling computed purely locally per-neuron (synaptic scaling with no diffusion term, D=0) with matched mean correction magnitude — spatial autocorrelation of deviations should collapse to near-zero beyond one neuron's width.

nearest_priors.explains: Neurons emit a diffusible signal driven by their activity. The signal spreads, decays, and integrates over a local neighbourhood. It then rescales excitability or synaptic gain toward a target rate. The result is spatially shared homeostasis that keeps local rate heterogeneity and responsive states, compared against a purely local homeostatic control.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not emphasise one specific predicted observable: an autocorrelation length of rate deviation that tracks sqrt(D/beta) independent of input strength. The multiplicative (1 - gamma*C) gating of a learning-rate term is also a parameterisation choice not explicit in the original.

nearest_priors.name: Synaptic scaling / integral-control homeostatic plasticity (Turrigiano; van Rossum, Bi & Turrigiano 2000)
nearest_priors.explains: Negative feedback on rate error around a set-point, with multiplicative rescaling of weights. This is exactly the D=0 null twin.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It has no spatial coupling, so it cannot produce a domain size or a correlation length.

nearest_priors.name: Linear reaction-diffusion field with screened-Poisson (Yukawa) kernel / volume transmission
nearest_priors.explains: At steady state, D*Laplacian(C) - beta*C = -kappa*e. C is therefore e convolved with a kernel of length sqrt(D/beta). Because the operator is linear, that length is independent of input amplitude, which accounts for the persistence and transfer claims.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It supplies no coupling back to plasticity or firing rates, and no homeostatic set-point.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little remains unexplained. The main open point is whether the closed loop (rates feeding C, C feeding weights, weights feeding rates) keeps the correlation length exactly at sqrt(D/beta). Network recurrence could renormalise the effective length, so 'independent of input strength' holds only in the linear regime. The (1 - gamma*C) factor on an unspecified [X] term is a minor reparameterisation.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Vary D and beta independently while also varying recurrent connection range and input patch size. If the measured deviation correlation length scales strictly as sqrt(D/beta), it is the pure diffusive-homeostasis prior. Deviations that depend on recurrent range, or on input amplitude through nonlinear rate saturation, would show a loop-renormalised length beyond the prior. A pharmacological analogue is to block NO synthase or scavenge extracellular NO and test whether the correlation length collapses to single-cell scale, as in the D=0 null.

statement: Choosing a particular tensor factorization mode (e.g., splitting state into position, velocity, and context factors) implicitly assumes those factors are causally exogenous with respect to the control-relevant coupling; if the true environment couples two of these modes below the chosen [X] rank across them, the maxent-[X] solution will systematically misattribute cost changes to the wrong factor under intervention. what persists: the chosen mode decomposition (position/velocity/context) is held fixed across the γ sweep
what is selected: not a selection process; this is a diagnostic mechanism revealing a structural bias
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: nothing adaptive; γ and R are external experimental controls
what can transfer: the bias-detection protocol (compare factorization-implied attribution to interventional attribution) transfers to any chosen mode decomposition
distinguishing observable: as γ increases beyond what rank R can represent across the velocity-context modes, the factorization's cost attribution to 'velocity' and 'context' should diverge from the true interventional attribution in a specific direction (over-crediting the mode with larger marginal variance), unlike a full-rank (uncoupled-assumption-free) attribution which tracks the interventional truth at all γ
minimal world: A control task where cost depends on a bilinear coupling term γ·(velocity)·(context) plus separable terms; sweep γ from 0 (fully separable, matches low [X] rank across those modes) to large (strongly coupled). At each γ, fit rank-R (R=1) maxent-[X] factorization and compute mode-wise cost attribution; separately perform ground-truth interventions (clamp velocity, vary context, and vice versa) to get the true causal attribution. Null twin: a factorization using rank R equal to the true coupling's rank (R=2, sufficient to capture the bilinear term) fit identically otherwise; this null should track the interventional attribution across all γ, showing the bias is specific to the rank-mismatched mode-choice, not to the factorization method itself.

statement: A fraction f of the quantity lost at each relaxation step leaves the system entirely (dissipation) rather than being conserved and passed to neighbors; the remaining (1-f) is conserved and redistributed locally. Varying f continuously interpolates the system between a strictly critical state (f=0, true power laws) and a subcritical state with a characteristic avalanche size (f>0), providing a control rule that decouples 'has local relaxation dynamics' from 'is actually at the critical point'.
what exists: lattice/network with conserved+dissipated flow at each toppling event; dissipation parameter f
what changes: At each toppling event, (1-f) of excess is redistributed to neighbors, f is removed from the system (dissipated).
what persists: Total conserved mass in the system decays according to f over long timescales unless replenished by drive; the ratio f itself is fixed as a world parameter for a given run.
what is selected: N/A - this is a parameter sweep, not a selection process.
what can reproduce: N/A.
what can learn: N/A in minimal form (this isolates a world-rule variable rather than a learning process).
what can transfer: The relationship between f and the avalanche cutoff scale should be a universal curve independent of lattice size (finite-size scaling collapse), which is the transferable signature.
distinguishing observable: A finite-size scaling collapse of avalanche-size distributions across different f and system sizes N onto a single curve when rescaled by a characteristic size that diverges as f -> 0; absence of such collapse would indicate the power-law-like appearance is a finite-size artifact rather than genuinely governed by the conservation/dissipation rule.
minimal world: Same [X] lattice as mechanism 1, but toppling redistributes only (1-f) of excess to neighbors and discards f. Sweep f in {0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3} and N in {32,64,128,256}; test finite-size scaling collapse. The null twin keeps f=0 (full conservation) always, but instead randomly discards mass at drive-injection time (unrelated to toppling) at rate f — matching total dissipated mass but not making dissipation contingent on relaxation events, which should fail to produce the systematic cutoff-vs-f relationship.

blind_text:
statement: The inference system applies default rules of the form 'if A then normally B,' licensing conclusion B from A alone, but any subsequently established more-specific exception rule overrides the default and retracts B without treating the original inference as ever having been false. This differs from monotonic reasoning, where additional premises can only add to, never remove, prior conclusions.
what exists: a rule base of defaults (A ⇒normally B) and exceptions (A∧C ⇒ ¬B); a working memory of currently licensed conclusions; a specificity ordering between rules
what changes: As facts accumulate, the conclusion set is recomputed by applying the most specific applicable rule; adding fact C can retract a previously licensed B with no contradiction generated.
what persists: Conclusions persist only as long as no more specific overriding rule becomes applicable; the rule base itself is stable background structure.
what is selected: Among competing applicable rules, the most specific one is selected to fire.
what can reproduce: Rule sets can be duplicated across agent instances for population-level testing.
what can learn: Specificity ordering and rule strengths can be tuned from observed override frequency, learning which defaults are unreliable.
what can transfer: Default rule sets learned in one environment can transfer to a structurally similar environment and still produce correct nonmonotonic retraction there.
distinguishing observable: Present sequences where a general cue predicts B, followed later by an exception cue; measure whether belief in B drops sharply to zero (defeasible retraction) versus a graded residual posterior under a strict monotonic [X] updater that treats the exception merely as additional evidence.
minimal world: A bird-world where agents observe a 'has-wings ⇒ flies' default, with some agents also possessing a 'penguin' exception feature. Feed 'has-wings' first (system infers flies), then reveal 'is-penguin.' The defeasible system cleanly retracts 'flies'; the null twin is a continuous weighted [X] classifier over the same features with no explicit override structure, matched for aggregate population accuracy but differing in single-case retraction sharpness and order-of-evidence sensitivity.

nearest_priors.name: Default logic / nonmonotonic reasoning with specificity (Reiter defaults; inheritance networks with exceptions, e.g. Touretzky's inferential distance; Tweety/penguin example)
nearest_priors.explains: Defaults 'A normally B', exception rules A∧C⇒¬B, specificity-based override, retraction of B on learning C without contradiction, the contrast with monotonic logic, and the bird/penguin minimal world (which is the canonical example).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Tuning rule strengths from observed override frequency, population-level duplication of rule sets, and transfer across environments. These are add-ons, not part of the core formalism.

nearest_priors.name: Production systems with conflict resolution by specificity plus truth maintenance (OPS5/Soar specificity ordering; Doyle's JTMS)
nearest_priors.explains: Working memory of licensed conclusions, selection of the most specific matching rule to fire, and dependency-directed retraction when the justification is defeated. Soar and ACT-R style utility learning covers tuning rule strengths from experience.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The formal semantics of 'normally'. It also does not supply the contrast with a Bayesian null model by itself.

nearest_priors.name: Probabilistic / ranking-based defaults (Pearl's System Z, Adams' ε-semantics, Kyburg's reference-class specificity, Bayesian naive classifier as null)
nearest_priors.explains: The specificity preference (narrowest reference class), learning default reliability from frequencies, and the weighted-classifier null twin with graded posteriors.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The sharp all-or-none retraction to zero. A graded model predicts residual belief unless the conditional probability is extreme.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Only the peripheral wrapping: population-level replication of rule sets and cross-environment transfer. Learning specificity orderings from override frequency is standard rule-utility or inductive-logic-programming learning. No novel core mechanism remains. Note that '[X]' in the null model is plausibly 'Bayesian'.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Present the exception cue first, then the general cue, and compare the result with the reverse order. Also give probabilistic exception features, for example 'penguin with 90% confidence'. Classical default logic with specificity is order-independent in its final extension and yields all-or-none retraction. A Bayesian classifier is also order-independent but graded. Any order sensitivity would therefore point to a production-system or belief-revision implementation rather than pure default logic. A thresholded ranking system (System Z) would show retraction that is sharp but threshold-dependent.

blind_text:
statement: The problems of state estimation from noisy partial observations and of [X] given full state knowledge can be solved by two independent modules, and combining them (estimator output feeding the full-information optimal controller) is itself optimal for the joint stochastic control problem. Under linear-quadratic-Gaussian conditions this licenses a strict architectural split into estimator and controller with zero performance loss, meaning modularity here is free rather than an approximation.
what exists: plant state x; noisy observation y; estimator module producing x̂; controller module mapping x̂ to u; combined closed loop
what changes: estimator recursively updates x̂ from y independently of the controller; controller computes u = -L x̂ where L equals the full-information optimal gain
what persists: the independence of estimator design from controller design persists as a structural invariant across horizons and realizations
what is selected: among all possible combined architectures, the separated [X] solution is selected as matching the cost of the infeasible full-information optimum
what can reproduce: the module pair can be reused: swap in a controller gain L' for a different cost weighting without redesigning the estimator, and vice versa
what can learn: each module can be adapted independently (noise [X] vs cost weights) without cross-interference
what can transfer: an estimator trained under one objective transfers unchanged to a controller with a different objective
distinguishing observable: total closed-loop cost of the separated architecture exactly equals the full-information optimum; a jointly co-trained observation-to-action mapping with matched parameter count generically costs more or requires full retraining when the objective changes
minimal world: linear scalar plant with Gaussian process/observation noise and a standard [X] cost. Intervention A: [X] filter plus [X] gain combined. Null twin B: a single end-to-end trained mapping from observation history to action, matched parameter count and training data. Measure cost under the original objective, then change the cost weighting: A only needs the controller gain updated (estimator untouched) and matches theoretical optimum; B needs full retraining and shows a performance drop before retraining.

nearest_priors.name: Separation principle / certainty-equivalence in LQG control (Kalman filter + LQR gain)
nearest_priors.field: Stochastic optimal control theory (Joseph & Tou 1961, Wonham 1968, Kalman)
nearest_priors.explains: Everything central. The estimator (Kalman filter) is designed from the noise covariances alone. The controller u = -L x̂ uses the deterministic LQR gain from the Riccati equation. Their composition is optimal for the partially observed LQG problem. Estimator and controller design are independent: the dual Riccati equations are decoupled. Cost weights can be swapped without touching the filter, and noise models without touching the gain. The [X] slots read as 'optimal control', 'covariances', 'LQG', 'Kalman' and 'LQR'.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The claim that separated cost 'exactly equals the full-information optimum' is false under the prior. LQG cost equals LQR cost plus an irreducible estimation-error term (trace of P times the weighted L'RL term). Separation is optimal among output-feedback policies; it does not recover the full-information cost.

nearest_priors.name: Certainty-equivalence principle (Simon 1956, Theil 1957)
nearest_priors.explains: Replacing the unknown state with its conditional expectation inside the deterministic optimal policy is optimal under quadratic cost and linear dynamics. This explains u = -L x̂ with the full-information L.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It does not specify the recursive Gaussian estimator, the dual Riccati structure, or the reuse and transfer framing for the modules.

nearest_priors.name: Modular vs end-to-end learning comparison (e.g., model-based vs model-free RL, world-model/policy factorisation)
nearest_priors.explains: The null twin B (end-to-end observation-history-to-action mapping) and the prediction of retraining cost when the objective changes. Factored representations transfer across reward changes, similar to successor representations and model-based RL.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It gives no exact optimality guarantee. The zero-loss claim comes only from the LQG structure.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing mechanistic is unexplained. One stated observable is incorrect: separated LQG does not equal the infeasible full-information (LQR) cost. It is optimal only among policies using the observations, with a strictly positive estimation penalty whenever observation noise is nonzero. The end-to-end comparison B is an ML benchmark framing, not a new mechanism. With sufficient capacity and data, B could in principle learn the same optimal linear map (Kalman filter feeding the gain); its deficit is only in transfer across objectives.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: In the scalar plant, compute the closed-loop cost for (i) LQR with true state, (ii) Kalman filter feeding the LQR gain, and (iii) the best output-feedback policy found by exhaustive search over causal linear filters of the observation history. Standard separation predicts (ii) = (iii) > (i), with a gap equal to the estimation-error term that grows with observation noise variance. The described mechanism's claim that (ii) = (i) would be refuted. Also, vary the cost weights and confirm that the Kalman gain stays invariant while only L changes.

what is selected: networks balancing task performance against wiring cost, favoring modular decompositions of function

The literature also covers stationarity and tracking penalties that depend on M and uneven convergence across coefficients.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It is normally framed for LMS/RLS weight vectors rather than for Kalman state correction with an innovation vector K_t r_t. It does not explicitly frame the per-dimension 'neglect signature' as the diagnostic observable. Online adaptation of M against a tracking-error/cost trade-off is less standard.

nearest_priors.name: Kalman filter with partial or constrained updates (Schmidt–Kalman 'consider' filter, partial-update Kalman filter, sensor/measurement scheduling, event-triggered estimation)
nearest_priors.explains: Some state components deliberately receive no correction and carry their prediction forward. Estimation under communication or bandwidth budgets. Resulting error growth concentrated on the unupdated or rarely scheduled components. Adaptive triggering thresholds that trade tracking error against update cost.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Consider-state and partial-update filters usually fix which states are frozen in advance, and scheduling selects measurements rather than state dimensions. Neither uses a dynamic top-k-by-innovation-magnitude mask on the state correction itself.

nearest_priors.name: Top-k gradient sparsification / greedy coordinate descent (Gauss–Southwell rule)
nearest_priors.explains: Choosing the k largest-magnitude components of the update vector each step under a hard bandwidth limit. Winner-take-most competition among coordinates. Starvation of coordinates that are rarely selected, which motivates error feedback.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It has no Bayesian filtering context: no prediction step, no gain, and no observation model. The tracking-error signature in a linear-Gaussian dynamical system is not addressed.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is unexplained. The specific pairing of M-max/top-k selection with the Kalman innovation vector K_t r_t is a straightforward composition, as is the proposed matched-average-error null twin used to expose non-uniform 'neglect' error. The description also leaves unstated how the covariance is updated for masked dimensions (full Joseph update versus prediction-only), and that choice affects the behaviour.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run the 10-dimensional system and compare top-k innovation gating against a partial-update Kalman filter whose update set is fixed or round-robin with the same budget k. Under top-k gating, error should concentrate on dimensions whose innovations are systematically small, such as low process noise or low gain. Round-robin should give roughly uniform, periodic error across dimensions. Compare also against a fixed-subset (Schmidt-style) filter, which should show error confined exactly to the frozen subset. Adding error feedback (accumulating unapplied corrections) should eliminate the neglect signature only if the mechanism is plain M-max selection without memory.

blind_text:
statement: Candidate policies or programs are ranked not by expected reward but by the width of their soundly abstracted worst-case output envelope under a fixed perturbation budget, computed via [X] rather than sampling. Selection favors small-envelope candidates even when their sampled point-performance is inferior to a large-envelope candidate. This exposes a robustness-first regime that is invisible to any selection rule using only executed trajectories.
what exists: a population of small programs mapping inputs to outputs; an abstract domain (interval or zonotope) transfer semantics for each program; a fixed perturbation budget epsilon defining the input uncertainty set; a fitness register per program
what changes: each generation, every program's abstract output envelope under epsilon is recomputed via [X]; fitness is set to negative envelope width (not sampled mean reward), and reproduction probability follows fitness
what persists: the perturbation budget epsilon and the abstract domain choice persist across generations
what is selected: programs with the tightest sound worst-case envelope, independent of their concrete sampled performance
what can reproduce: programs above a fitness threshold produce offspring via parameter mutation
what can learn: the population's average envelope width decreases over generations as an emergent robustness trend
what can transfer: envelope-minimizing structural motifs (e.g., saturating nonlinearities) transfer to task distributions under the same epsilon
distinguishing observable: the selected population's worst-case concrete performance under held-out adversarial perturbations exceeds that of a population selected by sampled mean reward alone, even though the reward-selected population has higher average reward
minimal world: Ten small piecewise-linear programs with tunable slope parameters map a scalar input to a scalar output; intervention: apply an unseen adversarial perturbation from within epsilon after selection and measure worst-case output deviation; null twin: a population selected purely on Monte Carlo sampled mean reward using the same number of forward evaluations, matched in compute, which lacks any soundness guarantee and shows larger worst-case deviation.

nearest_priors.name: Certified or provable robustness training via abstract interpretation (DiffAI, Mirman et al. 2018; Interval Bound Propagation, Gowal et al. 2018; CROWN-IBP and zonotope-based DeepZ/DeepPoly verification)
nearest_priors.explains: Sound interval or zonotope transfer semantics give a worst-case output envelope under an epsilon-ball. The envelope width, or a worst-case bound, is used as the optimization objective instead of sampled loss. It also explains why saturating or low-slope motifs are favoured, why certified models beat empirically trained models on worst-case adversarial deviation while having lower clean or average accuracy, and why this happens with epsilon and the domain held fixed.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Optimization is population-based evolutionary selection with fitness-proportional reproduction and parameter mutation, not gradient descent. Fitness is pure negative envelope width with no task-performance term.

nearest_priors.name: Genetic programming / evolutionary algorithm with fitness-proportional selection and mutation
nearest_priors.explains: A population of small programs, a fitness register, a selection threshold, mutation-only offspring, and a declining average objective across generations presented as an emergent trend.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The source of the fitness signal: sound abstract-domain envelope computation instead of executed evaluations.

nearest_priors.name: Robust (minimax / worst-case) optimization and robust evolutionary algorithms (Ben-Tal & Nemirovski; Tsutsui & Ghosh robust GA; interval-arithmetic fitness in evolutionary design)
nearest_priors.field: Operations research / robust design / interval analysis
nearest_priors.explains: Candidates are ranked by worst-case behaviour over an uncertainty set rather than by expected performance. This yields the trade-off of a lower mean for a better worst case. Interval arithmetic gives guaranteed enclosures.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific use of the zonotope abstract-interpretation formalism from program analysis, and the framing of transfer of structural motifs.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little is unexplained. The mechanism is an evolutionary search whose fitness is a certified interval or zonotope robustness bound, meaning [X] is abstract interpretation or bound propagation. One oddity is that fitness ignores the task entirely, so the global optimum is the constant (zero-slope) program. The 'robustness-first regime' is therefore largely a degenerate consequence of the objective, not a new phenomenon. The claim that it is 'invisible to trajectory-only selection' holds only in the sense that sampled evaluation cannot give sound bounds. That point is already standard in the certified-robustness literature.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare against IBP- or DiffAI-style certified training with an added task term. Run gradient-based certified training on the same piecewise-linear family with the same epsilon and domain, and also a GA whose fitness is the certified bound plus the task loss. If the pure-envelope GA's advantage in held-out adversarial worst-case deviation matches that of certified training at matched envelope width, the evolutionary wrapper adds nothing. Separately, check whether selected programs collapse toward slope 0. If they do, the reported regime is objective degeneracy and not a distinct selection mechanism.

This selection step prevents weight degeneracy and keeps the particle population an effective approximation of the true posterior under nonlinear, non-Gaussian dynamics.

what changes: particles propagate under the dynamics model, weights are updated by observation likelihood, and particles are resampled proportional to weight (with jitter) when effective sample size drops below a threshold
what persists: the particle population as an evolving empirical approximation to the posterior
what is selected: particles whose state predicts the observed data well survive and are copied; low-likelihood particles are eliminated
what can reproduce: high-weight particles are duplicated during resampling
what can learn: the population-level estimate of the hidden state improves in accuracy as effective particle diversity is maintained across nonlinear regimes
what can transfer: a converged particle cloud can seed (warm-start) a filter tracking a related but shifted dynamical regime
distinguishing observable: effective sample size stays bounded and tracking error remains low with resampling, while a matched importance-sampling scheme without a resampling/selection step shows exploding weight variance and estimator collapse (particle degeneracy) on the same observation sequence

nearest_priors.explains: Weighted particle population approximating the posterior; propagation through the transition model; likelihood weight update; multinomial/systematic resampling proportional to weight when ESS drops below a threshold; jitter (roughening) to preserve diversity; the known contrast with plain SIS, which degenerates with exploding weight variance; the bearings-only tracking benchmark (the original Gordon et al. test case); recovery after a regime change.

blind_text:
statement: A generative agent scales its learning rate for each error channel by a running estimate of that channel's inverse noise variance (precision), rather than using a fixed learning rate. High-precision (reliable) prediction errors drive larger weight updates; low-precision (noisy) errors are down-weighted. Precision estimates themselves update on a slower timescale from observed error variance.
what exists: prediction units producing ŷ_t per channel; observations y_t per channel; error e_t = y_t - ŷ_t; precision estimate π_t per channel ([X] of inverse error variance); weights w
what changes: Δw = η_base · π_t · e_t · input; π_t updated by [X] of 1/var(e_t) over a trailing window, on a slower timescale than w.
what persists: weights and per-channel precision estimates carry over across trials and episodes
what is selected: error signals from historically reliable channels come to dominate weight updates; noisy channels are progressively discounted
what can reproduce: not applicable (single-lifetime mechanism)
what can learn: the agent learns to reallocate effective learning rate across channels as their reliability changes over time
what can transfer: a channel's learned precision estimate transfers to tasks that reuse the same sensory channel, giving faster re-adaptation
distinguishing observable: when the noisy/reliable channel identity is swapped mid-experiment, the precision-weighted agent's per-channel update magnitude inverts to track the noise pattern within a short window, while a fixed-learning-rate agent shows no such reallocation despite matched average error
minimal world: Two-channel prediction task where each channel emits a linear signal plus channel-specific Gaussian noise; noise levels between the two channels are swapped at a fixed trial. Intervention: the swap itself. Null twin: identical architecture and error signals but π_t clamped to 1 (constant learning rate), matched average error and reward [X], differing only in whether learning rate is reallocated after the swap.

nearest_priors.name: Precision-weighted prediction error learning (predictive coding / active inference; Friston, Feldman & Friston 2010; hierarchical Gaussian filter, Mathys et al. 2011)
nearest_priors.explains: Error units weighted by estimated inverse variance; weight updates proportional to precision × prediction error; precision learned on a slower timescale; a noisy channel's errors are down-weighted; reallocation after a noise swap
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The HGF derives precision updates from a Bayesian hierarchy rather than a trailing-window moving average of 1/var(e), so the described estimator is a heuristic approximation to it

nearest_priors.name: Kalman filter / Kalman gain as an adaptive learning rate (also inverse-variance cue combination)
nearest_priors.explains: The update step scales with the relative reliability of each observation channel; noisier sensors get smaller gain; adaptive noise estimation (Mehra; innovation-based adaptive KF) estimates R from the empirical innovation variance over a window
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: It applies to state estimation rather than weight learning by a delta rule; the standard KF gain uses the ratio of prior to observation uncertainty, not raw precision multiplied by a base rate

nearest_priors.name: Per-parameter adaptive learning rates (RMSProp/Adam, delta-bar-delta, IDBD; Sutton 1992)
nearest_priors.explains: Per-channel learning rates driven by running second-moment estimates of error signals, adapted on a slower timescale, carrying over across trials
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: RMSProp divides by the RMS of the gradient, so noisy channels get normalised steps rather than being suppressed as unreliable; it is not a reliability weighting of the error by inverse noise variance

parsed.unexplained_residual: Little remains. The only extras are the trailing-window moving-average estimator of 1/var(e), a crude approximation to HGF volatility or precision learning, and the claim that the precision estimate transfers across tasks, which is standard persistence of a sensory-channel noise model.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Compare against a full HGF or Bayesian precision learner after the swap. The described agent's re-adaptation latency should be fixed by the window length, whereas the HGF adapts faster when estimated volatility is high. Separately, add a mean-shift (bias) to one channel without changing its noise: raw 1/var(e) will treat the resulting large systematic errors as low precision, while a model that separates noise from prediction mismatch will not.

blind_text:
statement: Avalanche fronts propagate through a medium whose local propagation rule switches discontinuously depending on which side of a phase boundary the local order parameter sits on: on the disordered side topples cascade freely, on the ordered side topples are absorbed after one step. Because avalanches themselves deposit stress that nudges the local order parameter, avalanche fronts become the mechanism that pins the phase boundary's spatial location, producing an interface that wanders subdiffusively rather than either freezing or diffusing freely.
what exists: order-parameter field φ_i ∈ {ordered, disordered} per site; stress field h_i; an explicit boundary interface position; propagation rule R(φ_i) that differs by phase
what changes: topples follow [X] rule but only propagate to neighbor j if φ_j = disordered; every topple also has probability p to flip φ_i toward disordered proportional to local stress released.
what persists: the total count of ordered vs disordered sites drifts slowly; the interface remains a well-defined 1D (or 2D) boundary at all times.
what is selected: none; interface position is an emergent order parameter tracked, not selected.
what can reproduce: not applicable.
what can learn: not applicable at this level (no adaptive weights); the interface position functions as an implicit memory of past avalanche history.
what can transfer: the pinning-interface roughness exponent should be invariant to lattice size and driving rate, testable as a transferable universality class.
distinguishing observable: interface width scales as t^β with anomalously small β (subdiffusive, avalanche-pinned) compared to a null twin where φ flips randomly with matched flip rate but is decoupled from avalanche propagation, giving ordinary random-walk interface scaling t^{1/2}.
minimal world: a 1D strip [X] with a binary phase label per site controlling topple propagation; intervene by decoupling flip probability from local stress release (null twin uses the same average flip rate but drawn independently of avalanches); measure interface width growth exponent in coupled vs decoupled runs.

nearest_priors.name: Sandpile–interface depinning mapping (Paczuski–Maslov–Bak; Sneppen model; quenched Edwards–Wilkinson / Alava–Narayan SOC–depinning correspondence)
nearest_priors.explains: Avalanche dynamics that advance and pin an interface. Subdiffusive, anomalously rough interface motion with a universal roughness/growth exponent β that is independent of lattice size and driving rate. The interface position acting as a record of past avalanche history.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The explicit binary phase label that switches the toppling rule. In these models the pinning comes from quenched disorder, not from a phase field that avalanches themselves write.

nearest_priors.name: BTW / Manna sandpile on a diluted or heterogeneous lattice (dissipative or absorbing sites; SOC with site-dependent toppling rules)
nearest_priors.explains: Topples cascade freely through 'disordered' (active) sites and are absorbed after one step at 'ordered' (dissipative) sites. Stress field h_i with threshold toppling and a site-dependent propagation rule R(φ_i).
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Feedback in which avalanches convert sites and so move the absorbing/active boundary. Interface roughening exponents.

nearest_priors.name: Coupled SOC–coarsening, or absorbing-state interface dynamics (conserved directed percolation / Dickman–Vespignani–Zapperi absorbing-state SOC; voter/Glauber interface wandering as the null)
nearest_priors.explains: A two-phase field with a moving boundary. A null twin with decoupled random flips gives random-walk (t^{1/2}) wandering. Activity spreading only into the active phase. Emergent, slowly drifting phase fractions.
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The specific stress-release-proportional flip rule that couples avalanche size to boundary motion.

parsed.unexplained_residual: The self-written pinning landscape. The phase label that gates avalanche propagation is itself flipped by avalanche stress release, so the 'disorder' pinning the interface is dynamically generated rather than quenched. This resembles self-organized depinning, but it is not a standard named model. Flips are described as only 'toward disordered', which implies net drift rather than pure wandering; this is a mild inconsistency with the claimed slow two-way drift.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Freeze the φ field after a warm-up period and replace it with a quenched random φ landscape that has the same spatial statistics. Then compare β and the interface roughness exponent between two runs: the coupled, self-written landscape versus the quenched-disorder depinning model. If the exponents match quenched EW/Sneppen values, the mechanism reduces to standard depinning. A distinct β, or a dependence on the flip-probability coupling p, indicates the feedback defines a new class.

statement: The system begins with decomposition rank R=1 and increases R by one whenever residual reconstruction error fails to decrease over a training window, progressively adding representational capacity only when the current capacity is exhausted. This yields a developmental trajectory from coarse to fine-grained multilinear structure.
what exists: a current rank R; R sets of per-mode factor vectors; a residual-error history buffer; a growth threshold
what changes: factor vectors are trained at the current rank; when the smoothed residual-error slope falls below the growth threshold, a rank-one component is appended with small random initialization.
what persists: previously learned rank-one components persist and continue to be fine-tuned after components are added.
what is selected: components that continue to reduce residual error survive fine-tuning; the growth event itself is triggered by a plateau, not chosen by an external supervisor.
what can reproduce: a converged low-rank component set can be copied as the starting point (initialization) for a related tensor.
what can learn: an appropriate final rank for a given data-generating process, discovered rather than pre-specified.
what can transfer: the growth schedule (plateau-length before adding rank) transfers across different tensor tasks as a general capacity-allocation policy.
distinguishing observable: final rank and error-vs-training-time curve should show step-like drops at growth events correlated with plateau detection; compare to a fixed-rank model matched for final parameter count, which shows a single smooth descent with no step structure and may over/under-fit depending on whether R was guessed correctly.
minimal world: Generate a tensor from a true rank-3 [X] structure plus noise. statement: The agent stores a successor representation M(s,s'), the expected discounted future occupancy of state s' starting from s, learned independently of any specific reward function via [X] updates. Value is computed by combining M with a separately-learned reward weight vector, V(s) = M(s,:)·w_R. Because transition structure and reward are factorized, a change in reward function requires relearning only w_R, not M.
what exists: discrete states s; successor matrix M(s,s'); reward weight vector w_R; [X] error signals for both M and w_R
what changes: M(s,:) += α[onehot(s) + γM(s',:) - M(s,:)] on each transition; w_R updated by regression against observed rewards
what persists: M persists unchanged across reward-function changes as long as transition dynamics are stable
what is selected: frequently traversed, reward-relevant successor paths accumulate higher weight in M
what can reproduce: not applicable
what can learn: fast revaluation: after reward relocation, correct value estimates for all states follow immediately from re-fitting w_R against the unchanged M
what can transfer: M transfers across any task sharing the same environment dynamics but different reward functions
distinguishing observable: after moving the reward to a but previously-visited location, the successor-representation agent reaches optimal policy within very few trials (one-shot revaluation), whereas a model-free [X]/Q-learning agent with matched learning rate and prior performance requires many trials to relearn values via renewed exploration
minimal world: Gridworld with fixed transition dynamics and two candidate reward locations; train agent to convergence with reward at location A. Intervention: relocate reward to location B (already explored, distinct successor profile) with no further changes to walls/transitions. Null twin: a model-free [X]/Q-learning agent with matched state-action visitation history, learning rate, and pre-switch performance, which lacks the factorized M/w_R structure and must relearn values from scratch after the switch.

nearest_priors.name: Successor representation learned by temporal-difference updates (Dayan 1993; Momennejad et al. 2017; Gershman 2018)
nearest_priors.explains: M(s,s') as expected discounted future occupancy; the TD update M(s,:) += α[onehot(s)+γM(s',:)−M(s,:)]; the linear value decomposition V = M·w_R; w_R fitted by regression against observed rewards; fast reward revaluation; transfer across tasks that share dynamics; greater reward-revaluation sensitivity than model-free TD/Q-learning
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The claim that reward-relevant paths gain weight in M. Standard SR M depends on the policy, not directly on reward, so reward shapes M only indirectly through policy. Also, 'optimal policy immediately' is overstated: the old M encodes the old policy's occupancy, so revaluation is approximate until M is re-learned under the new policy.

nearest_priors.name: Successor features with generalized policy improvement (Barreto et al. 2017)
nearest_priors.explains: Factorizing value into feature-occupancy times reward weights; transfer across reward functions with fixed dynamics; re-fitting only the reward weights after a task change
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: Uses features rather than a tabular one-hot M. Adds a library of stored policies and GPI, which the description does not include.

nearest_priors.name: Model-based planning / Dyna vs. model-free TD dissociation (Sutton 1990; Daw, Niv & Dayan 2005)
nearest_priors.explains: One-shot reward revaluation compared with slow relearning by a model-free Q-learning twin
nearest_priors.does_not_explain: The cached, reward-independent occupancy matrix and its TD update rule. Full model-based planning would also handle transition revaluation, which SR does not.

parsed.unexplained_residual: Nothing substantive. The only mismatch is the 'what is selected' claim that M preferentially weights reward-relevant paths, and that is only true indirectly, through reward-driven changes in policy.
parsed.discriminating_intervention: Run a transition-revaluation test (Momennejad et al. 2017): change the walls or transitions while keeping the reward fixed. An SR agent should fail to revalue quickly because M is stale. A full model-based planner should adapt immediately. Also run a policy-revaluation test in which the new reward lies on a path rarely taken under the old policy. There the SR agent should show characteristic errors that a model-based agent does not.

statement: A reliability ledger tracks, per [X] generator (not per hypothesis), the historical fraction of its outputs that passed [X]; hypotheses from a generator are provisionally trusted in proportion to this ledger score without being individually re-verified, instantiating reliabilism as a computable policy only meaningful when both generation and exhaustive verification exist.
what exists: set of abduction generators g_1..g_n; ledger scores r(g_i) in [0,1]; stream of hypotheses tagged by source generator; sparse [X] budget
what changes: r(g_i) updates via exponential moving average of pass/fail outcomes whenever a budgeted check occurs; unchecked hypotheses inherit trust = r(g_i).
what persists: the ledger scores across many episodes and many distinct hypothesis contents.
what is selected: generators with high r(g_i) get more of the scarce checking budget and more downstream trust.
what can reproduce: high-r generators are cloned/mutated to produce generator variants competing for budget.
what can learn: the ledger itself is the learned quantity; it is meta-knowledge about process reliability, not content.
what can transfer: r(g_i) transfers a generator's trust to a domain before any domain-specific checking occurs.
distinguishing observable: under a fixed, scarce checking budget, task accuracy tracks ledger score even for entirely , never-checked hypotheses — a correlation absent in a content-based-confidence control that has no generator identity.
minimal world: Three generators propose explanations for anomalies in a stream; only 10% of hypotheses can be model-checked per episode due to budget. Intervention: swap which generator is secretly reliable at episode 200. Null twin: confidence assigned per-hypothesis by a static heuristic (e.g. hypothesis length) uncorrelated with generator identity, matched for overall check rate; the twin fails to adapt after the swap while the ledger mechanism reallocates trust within a few episodes.
